On the first view it has no grammatical position, because the ṣila (relative clause) has no grammatical position. مَا may not be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), because the act [of providing] is not what is spent. مِنْ is partitive; it may also be for the beginning of the extent of spending.
The original form of (يُنْفِقُونَ) is يُؤَنْفِقُونَ, because its past tense is أَنْفَقَ; its counterpart has preceded.

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَتَأْمُرُونَ النَّاسَ بِالْبِرِّ وَتَنْسَوْنَ أَنْفُسَكُمْ وَأَنْتُمْ تَتْلُونَ الْكِتَابَ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ) ((٤٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَتَنْسَوْنَ): its original form is تُنْسِيُونَ [Translator's note: so vocalized in the text; the expected base form of تَنْسَوْن is تَنْسَيُون], then what we mentioned regarding His saying, Exalted is He: (اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلَالَةَ) was done to it. (أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ): a question in the sense of rebuke, and it has no grammatical position.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ وَبِالْآخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ (٤)).
His saying, the Exalted: (بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ): مَا here has the meaning of الَّذِي. It may not be an indefinite noun described [by what follows], i.e. "in something sent down to you", because on that view there is no generality in it, and faith is not complete unless it is in all that was sent down to the Prophet; مَا is for generality, and by that faith is realised.
The good reading is أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ, pronouncing the hamza fully. It has been read, among the irregular (shādhdh) readings, (أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ) with the lām doubled [Translator's note: the quoted form in the text does not show the doubling; the reading meant is أُنْزِلَّيْكَ, as the explanation below makes clear].
The explanation of it is that he made the lām of أُنْزِلَ quiescent and threw the vowel of the hamza onto it, so the lām took kasra and the hamza was dropped; then the lām of إِلَى met it, so that the wording became بِمَا (أُنْزِلْ لَّيْكَ); then the first lām was made quiescent and assimilated into the second lām. The kāf here is the pronoun of the addressee, who is the Prophet. It may also be the pronoun of the addressed category, having a plural meaning; this has been made explicit in other verses, as in His saying: (لَقَدْ أَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكُمْ كِتَابًا فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَبِالْآخِرَةِ): the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (يُوقِنُونَ). It is not impossible for the khabar (predicate) to govern something placed before the mubtadaʾ (subject); and this shows that placing the khabar before the mubtadaʾ is permitted, since the governed word does not occur in a place where its governor cannot occur. الْآخِرَةُ is an adjective whose described noun is omitted, its implied form being "in the Last Hour" or "in the Last Abode", as He said: (وَلَلدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ), and said: (وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ).
His saying, the Exalted: (هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ): هُمْ is a mubtadaʾ mentioned by way of emphasis. Had He said وَبِالْآخِرَةِ يُوقِنُونَ, the meaning and the i'rab would be sound. The point of the emphasis in هُمْ is to make certain that the pronoun refers back to those mentioned and not to others. يُوقِنُونَ is the khabar. Its original form is يُؤَيْقِنُونَ, because its past tense is أَيْقَنَ, and the basic rule is that the imperfect should contain the letters of the past tense; however, the hamza was dropped for the reason we mentioned in يُؤْمِنُونَ, and the yāʾ was replaced by a wāw because it is quiescent and the letter before it has ḍamma.

ukberi-tibyan:45-45.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاسْتَعِينُوا بِالصَّبْرِ وَالصَّلَاةِ وَإِنَّهَا لَكَبِيرَةٌ إِلَّا عَلَى الْخَاشِعِينَ) ((٤٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَاسْتَعِينُوا): its original form is استعْوِنوا, and this was mentioned in al-Fātiḥa. In وإنها, the pronoun refers to الصلاة; it has also been said: to the seeking of help (الاستعانة), because استعينوا indicates it; and it has also been said: to the qibla, because الصلاة indicates it, and the change [of qibla] to the Kaʿba was hard on the Jews. إلا على الخاشعين is in the position of the accusative by كبيرة; إلا came in for the meaning and does not govern, because there is nothing before it attached to كبيرة from which an exception could be made; so it is like your saying هو كبير على زيد ("it is hard upon Zayd").

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أُولَئِكَ عَلَى هُدًى مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ (٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (أُولَئِكَ): this is a plural form not built on the wording of its singular; its singular is ذَا. أُولَئِكَ is used for feminine and masculine. The kāf in it is a particle of address and not a noun, since if it were a noun it would be either nominative or accusative, and neither is valid, since there is nothing here to put it in the nominative or the accusative; or it would be genitive through the genitive construct, but أُولَاءِ cannot be put in a genitive construct, because it is a vague noun (mubham), and vague nouns are not put in a genitive construct. What remains is that it is a bare particle of address. أُولَاءِ may be pronounced with the long or the short form outside the Qur'an.
Its position here is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (عَلَى هُدًى) is the khabar (predicate); the preposition is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, i.e. "those are firmly established on guidance". أُولَئِكَ may also be the khabar of الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْغَيْبِ, as has been mentioned.
If it is asked: the basic meaning of عَلَى is superiority (being above), and guidance is not something one is above, so how is its meaning valid here?
It is answered: the meaning of superiority is present, because their rank has risen through following the guidance.
It may also be that, since all their actions accord with what guidance requires, their conduct with guidance is like the rider's control of what he rides.
His saying, the Exalted: (مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ) is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of هُدًى, and the preposition is attached to something omitted, its implied form being "guidance existing [from their Lord]". In the preposition and its genitive noun there is a pronoun referring back to الْهُدَى. Kasra and ḍamma are both permitted on the hāʾ, as we mentioned on عَلَيْهِمْ in al-Fātiḥa.
His saying, the Exalted: (وَأُولَئِكَ) is a mubtadaʾ; هُمْ is a second mubtadaʾ; and (الْمُفْلِحُونَ) is the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ; the second with its khabar is the khabar of the first.
هُمْ may also be a separating pronoun (faṣl) that has no grammatical position, with الْمُفْلِحُونَ the khabar of أُولَئِكَ.
The original form of مُفْلِحٌ is مُؤَفْلِحٌ; then the same was done to it as we mentioned in يُؤْمِنُونَ.

ukberi-tibyan:133-133.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَمْ كُنْتُمْ شُهَدَاءَ إِذْ حَضَرَ يَعْقُوبَ الْمَوْتُ إِذْ قَالَ لِبَنِيهِ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ بَعْدِي قَالُوا نَعْبُدُ إِلَهَكَ وَإِلَهَ آبَائِكَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ إِلَهًا وَاحِدًا وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ (١٣٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَمْ كُنْتُمْ): it is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) [أَمْ], i.e. "Rather, were you witnesses?", by way of rebuke.
(إِذْ حَضَرَ): it is read [شُهَدَاءَ إِذْ] with both hamzas pronounced fully, according to the original; with the second softened and made "between-between" (bayna bayna); and some pronounce it as a pure yāʾ because it has kasra. The majority read (يَعْقُوبَ) in the accusative and (الْمَوْتُ) in the nominative; it was also read the other way round, and the two meanings are close to one another. And the second (إِذْ) is a badal (substitute) for the first; what governs the first is شُهَدَاءَ, so it governs the second as well. It is also possible for the second to be an adverb of time for حَضَرَ, and on this view it is not a badal.
And (مَا) is interrogative, in the position of the accusative governed by (تَعْبُدُونَ); مَا here is in the sense of مَنْ ("who"), which is why the answer came as إِلَهَكَ ("your God"). It is also possible for «مَا» to have its usual sense, this being a test of them by Yaʿqūb.
And (مِنْ بَعْدِي): i.e. "after my death"; the muḍāf was omitted.
(وَإِلَهَ آبَائِكَ): He repeated the mention of "God" so that [آبَائِكَ] would not be conjoined to the genitive pronoun without repeating the governing word. The majority read (آبَائِكَ) as a broken plural. And (إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ) are a badal (substitute) for them. It is also read وَإِلَهُ أَبِيكَ, and there are two views on it. The first: it is a sound plural from which the nūn was dropped because of the genitive construct; they have said أَبٌ, أَبُونَ and أَبِينَ. On this reading the names after it are also a badal. The second view: that it is singular, and on this there are two views. The first: that it is singular in wording but intended as plural.
The second: that it is singular in wording and meaning; on this view إِبْرَاهِيمُ is a badal for it, and إِسْمَاعِيلُ and إِسْحَاقُ are conjoined to أَبِيكَ, its implied form being: "and the God of Ismāʿīl and Isḥāq".
(إِلَهًا وَاحِدًا): a badal for the first إِلَه. It may also be a preparatory ḥāl (ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa), as when you say: رَأَيْتُ زَيْدًا رَجُلًا صَالِحًا ("I saw Zayd, a righteous man"). The name إِسْمَاعِيلُ has the plurals سَمَاعِلَةٌ, مَسَاعِيلُ and أَسَامِيعُ.

ukberi-tibyan:134-134.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (تِلْكَ أُمَّةٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَلَكُمْ مَا كَسَبْتُمْ وَلَا تُسْأَلُونَ عَمَّا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ (١٣٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تِلْكَ أُمَّةٌ): the noun in it is «تِي», which is one of the demonstratives for the feminine, and the yāʾ is part of the noun. The Kufans said: the tāʾ alone is the noun and the yāʾ is additional. The yāʾ was dropped together with the lām because it is quiescent and the lām after it is quiescent.
If it is asked: why was the lām not given kasra and the yāʾ kept, as was done in ذَلِكَ?
It is answered: that would lead to heaviness, because the yāʾ would fall between two kasras. Its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and أُمَّةٌ is its khabar (predicate). And (قَدْ خَلَتْ) is an adjective (ṣifa) of أُمَّةٌ. And (لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ) is also in the position of an adjective; it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in خَلَتْ, and it may be resumptive. (وَلَا تُسْأَلُونَ): resumptive and nothing else. There is an omission in the speech, its implied form being: "and you will not be asked about what you used to do"; and what indicates the omission is His saying: (لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَلَكُمْ مَا كَسَبْتُمْ).

ukberi-tibyan:135-135.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالُوا كُونُوا هُودًا أَوْ نَصَارَى تَهْتَدُوا قُلْ بَلْ مِلَّةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ حَنِيفًا. . . . . (١٣٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَوْ نَصَارَى): what is said about «أَوْ» here is like what was said about it in His saying (وَقَالُوا لَنْ يَدْخُلَ الْجَنَّةَ), because the implied form is: "the Jews said: be Jews, and the Christians said: be Christians". (مِلَّةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ): its implied form is: "rather we follow the religion of Ibrāhīm", or "say: follow the religion".
And (حَنِيفًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from إِبْرَاهِيمَ. A ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi is weak by analogy and rare in usage. The reason for that is that a ḥāl must have something that governs it, and what governs it is what governs the one it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl), and it is not valid for the muḍāf to govern the ḥāl in a case like this.
The justification of the view of those who made it accusative as a ḥāl is that they took the governing factor to be the meaning of the lām, or the meaning of the genitive construct, namely accompaniment and close connection. It is also said: it is good to make حَنِيفًا a ḥāl because the meaning is "we follow Ibrāhīm, as one inclining to the truth (ḥanīf)"; and this is good, because the religion (al-milla) is the creed (al-dīn), and the one followed is Ibrāhīm. It is also said: it is accusative by an implied "I mean" (أَعْنِي).

ukberi-tibyan:136-136.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُولُوا آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْنَا وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطِ وَمَا أُوتِيَ مُوسَى وَعِيسَى وَمَا أُوتِيَ النَّبِيُّونَ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ. . . . . . . (١٣٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ): the hāʾ and mīm refer to the prophets specifically; on this view مِنْ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the second أُوتِيَ.
It is also said that it refers to Mūsā and ʿĪsā as well, and the second (وَمَا أُوتِيَ) is a repetition, being in meaning like the one in [Sūrat] Āl ʿImrān; on this view مِنْ is attached to the first أُوتِيَ.
The position of مِنْ is accusative, on the basis that it is for the beginning (ibtidāʾ) of the extent of the giving.
Its position may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted referent pronoun, its implied form being: "and what the prophets were given, being from their Lord". It is also possible for the second مَا أُوتِيَ to be in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ as its khabar (predicate). (بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ): أَحَدٌ here is the one used in negation, because «بَيْنَ» is put in construct only with a plural, or with a singular that has something conjoined to it. It is also said that أَحَدٌ here means "a group" (فَرِيقٌ).

ukberi-tibyan:137-137.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِنْ آمَنُوا بِمِثْلِ مَا آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ فَقَدِ اهْتَدَوْا. . . (١٣٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِمِثْلِ مَا آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ): the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and مِثْل is an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being: "a belief like your belief". The hāʾ refers to Allah, or to the Quran, or to Muḥammad, and مَا is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun). The parallel of the redundancy of the bāʾ here is its redundancy in His saying: (جَزَاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ بِمِثْلِهَا). It is also said that مِثْل here is redundant and مَا means "that which" (الَّذِي). Ibn ʿAbbās read: بِمَا آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ, dropping مِثْل.

ukberi-tibyan:138-138.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (صِبْغَةَ اللَّهِ وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ اللَّهِ صِبْغَةً (١٣٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (صِبْغَةَ اللَّهِ): الصِّبْغَةُ ("the dye") here means the religion, and it is accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "follow the religion of Allah".
It is also said that it is an incitement (ighrāʾ), i.e. "hold fast to the religion of Allah". And it is said that it is a badal (substitute) for مِلَّةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ. (وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). And (مِنَ اللَّهِ) is in the position of the accusative. And (صِبْغَةً) is a tamyīz (specification).

ukberi-tibyan:140-140.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَمْ تَقُولُونَ إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطَ كَانُوا هُودًا أَوْ نَصَارَى قُلْ أَأَنْتُمْ أَعْلَمُ أَمِ اللَّهُ وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنْ كَتَمَ شَهَادَةً عِنْدَهُ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ (١٤٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَمْ يَقُولُونَ): it is read with yāʾ, referring back to His saying (فَسَيَكْفِيكَهُمُ اللَّهُ), and with tāʾ, referring back to His saying (أَتُحَاجُّونَنَا).
(هُودًا أَوْ نَصَارَى): أَوْ here is like it in His saying (وَقَالُوا كُونُوا هُودًا أَوْ نَصَارَى), i.e. the Jews said: these prophets were Jews, and the Christians said: they were Christians. (أَمِ اللَّهُ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "or is Allah more knowing?" أَمْ here is the connected (muttaṣila) one, i.e. "which of [you two] is more knowing?", and it is a question with the sense of disavowal (inkār). (كَتَمَ شَهَادَةً): كَتَمَ is transitive to two objects, and the first of them has been omitted here, its implied form being: "concealed from the people a testimony". On this view «عِنْدَهُ» is an adjective (ṣifa) of شَهَادَةً, and likewise «مَنَّ اللَّهُ» [Translator's note: so in the source; the Quranic text is مِنَ اللَّهِ]. It is not permissible to attach مِنْ to شَهَادَةً, lest the ṣila (relative clause) be separated from what it belongs to (al-mawṣūl) by the adjective. It is possible to make عِنْدَهُ and مِنَ اللَّهِ two adjectives of شَهَادَةً; and it is possible to make مِنْ an adverbial [complement] for what governs the first adverb, or to make it a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in عِنْدَهُ.

ukberi-tibyan:142-142.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (سَيَقُولُ السُّفَهَاءُ مِنَ النَّاسِ مَا وَلَّاهُمْ عَنْ قِبْلَتِهِمُ الَّتِي كَانُوا عَلَيْهَا. . . . . . . (١٤٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (السُّفَهَاءُ مِنَ النَّاسِ): مِنَ النَّاسِ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and what governs it is يَقُولُ. (مَا وَلَّاهُمْ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of the accusative governed by "saying".
(كَانُوا عَلَيْهَا): it contains an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being: "upon facing it" or "upon believing in it".

ukberi-tibyan:84-84.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَكُمْ لَا تَسْفِكُونَ دِمَاءَكُمْ وَلَا تُخْرِجُونَ أَنْفُسَكُمْ مِنْ دِيَارِكُمْ ثُمَّ أَقْرَرْتُمْ وَأَنْتُمْ تَشْهَدُونَ (٨٤)).
His saying, the Exalted: (مِنْ دِيَارِكُمْ): the yāʾ is converted from a wāw, because it is the plural of دَارٌ, and the alif in دَارٌ is originally a wāw, since it is from دَارَ يَدُورُ. It was changed into a yāʾ in the plural only because of the kasra on what precedes it and its being weakened in the singular.
If you say: then how did it remain sound in (لِوَاذًا)? It is answered: since it remained sound in the verb, it remained sound in the maṣdar (verbal noun), the verb being لَاوَذَ.
If you say: then how did it [become yāʾ] in دَيَّارٌ? It is answered: its original form is دَيْوَارٌ; the wāw was changed and assimilated.
(ثُمَّ أَقْرَرْتُمْ): there are two views on it.
The first: that ثُمَّ is in its usual function of conveying conjunction with delay, and what it is conjoined to is omitted, its implied form being: "so you accepted, then you acknowledged". The second: that «ثُمَّ» has come to order the report, not to order what is reported, as in His saying, the Exalted: (ثُمَّ اللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ).

ukberi-tibyan:85-85.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ هَؤُلَاءِ تَقْتُلُونَ أَنْفُسَكُمْ وَتُخْرِجُونَ فَرِيقًا مِنْكُمْ مِنْ دِيَارِهِمْ تَظَاهَرُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِالْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوَانِ وَإِنْ يَأْتُوكُمْ أُسَارَى تُفَادُوهُمْ وَهُوَ مُحَرَّمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ إِخْرَاجُهُمْ أَفَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِبَعْضِ الْكِتَابِ وَتَكْفُرُونَ بِبَعْضٍ فَمَا جَزَاءُ مَنْ يَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا خِزْيٌ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَيَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يُرَدُّونَ إِلَى أَشَدِّ الْعَذَابِ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ (٨٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ هَؤُلَاءِ): أَنْتُمْ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and there are three views on its khabar (predicate). The first: تَقْتُلُونَ. On this view there are two views on هَؤُلَاءِ: one, that it is in the position of the accusative by an implied أَعْنِي ("I mean"); the second, that it is the one addressed in a vocative (munādā), i.e. "O these (يَا هَؤُلَاءِ)" — except that this is not permissible according to Sībawayh, because أُولَاءِ is vague (mubham), and the vocative particle is not omitted with a vague noun. The second view: that the khabar is هَؤُلَاءِ, taking it in the sense of الَّذِينَ ("those who"), with تَقْتُلُونَ as its ṣila (relative clause). This too is weak, because the doctrine of the Basrans is that this أُولَاءِ does not take the place of الَّذِينَ; the Kufans allowed it. The third view: that the khabar is هَؤُلَاءِ on the assumption that a muḍāf is omitted, its implied form being "then you are like these", as when you say: "Abū Yūsuf is Abū Ḥanīfa". On this view تَقْتُلُونَ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) governed by the sense of likening.
His saying: (تَظَاهَرُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; what governs it is تُخْرِجُونَ, and the one it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl) is the wāw. It is read with a doubled ẓāʾ; the original form is تَتَظَاهَرُونَ, and the second tāʾ was changed into a ẓāʾ and assimilated.
It is read with the light form, on the omission of the second tāʾ, because the heaviness and repetition came about through it, and because the first is a letter that indicates a meaning; it is also said that the omitted one is the first.
It is also read with a ḍamma on the tāʾ, a kasra on the hāʾ and the light form [i.e. تُظَاهِرُونَ], its past being ظَاهَرَ.
And
(وَالْعُدْوَانِ): a maṣdar (verbal noun), like الْكُفْرَانُ; the kasra [i.e. الْعِدْوَانُ] is a weak dialectal form. (أُسَارَى): a ḥāl, and it is the plural of أَسِيرٌ. It is read with a ḍamma on the hamza and with a fatḥa, like سُكَارَى and سَكَارَى; it is also read أَسْرَى, like جَرِيحٌ and جَرْحَى. In ordinary speech أُسَرَاءُ is permissible, like شَهِيدٌ and شُهَدَاءُ.
(تُفْدُوهُمْ): without an alif, and تُفَادُوهُمْ with the alif; the latter is of the pattern of mutual action (al-mufāʿala). It may have the meaning of the first reading, or it may be of the mufāʿala that takes place between two parties, because ransoming (al-mufādāh) takes place in that way.
(وَهُوَ مُحَرَّمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ): هُوَ is a mubtadaʾ, and it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); مُحَرَّمٌ is its khabar, and إِخْرَاجُهُمْ is made nominative by مُحَرَّمٌ.
It may also be that إِخْرَاجُهُمْ is a mubtadaʾ and مُحَرَّمٌ a fronted khabar, the clause being the khabar of هُوَ.
It may also be that هُوَ is the pronoun of the expelling indicated by His saying «وَتُخْرِجُونَ فَرِيقًا مِنْكُمْ», with مُحَرَّمٌ as the khabar, and إِخْرَاجُهُمْ a badal (substitute) for the pronoun in مُحَرَّمٌ, or for هُوَ.
(فَمَا جَزَاءُ): مَا is negation, and the khabar is (خِزْيٌ). It may also be interrogative, a mubtadaʾ, with جَزَاءٌ as its khabar and إِلَّا خِزْيٌ a badal of جَزَاءٌ.
(يَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ مِنْكُمْ): [i.e. مِنْكُمْ] is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in يَفْعَلُ.
(فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا): an adjective of الْخِزْيُ.
It may also be an adverbial (ẓarf), its implied form being "except that he be disgraced in the life of this world".
(يُرَدُّونَ): with the yāʾ, as third person, because what precedes it is similar; and it is read with the tāʾ, as second-person address, referring back to His saying: تَقْتُلُونَ. Like it is (عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ): with the tāʾ and the yāʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:87-87.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ وَقَفَّيْنَا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ بِالرُّسُلِ وَآتَيْنَا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ الْبَيِّنَاتِ وَأَيَّدْنَاهُ بِرُوحِ الْقُدُسِ أَفَكُلَّمَا جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ بِمَا لَا تَهْوَى أَنْفُسُكُمُ اسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ فَفَرِيقًا كَذَّبْتُمْ وَفَرِيقًا تَقْتُلُونَ (٨٧)).
His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: (وَقَفَّيْنَا): the yāʾ is a substitute for a wāw, as shown by your saying قَفَوْتُهُ and هُوَ يَقْفُوهُ, when he
follows him; when it came in fourth position, it was changed into a yāʾ. (بِالرُّسُلِ): with the ḍamma, which is the original, and the sukūn is permissible for lightness. Some of them use the sukūn when it is put in construct with a pronoun, to escape a succession of vowels, and use the ḍamma otherwise.
(عِيسَى): the pattern فِعْلَى, from الْعِيسُ, which is a whiteness mixed with reddish-blondness. It is also said that it is a foreign word with no derivation. And مَرْيَمُ is a foreign proper name; had it been derived from رَامَ يَرِيمُ, it would have been مَرْيَمٌ [Translator's note: printed «مَرَيْمًا»] with a sukūn on the yāʾ. [Such forms] have come among proper names with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, such as مَزْيَدٌ, and that is contrary to the analogical rule. (وَأَيَّدْنَاهُ): its pattern is فَعَّلْنَاهُ [Translator's note: printed «فَعَلْنَاهُ»], and it is from الْأَيْدُ, which means strength.
It is also read «آيَدْنَاهُ» with a lengthened alif and a light yāʾ, its pattern being أَفْعَلْنَاهُ.
If you say: why was the yāʾ, which is the second radical, not omitted as it was omitted in the like of أَسَلْنَاهُ, from سَالَ يَسِيلُ? It is answered: had they done that, two weakenings would have followed one another: one, changing the second hamza into an alif, then omitting the alif substituted for the yāʾ because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the alif before it; so the word would have become أَدْنَاهُ, and both the first and the second radicals would have been omitted. أَسَلْنَاهُ is not like that, because there the second radical alone was omitted. (الْقُدُسِ): with a ḍamma on the dāl and with a sukūn; two dialectal forms, like الْعُسْرُ and الْعُسُرُ.
(أَفَكُلَّمَا): the fāʾ entered here to link what follows it with what precedes it, and the hamza is for interrogation in the sense of rebuke. And «جَاءَكُمْ» is transitive by itself and by a preposition: you say جِئْتُهُ and جِئْتُ إِلَيْهِ.
(تَهْوَى): its alif is converted from a yāʾ, because its second radical is a wāw, and the pattern of طَوَيْتُ and شَوَيْتُ is more frequent than the pattern of حُوَّةٌ and قُوَّةٌ. There is no evidence in هَوِيَ, because of the kasra on the second radical; it is like شَقِيَ, whose original is a wāw. What shows that هَوًى is also of the yāʾ type is their saying in the dual هَوِيَانِ. (اسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ): the answer of كُلَّمَا. (فَفَرِيقًا كَذَّبْتُمْ): i.e. "so you denied a party"; the fāʾ conjoined كَذَّبْتُمْ to اسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ, but the object was put first so that the verse-endings would agree. And in the speech there is an omission, i.e. "so a party of them you denied".

ukberi-tibyan:88-88.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالُوا قُلُوبُنَا غُلْفٌ بَلْ لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِكُفْرِهِمْ فَقَلِيلًا مَا يُؤْمِنُونَ (٨٨)).
His saying, the Exalted: (غُلْفٌ): it is read with a ḍamma on the lām [i.e. غُلُفٌ], and it is the plural of غِلَافٌ ("covering").
It is read with a sukūn on it, and there are two views on it. The first: it is the quiescing of a ḍamma, like كُتْبٌ and كُتُبٌ.
The second: it is the plural of أَغْلَفُ ("uncircumcised, covered"), like أَحْمَرُ and حُمْرٌ; on this view it may not take the ḍamma. And (بَلْ) here is a turning away (iḍrāb) from their claim and an affirmation that the cause of their denial is Allah's cursing them as a punishment for them.
His saying: (بِكُفْرِهِمْ): the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (لُعِنَ) [Translator's note: so printed; the verse has لَعَنَهُمُ]. Abū ʿAlī said: it is intended to come first, i.e. "and they said: our hearts are covered, because of their disbelief", and بَلْ لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ is parenthetical.
It may also be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object in لَعَنَهُمْ, i.e. "disbelievers", as He said: (وَقَدْ دَخَلُوا) بِالْكُفْرِ.
(فَقَلِيلًا): accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), and (مَا) is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "so with a little belief they believe". It is also said that it is an adjective of an adverbial, i.e. "so for a little time they believe". مَا cannot be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), because then قَلِيلًا would be left with nothing to make it accusative. It is also said: مَا is negating, i.e. "so they do not believe, neither a little nor much"; and like it are (قَلِيلًا مَا تَشْكُرُونَ) and (قَلِيلًا مَا تَذَكَّرُونَ). This is stronger in meaning; it is somewhat weak only from the point of view that what is governed by something within the scope of مَا is put before it.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ (٦)).
His saying, the Exalted: (سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ): it is put in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ is a clause in the position of the fāʿil (agent); this clause stands in place of the khabar (predicate). The implied sense is "warning and not warning are equal in their regard"; it is a statement construed according to the meaning. This clause may also be in the position of a mubtadaʾ, with سَاءَ [Translator's note: so in the text; evidently سَوَاءٌ is meant] as a khabar placed first. On both views the clause is the khabar of إِنَّ, and on this view لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ has no grammatical position. سَوَاءٌ may also be the khabar of إِنَّ, with what follows it governed by it. لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ may also be the khabar of أَنَّ [Translator's note: so in the text; إِنَّ is meant], with سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ and what follows it parenthetical between the two.
It may also be a khabar after a khabar. (سَوَاءٌ) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) occurring in place of the active participle, namely مُسْتَوٍ ("equal"), and it governs as يَسْتَوِي does; because it is a maṣdar, it is not put in the dual or the plural. The hamza in سَوَاءٌ is substituted for a yāʾ, because the class of طَوَيْتُ and شَوَيْتُ [where the second radical is wāw and the third yāʾ] is more numerous than the class of قُوَّةٌ and حُوَّةٌ [where both are wāw], so it was assigned to the more numerous.
His saying, the Exalted: (أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ): Ibn Muḥayṣin read it with a single hamza, in the wording of a statement, while the interrogative hamza is intended; they dropped it for lightness, and in the phrase there is what indicates it, namely His saying أَمْ لَمْ, because أَمْ is the counterpart of the hamza. Most read it in the wording of the interrogative, and then differed over how to pronounce it. Some pronounced both hamzas fully without separating them; this is the original, but combining two hamzas is felt heavy, because the hamza is a burst of sound that comes out of the chest with effort, so pronouncing it resembles retching; when two hamzas come together it is heavier on the speaker, and for this reason most of the Arabs do not pronounce both fully.
Some of them pronounce the first fully and make the second "between-between" (bayna bayna), i.e. between hamza and alif; this is in reality a softened hamza, not an alif. Some make the second a true alif, as was done in آدَمُ and آمَنَ. Some soften the second and separate it from the first with an alif. And some pronounce both hamzas fully and separate them with an alif.
Some of the Arabs replace the first with a hāʾ and pronounce the second fully, and some of them soften the second along with that. It is not permitted to pronounce the first fully, make the second a true alif, and separate the two with an alif, because that would combine two alifs. The interrogative hamza entered here for equalisation (taswiya); this resembles interrogation, because to the questioner existence and non-existence are equal, and so likewise does one who intends equalisation. This occurs after سَوَاءٌ, as in this verse; after لَيْتَ شِعْرِي, as in your saying لَيْتَ شِعْرِي أَقَامَ أَمْ قَعَدَ ("would that I knew whether he stood or sat"); and after لَا أُبَالِي ("I do not care") and لَا أَدْرِي ("I do not know").
This أَمْ is the one that is the counterpart (al-muʿādila) of the interrogative hamza. لَمْ turns the imperfect to the meaning of the past, so that أَمْسِ ("yesterday") fits well with it; and if the conditional إِنْ enters upon it, the verb returns to its original future sense.

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (خَتَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ وَعَلَى سَمْعِهِمْ وَعَلَى أَبْصَارِهِمْ غِشَاوَةٌ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ (٧))
His saying, the Exalted: (وَعَلَى سَمْعِهِمْ): السَّمْعُ is originally the maṣdar (verbal noun) of سَمِعَ, and there are two views on how to construe it here. First: it is used as a maṣdar in its original sense, and there is an omission in the phrase, its implied form being "upon the places of their hearing", because hearing itself is not sealed.
Second: السَّمْعُ here is used in the sense of the hearing organ (al-sāmiʿa), which is the ear, as they said الْغَيْبُ in the sense of الْغَائِبُ, and النَّجْمُ in the sense of النَّاجِمُ ("what appears") [Translator's note: the text reads «وَالنَّجْمُ الْغَائِبُ وَالنَّجْمُ بِمَعْنَى النَّاجِمِ», apparently with a repetition]. The singular is made to suffice here for the plural, as the poet said:
بِهَا جِيَفُ الْحَسْرَى فَأَمَّا عِظَامُهَا ... فَبِيضٌ وَأَمَّا جِلْدُهَا فَصَلِيبُ
("In it are the carcasses of the exhausted beasts: as for their bones, they are white, and as for their skin, it is hard")
meaning جُلُودُهَا ("their skins").
His saying, the Exalted: (وَعَلَى أَبْصَارِهِمْ غِشَاوَةٌ) is read in the nominative, as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with وَعَلَى أَبْصَارِهِمْ as its khabar (predicate); on this view there is a pronoun in the preposition.
According to the view of al-Akhfash, غِشَاوَةٌ is put in the nominative by the preposition, as the agent is put in the nominative by the verb; on this view there is no pronoun in the preposition, because the overt noun is in the nominative [by it] (لِارْتِفَاعِ الظَّاهِرِ) [Translator's note: the text reads «لارْتِفَاع الظَّاهِرِيَّة»; rendered according to the evident sense]. On this reading the pause is on (وَعَلَى سَمْعِهِمْ).
It is also read in the accusative (غِشَاوَةً), by an implied verb, its implied form being "and He placed upon their eyes a covering". It may not be accusative by خَتَمَ, because that is not transitive by itself. Kasra and fatḥa on the ghayn are both permitted; and there are three other dialectal forms of it: غِشْوَةٌ without alif, with fatḥa, ḍamma and kasra on the ghayn.
His saying, the Exalted: (وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ) is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, or [عَذَابٌ is] an agent governed by the preposition, as we mentioned before. In (عَظِيمٌ) there is a pronoun referring back to الْعَذَابُ, because it is its adjective.

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَقُولُ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَبِالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَمَا هُمْ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ (٨)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَمِنَ النَّاسِ): the wāw entered here as a conjunction, conjoining to His saying (الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْغَيْبِ). That is because these verses cover all the categories of people: the first verses contain the mention of those sincere in faith; His saying (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) contains the mention of those who displayed unbelief and concealed it; and this verse contains the mention of those who displayed faith and concealed unbelief. Hence the wāw entered, to make clear that those mentioned are part of the completion of the first discourse. مِنْ here is partitive; its nūn was given fatḥa and not kasra so that two kasras would not follow one another.
The original form of النَّاسُ according to Sībawayh is أُنَاسٌ; its hamza, which is the first radical of the word, was dropped, and the alif and lām were made a kind of compensation for it. So النَّاسُ is hardly ever used except with the alif and lām, and أُنَاسٌ is hardly ever used with the alif and lām. On this view the alif in النَّاسُ is extra, and its derivation is from al-uns (familiarity).
Others said: there is no omission in the word; the alif is converted from a wāw, which is the second radical of the word, and its derivation is from نَاسَ يَنُوسُ نَوْسًا, said when something moves; and they said in its diminutive نُوَيْسٌ.
His saying (مَنْ يَقُولُ): (مَنْ) is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what precedes it is the khabar (predicate); or it is put in the nominative by the preposition before it, as has preceded.
(مَنْ) here is an indefinite noun described [by what follows], and يَقُولُ is its adjective. It is weak for it to have the meaning of الَّذِي, because الَّذِي covers a specific people, while the meaning here is one of vagueness; the implied wording is "and among the people is a group who says".
(مَنْ) is singular in form and is used for the dual, the plural and the feminine with one wording. The pronoun referring back to it may be singular, following its wording, or dual, plural or feminine, following its meaning. In this verse both ways have come: the pronoun in يَقُولُ is singular, and in آمَنَّا and وَمَا هُمْ plural.
The original form of يَقُولُ is يَقْوُلُ, with sukūn on the qāf and ḍamma on the wāw, because it is the counterpart of يَقْعُدُ and يَقْتُلُ, and it has only come in that form. The ḍamma of the wāw was transferred to the qāf, to make pronouncing the wāw lighter. Hence when you give a command you do not need the hamza, but say قُلْ, because the first radical of the word has taken a vowel, so there is no need for the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl).
His saying, the Exalted: (آمَنَّا): the alif was originally a quiescent hamza, which was turned into alif so that two hamzas would not come together; it was turned into alif because of the fatḥa before it. The pattern of آمَنَ is afʿala, from al-amn (security).
(الْآخِرِ) is on the pattern fāʿil, so the alif in it is not substituted for anything.
His saying (وَمَا هُمْ): هُمْ is a detached pronoun, put in the nominative by مَا according to the people of the Ḥijāz, and a mubtadaʾ according to Tamīm. The bāʾ in the khabar is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis and is not attached (mutaʿalliq) to anything; and so is every preposition added to the mubtadaʾ, the khabar or the agent. مَا negates what is in the present, and it is sometimes used to negate the future.

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُمْ مُلَاقُو رَبِّهِمْ وَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ) ((٤٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ): a ṣifa (adjective) of الخاشعين; it may also be in the position of the accusative by an implied أعني ("I mean"), or of the nominative by an implied «هم» ("they are").
(أَنَّهُمْ): أنّ with its noun and its khabar (predicate) takes the place of the two objects, because it contains what the supposition is attached to, namely the meeting, and mentions the one to whom the meeting is attributed. Al-Akhfash said: أنّ and what it governs is a single object, which is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and the second object is omitted, its implied form being: "they think the meeting with Allah to be occurring".
(مُلَاقُو): its original form is مُلاقِيُوا, then what we have mentioned in more than one place was done to it. The nūn was omitted for lightness, because it is indefinite when it refers to the future; and when the nūn was omitted, it was put into iḍāfa. (إِلَيْهِ): the hāʾ refers to Allah; it has also been said: to the meeting indicated by ملاقوا.

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتِيَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَنِّي فَضَّلْتُكُمْ عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ (٤٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَنِّي فَضَّلْتُكُمْ): in the position of the accusative, its implied form being: "and remember My favouring of you".

ukberi-tibyan:48-48.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاتَّقُوا يَوْمًا لَا تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ عَنْ نَفْسٍ شَيْئًا وَلَا يُقْبَلُ مِنْهَا شَفَاعَةٌ وَلَا يُؤْخَذُ مِنْهَا عَدْلٌ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ (٤٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَاتَّقُوا يَوْمًا): يوما here is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because the command to be mindful does not take place on the Day of Resurrection; the implied form is: "and guard against the punishment of a day", or the like.
(لَا تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ): the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ṣifa (adjective) of اليوم, and the referring pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, its implied form being تجزى فيه ("[in which no soul] will avail … in it"); then the preposition and its genitive noun were omitted [together], according to Sībawayh, because adverbials are treated with latitude, and what is permissible in them is not permissible in others. Others said: «في» is omitted, so it becomes تجزيه; then, once the verb reaches [its object] by itself, the object is omitted after that. (عَنْ نَفْسٍ): in the position of the accusative by (تجزى).
It may also be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), on the basis that the implied form is "anything on behalf of a soul". And (شَيْئًا) here has the status of a maṣdar (verbal noun), because it occurs in the place of جزاء ("availing"); this is frequent in the Qur'an, because availing is a "thing", so the general was put in the place of the specific.
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَا يُقْبَلُ مِنْهَا شَفَاعَةٌ وَلَا يُؤْخَذُ مِنْهَا عَدْلٌ): i.e. "in it"; and likewise: (وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ). And (مِنْهَا) in both places may be attached to (يقبل) and يؤخذ, and it may be an adjective of شفاعة and عدل, which, when placed before [them], became accusative as a ḥāl. [Translator's note: the Arabic reads «فلمّا قد انتصب», apparently a corruption of «فلمّا قُدِّم انتصب»; translated according to the evident sense.]
And «يقبل» is read with tāʾ because شفاعة is feminine, and with yāʾ because it is not a true feminine; this is made more acceptable by the separation [between verb and agent].

ukberi-tibyan:49-49.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذْ نَجَّيْنَاكُمْ مِنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوءَ الْعَذَابِ يُذَبِّحُونَ أَبْنَاءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِسَاءَكُمْ وَفِي ذَلِكُمْ بَلَاءٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ) ((٤٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِذْ نَجَّيْنَاكُمْ): إذ is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to (اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتِيَ); [likewise] (وَإِذْ وَاعَدْنَا), وإذ قلتم يا موسى, and the like among the conjunctions. (مِنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ): the original form of آل is أهل; the hāʾ was changed to hamza because of its closeness to it in point of articulation, then the hamza was changed to alif because it was quiescent and preceded by a hamza with fatḥa, as in آدم and آمن. Its diminutive is أُهَيل, because the diminutive restores [a word] to its origin; some said أُوَيل, changing the alif to wāw without restoring it to its origin, just as they did not restore عيد to its origin in the diminutive.
It has also been said that the original form of آل is أوَل, from آل يؤول ("to return"), because a person returns to his family. And فرعون is a foreign, definite noun. (يَسُومُونَكُمْ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from آل.
(سُوءَ الْعَذَابِ): a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because يسومونكم takes two objects; one says سمته الخسف, i.e. "I imposed humiliation on him". (يُذَبِّحُونَ): in the position of a ḥāl, if you wish, from «آل», on the basis that it is a badal (substitute) from the first ḥāl, because two or more ḥāls cannot be from a single thing, since the ḥāl resembles the object, and the operator does not govern two objects of this description. If you wish, you may make it a ḥāl from the agent in يسومونكم. The majority read it with doubling of the bāʾ for multiplicity, and it has been read without doubling.
(بَلَاءٌ): the hamza replaces a wāw, because the verb from it is بلوته ("I tested him"), and from it is His saying: (وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُمْ). (مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ): in the position of the nominative as an adjective of بلاء, so it is attached to something omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:50-50.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذْ فَرَقْنَا بِكُمُ الْبَحْرَ فَأَنْجَيْنَاكُمْ وَأَغْرَقْنَا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَأَنْتُمْ تَنْظُرُونَ (٥٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَرَقْنَا بِكُمُ الْبَحْرَ): بكم is in the position of the accusative as a second object, and البحر is the first object; the bāʾ here is in the sense of the lām. It may also be that the implied form is: "because of you". It may also be the transitivizing bāʾ, as in your saying ذهبت بزيد ("I took Zayd away"), so the implied form would be: "We made you part the sea", and in meaning it would be like His saying, Exalted is He: (وَجَاوَزْنَا بِبَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ الْبَحْرَ). The bāʾ may also be for the ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "We parted the sea while you were in it", in which case it is either an anticipated (muqaddara) or a simultaneous (muqārina) ḥāl. (وَأَنْتُمْ تَنْظُرُونَ): in the position of the ḥāl, its operator being «أغرقنا».

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذْ وَاعَدْنَا مُوسَى أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً ثُمَّ اتَّخَذْتُمُ الْعِجْلَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ وَأَنْتُمْ ظَالِمُونَ) ((٥١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَاعَدْنَا مُوسَى): وعد takes two objects; you say وعدت زيدا مكان كذا ويوم كذا ("I gave Zayd an appointment at such a place and such a day"). So the first object is موسى and «أربعين» is the second object; there is an omission in the speech, its implied form being "the completion of forty", and أربعين is not an adverbial (ẓarf), since the meaning is not that He made him a promise within forty [nights].
It is read واعدنا with alif, and it is not of the mufāʿala type that occurs between two parties; rather it is like your saying عافاه الله ("Allah granted him well-being") and عاقبت اللص ("I punished the thief"). It has also been said that it is of that [mutual] type, because the promise was from Allah and the acceptance from Moses, so it became like a promise from him. It has also been said that Allah commanded Moses to promise to fulfil, and he did so.
And (مُوسَى) is مُفعَل, from أوسيت رأسه, when I shaved his head; so it is like أعطى, giving مُعطًى.
It has also been said: it is فُعلى from ماس يميس, when one struts in one's gait; the iron razor (موسى الحديد) is from this sense, because of how much it shakes and moves during shaving. On this view the wāw in موسى replaces a yāʾ, because it is quiescent and preceded by ḍamma.
But موسى as the name of the Prophet is not judged by derivation, because it is foreign; only the iron razor موسى is derived. (ثُمَّ اتَّخَذْتُمُ الْعِجْلَ): i.e. "as a god"; the second object was omitted, and similar to it is: باتخاذكم العجل. اتخذتُ may come as taking one object when it is in the sense of جعل and عمل ("made"), as in His saying, Exalted is He: (وَقَالُوا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَدًا), and as in your saying: اتخذت دارا وثوبا ("I acquired a house and a garment"), and the like. The dhāl may be assimilated into the tāʾ because of the closeness of their points of articulation, and it may be pronounced distinctly according to the original form.
(مِنْ بَعْدِهِ): i.e. "after his departure"; the muḍāf was omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ثُمَّ عَفَوْنَا عَنْكُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ) ((٥٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَعَلَّكُمْ): the first lām is a radical according to a group [of grammarians], and it is only omitted for lightness in your saying علّك. It has also been said that it is redundant (zāʾida), and that the original form is علّك; but لعلّ is a particle, and omission is a kind of inflectional modification, from which particles are remote.

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ وَالْفُرْقَانَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ (٥٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالْفُرْقَانَ): it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), like الرجحان and الغفران, and it has been made a name for the Qur'an.

ukberi-tibyan:54-54.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَى لِقَوْمِهِ يَا قَوْمِ إِنَّكُمْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ بِاتِّخَاذِكُمُ الْعِجْلَ فَتُوبُوا إِلَى بَارِئِكُمْ فَاقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ ذَلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ عِنْدَ بَارِئِكُمْ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ (٥٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِقَوْمِهِ): the good dialect is for the hāʾ to take kasra when the letter before it has kasra, and for a yāʾ to be added to it in pronunciation, because it is a faint letter that is not fully clear with the kasra alone. If a yāʾ precedes it, as in عليه, the good [practice] is for the hāʾ to take kasra without a yāʾ, because the hāʾ is faint and weak, so when there is a yāʾ before it and a yāʾ after it, the barrier between the two quiescent letters is not strong enough. If a fatḥa or a ḍamma precedes the hāʾ, it takes ḍamma and is followed by a wāw in pronunciation, as in إنه and غلامه, for the reason we mentioned. (يَا قَوْمِ): the yāʾ of the first person was omitted, the kasra sufficing; this is permissible, and it is specific to the vocative, because there is no ambiguity. Some keep the yāʾ quiescent, some give it fatḥa, some change it into an alif after giving fatḥa to the letter before it, and some say يا قومُ, with ḍamma on the mīm. (إِلَى بَارِئِكُمْ): the reading is with kasra on the hamza, because its kasra is the case ending. Making it quiescent is reported from Abū ʿAmr, to avoid a succession of vowels; Sībawayh does not accept this report, and he used to say that the transmitter did not record Abū ʿAmr accurately, because Abū ʿAmr pronounced the vowel very briefly (ikhtilās), so the hearer thought that he made it quiescent. (ذَلِكُمْ): some said the original form is ذانكم, because what was mentioned before is repentance and killing, so the singular was put in the place of the dual, since ذا can cover all of it; but this is nothing, because His saying فاقتلوا is an explanation of the repentance, so it is a single thing. (فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ): there is an omission in the speech, its implied form being: "so you did [so], and He accepted your repentance".

ukberi-tibyan:89-89.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ كِتَابٌ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ مُصَدِّقٌ لِمَا مَعَهُمْ وَكَانُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ يَسْتَفْتِحُونَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ مَا عَرَفُوا كَفَرُوا بِهِ فَلَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ (٨٩)).
His saying, the Exalted: (مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ): it may be in the position of the accusative, for the beginning of the extent of the coming. It may also be in the position of the nominative as an adjective of كِتَابٌ.
(مُصَدِّقٌ): with the nominative, as an adjective of كِتَابٌ. It was read anomalously (shādhdh) with the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and there are two views on the one it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl). The first: الْكِتَابُ, because it has been qualified and so has come close to being definite. The second: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in the adverbial phrase, what governs it being the adverbial phrase or what the adverbial phrase is attached to. Like it is: (رَسُولٌ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ مُصَدِّقٌ).
His saying: (مِنْ قَبْلُ): it is indeclinable (mabnī) here because it is cut off from the genitive construct; the implied form is: "before that".
(فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ): He brought لَمَّا after لَمَّا before the answer of the first. There are two views on the answer of the first. One: its answer is the second لَمَّا together with its answer. This is weak, because the fāʾ is with the second لَمَّا, and لَمَّا is not answered with the fāʾ — unless one holds that the fāʾ is redundant, according to what al-Akhfash permits.
The second: that كَفَرُوا is the answer of both the first and the second, because what they require is one and the same.
It is also said: the second is a repetition, so it needed no answer.
It is also said: the answer of the first is omitted, its implied form being "they rejected it", or something like that.
(فَلَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ): it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in construct with its agent.

ukberi-tibyan:90-90.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (بِئْسَمَا اشْتَرَوْا بِهِ أَنْفُسَهُمْ أَنْ يَكْفُرُوا بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ بَغْيًا أَنْ يُنَزِّلَ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ عَلَى مَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ فَبَاءُوا بِغَضَبٍ عَلَى غَضَبٍ وَلِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابٌ مُهِينٌ (٩٠)).
His saying, the Exalted: (بِئْسَمَا اشْتَرَوْا): there are several views on it. The first: that مَا is an unqualified indefinite noun (nakira ghayr mawṣūfa), accusative as a tamyīz (specification); al-Akhfash said this. On this view اشْتَرَوْا is an adjective of something omitted, its implied form being "a thing" or "disbelief"; this omitted element is the one specified [for blame] (al-makhṣūṣ), and the fāʿil (agent) of بِئْسَ is concealed in it. Its parallel is: لَنِعْمَ الْفَتَى أَضْحَى بِأَكْنَافِ حَايِلِ ("How excellent a youth, [one who] came to be in the environs of Ḥāyil"), i.e. "a youth who came to be".
And His saying: (أَنْ يَكْفُرُوا): the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is that they disbelieve". It is also said that أَنْ يَكْفُرُوا is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) of the hāʾ in بِهِ. It is also said that it is a mubtadaʾ, and بِئْسَ with what follows it is a khabar about it.
The second view: that مَا is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa), with اشْتَرَوْا as its adjective, and أَنْ يَكْفُرُوا on the views mentioned; here one adds that it may be the one specified for blame.
The third view: that مَا takes the place of الَّذِي ("that which"), and it is the noun of بِئْسَ, and أَنْ يَكْفُرُوا is the one specified for blame. It is also said that the noun of بِئْسَ is concealed in it, and الَّذِي with its ṣila (relative clause) is the one specified for blame.
The fourth view: that مَا is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), i.e. "evil is their purchase"; on this view the fāʿil of بِئْسَ is concealed, because the maṣdar here is specific, not a genus.
His saying: (بَغْيًا): a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose).
It may also be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because what precedes indicates that they transgressed a transgression.
(أَنْ يُنَزِّلَ اللَّهُ): an object of purpose (mafʿūl min ajlihi), i.e. "they transgressed because Allah sent down". It is also said that the implied form is "out of transgression over what Allah sent down", i.e. out of envy over the revelation with which Allah singled out His Prophet. The object of يُنَزِّلُ is omitted, i.e. "that Allah sends down something". (مِنْ فَضْلِهِ): مِنْ may also be redundant (zāʾida), according to the view of al-Akhfash.
And (مِنْ) [Translator's note: so printed; the word meant is مَنْ in عَلَى مَنْ يَشَاءُ] is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, i.e. "upon a man whom He wills".
It may also mean "the one whom", and the object of يَشَاءُ is omitted, i.e. "He wills its descent upon him".
It may also be that يَشَاءُ means "He chooses" and "He selects". And (مِنْ عِبَادِهِ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted hāʾ; it may also be in the position of the genitive as a further adjective of مَنْ. (فَبَاءُوا بِغَضَبٍ): i.e. "being objects of wrath", so it is a ḥāl. عَلَى غَضَبٍ is an adjective of the first غَضَبٍ. (مُهِينٌ): the yāʾ is a substitute for a wāw, because it is from الْهَوَانُ ("humiliation").

ukberi-tibyan:91-91.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ آمِنُوا بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ قَالُوا نُؤْمِنُ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْنَا وَيَكْفُرُونَ بِمَا وَرَاءَهُ وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا مَعَهُمْ قُلْ فَلِمَ تَقْتُلُونَ أَنْبِيَاءَ اللَّهِ مِنْ قَبْلُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ (٩١)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَيَكْفُرُونَ): i.e. "while they disbelieve"; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and what governs it is قَالُوا in His saying: (قَالُوا نُؤْمِنُ). What governs it cannot be نُؤْمِنُ, since if it were so, the wording of the ḥāl would have had to be وَنَكْفُرُ, i.e. "while we disbelieve". The hāʾ in (وَرَاءَهُ) refers back to مَا. The hamza in وَرَاءَ is a substitute for a yāʾ, because a word whose first radical is a wāw does not have a wāw as its third radical; and what shows it is that it is a yāʾ in تَوَارَيْتُ, not a hamza. Ibn Jinnī said: according to us it is a hamza, because of their saying وُرَيْئَةٌ with a hamza in the diminutive.
(وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ): a clause in the position of the ḥāl, and what governs it is يَكْفُرُونَ.
It may also be that what governs it is the sense of settledness indicated by (مَا), since the implied form is "in that which is settled beyond it". (مُصَدِّقًا): a corroborative ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida); what governs it is the verbal sense in الْحَقُّ, since the meaning is "and it is established, confirming". The one it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl) is, according to some, the latent (mustatir) pronoun in الْحَقُّ; according to others the one it describes is a pronoun indicated by the speech, and الْحَقُّ is a maṣdar (verbal noun) that does not carry a pronoun in the way an active participle carries one, in their view. As for the maṣdar that stands in for the verb, as when you say ضَرْبًا زَيْدًا ("strike Zayd!"), it carries the pronoun according to some.
(فَلِمَ): مَا here is interrogative, and its alif was omitted with the preposition to distinguish between the interrogative and the declarative (khabariyya); it has come in poetry without omission. Like it are: (فِيمَ أَنْتَ مِنْ ذِكْرَاهَا), (عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ) and (مِمَّ خُلِقَ).
(تَقْتُلُونَ): i.e. "you killed". The meaning is that their forefathers killed, and since they were pleased with their deed, He attributed the killing to them. إِنْ كُنْتُمْ: its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what preceded.

ukberi-tibyan:92-92.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ مُوسَى بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ ثُمَّ اتَّخَذْتُمُ الْعِجْلَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ وَأَنْتُمْ ظَالِمُونَ (٩٢)).
His saying, the Exalted: (بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ): it may be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from مُوسَى, its implied form being: "he came to you possessing clear proofs and argument", or "he came with the clear proofs accompanying him". It may also be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "by reason of establishing the clear proofs".

ukberi-tibyan:93-93.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَكُمْ وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ الطُّورَ خُذُوا مَا آتَيْنَاكُمْ بِقُوَّةٍ وَاسْمَعُوا قَالُوا سَمِعْنَا وَعَصَيْنَا وَأُشْرِبُوا فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْعِجْلَ بِكُفْرِهِمْ قُلْ بِئْسَمَا يَأْمُرُكُمْ بِهِ إِيمَانُكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ (٩٣)).
His saying, the Exalted: (فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْعِجْلَ): i.e. "the love of the calf"; the muḍāf was omitted, because what the heart drinks in is love, not the calf itself.
(بِكُفْرِهِمْ): i.e. "because of their disbelief".
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted element, i.e. "mixed with their disbelief".
(وَأُشْرِبُوا): in the position of the ḥāl, and what governs it is قَالُوا, i.e. "they said that, having been made to drink in"; قَدْ is intended, because the past verb is not a ḥāl except with قَدْ. The Kufans said: it is not needed.
It may also be that وَأُشْرِبُوا is resumptive (mustaʾnaf); but the first is stronger, because He said after that: (قُلْ بِئْسَمَا يَأْمُرُكُمْ), which is the reply to their saying: (سَمِعْنَا وَعَصَيْنَا); so it is preferable that there be nothing extraneous between them.

ukberi-tibyan:185-185.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ فِيهِ الْقُرْآنُ هُدًى لِلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَاتٍ مِنَ الْهُدَى وَالْفُرْقَانِ فَمَنْ شَهِدَ مِنْكُمُ الشَّهْرَ فَلْيَصُمْهُ وَمَنْ كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَى سَفَرٍ فَعِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ بِكُمُ الْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ الْعُسْرَ وَلِتُكْمِلُوا الْعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُوا اللَّهَ عَلَى مَا هَدَاكُمْ (١٨٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ): there are two views on its nominative case. The first: it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "it is a month", meaning the counted days; on this view (الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ) is a naʿt (adjective) of (شهر) or of (رمضان). The second: it is a mubtadaʾ, and then there are two views on the khabar: one, that it is (الذي أنزل); the other, that (الذي أنزل) is an adjective and the khabar is the clause, namely His saying (فمن شهد).
If it is said: had it been a khabar, the fāʾ would not be in it, because (شهر رمضان) does not resemble a conditional — the reply is: according to al-Akhfash the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); according to others it is not redundant, but entered because you described (الشهر) with (الذي), so the fāʾ entered just as it enters the khabar of (الذي) itself; similar to it is: «قُلْ إِنَّ الْمَوْتَ الَّذِي تَفِرُّونَ مِنْهُ فَإِنَّهُ مُلَاقِيكُمْ».
If it is said: where then is the pronoun in the clause referring back to the mubtadaʾ?
The reply: the overt noun was put in its place for emphasis of grandeur, i.e. "whoever of you witnesses it", as the poet said:
لَا أَرَى الْمَوْتَ يَسْبِقُ الْمَوْتُ شَيْءٌ ... بَغَّضَ الْمَوْتُ ذَا الْغِنَى وَالْفَقِيرَا
(I do not see anything outstripping death; death has made the rich and the poor alike hate it.)
That is, "nothing outstrips it". And (مَن) here is conditional and a mubtadaʾ, and what follows it is the khabar. It may also mean "the one who" (الذي), in which case the khabar is (فليصمه).
And (مِنْكُمْ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent pronoun; the object of (شهد) is omitted, i.e. "witnessed (was present in) the town". And (الشَّهْرَ): an adverbial of time, or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa).
It is not permissible for the implied form to be "whoever witnesses the new moon of the month", because that would apply to the sick, the traveller and the healthy resident, whereas the one obliged to fast is the one present in the town when he is healthy.
It has also been said: the implied form is "the new moon of the month"; on this view (الشهر) is an explicit direct object, standing in place of "the new moon". This is weak for two reasons: the first is what we have mentioned — it would make fasting obligatory on everyone without exception, which is not the case.
The second: (شهد) means "was present", and one does not say "I was present at the new moon of the month"; one only says "I saw the new moon". The hāʾ in (فَلْيَصُمْهُ) is the pronoun of the month, and it is a direct object by extension, not an adverbial, since if it were an adverbial (فِي) would be with it, because the pronoun of an adverbial is not an adverbial by itself.
(شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ) is also read in the accusative («شَهْرَ رَمَضَانَ»), and there are three views on it:
The first: it is a badal (substitute) for (أَيَّامًا مَعْدُودَاتٍ). The second: by implying "I mean" (أعني) (شَهْرَ).
The third: that it is accusative by (تَعْلَمُونَ), i.e. "if you know the honour of the month of Ramaḍān", the muḍāf having been omitted. In an irregular (shādhdh) reading it is read «شَهْرِي رَمَضَانَ» as mubtadaʾ and khabar.
As for His saying (أُنْزِلَ فِيهِ الْقُرْآنُ): the meaning is "concerning its merit", as you say "a verse was revealed about (في) the thing".
It has also been said: it is an adverbial, i.e. the whole Quran was sent down in this month to the lowest heaven.
And (هُدًى) and (بَيِّنَاتٍ): two ḥāls of (القرآن).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ بِكُمُ الْيُسْرَ): the bāʾ here is for adhesion (ilṣāq); the meaning is: He wants to make ease adhere to you in what He has prescribed for you. The implied form is: "Allah wants, by your breaking the fast in a state of excuse, ease."
(وَلِتُكْمِلُوا الْعِدَّةَ): it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (اليسر); the implied form is "that you complete" (لأن تكملوا), and on this view the lām is redundant, like His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَكِنْ يُرِيدُ لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ).
It has also been said: the implied form is "in order to make it easy for you, and that you complete". It has also been said: "and that you complete the number, He did that".

ukberi-tibyan:186-186.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ الدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لِي وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا بِي لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ (١٨٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ): i.e. "then say to them: I am…", because it is the answer to «إِذَا سَأَلَكَ». And (أُجِيبُ): a second khabar (predicate).
And (فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا) means "let them respond" (فليجيبوا), just as you say قَرَّ and اسْتَقَرَّ with one meaning; and they said اسْتَجَابَهُ meaning جَابَهُ. (لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ): the majority read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the shīn; its past tense is رَشَدَ with fatḥa.
It is also read with fatḥa on the shīn (يَرْشَدُونَ), its past tense being رَشِدَ with kasra, and that is a dialect.
It is also read with kasra on the shīn (يُرْشِدُونَ), its past tense being أَرْشَدَ, i.e. "they guide others".

ukberi-tibyan:187-187.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ الصِّيَامِ الرَّفَثُ إِلَى نِسَائِكُمْ هُنَّ لِبَاسٌ لَكُمْ وَأَنْتُمْ لِبَاسٌ لَهُنَّ عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَخْتَانُونَ أَنْفُسَكُمْ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَعَفَا عَنْكُمْ فَالْآنَ بَاشِرُوهُنَّ وَابْتَغُوا مَا كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَكُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا حَتَّى يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ الْخَيْطِ الْأَسْوَدِ مِنَ الْفَجْرِ ثُمَّ أَتِمُّوا الصِّيَامَ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ وَلَا تُبَاشِرُوهُنَّ وَأَنْتُمْ عَاكِفُونَ فِي الْمَسَاجِدِ تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ فَلَا تَقْرَبُوهَا كَذَلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ آيَاتِهِ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ (١٨٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ الصِّيَامِ): (ليلة) is an adverbial of time (ẓarf) for (أحل). From the standpoint of i'rab it may not be an adverbial for (الرفث), because that is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and the governed word of a maṣdar does not precede it.
It is permissible, however, for (الليلة) to be an adverbial for (الرفث) by way of explication (tabyīn); the implied form is "it is made lawful for you that you have relations on the night of the fast", so it was omitted and the mentioned word was made an explication of it. The common usage is رَفَثَ بِالْمَرْأَةِ with the bāʾ; it came here with (إلى) only because the meaning of (الرفث) is "going in unto" (الإفضاء), as though He said "going in unto".
(إِلَى نِسَائِكُمْ): the hamza in (نساء) is substituted for a wāw, as you say with the same meaning نِسْوَة. It is a plural with no singular from its own root; rather its singular is امرأة. As for (نساء), it is the plural of نسوة; and it has also been said: it has no singular.
(كُنْتُمْ تَخْتَانُونَ): (كنتم) here has the form of the past, and its meaning is also past; the meaning is that the betrayal used to occur from them, and He turned to them in forgiveness for it.
It has also been said: He meant betrayal in the future, and mentioned (كان) to relate the situation by it, as you say: "if you do it, you will have been (كنتَ) unjust". The alif of (تختانون) is substituted for a wāw, because it is from خَانَ يَخُونُ, and you say in the plural خَوَنَة.
(فَالْآنَ): the real sense of (الآن) is the time you are in; it may also apply to the recent past and to the future whose occurrence is near, treating the near as though it were present, and that is what is meant here, because His saying «فَالْآنَ بَاشِرُوهُنَّ» means: "the time of the night in which intercourse used to be forbidden to you, We have now made it permissible for you". On this view (الآن) is an adverbial for «بَاشِرُوهُنَّ».
It has also been said: the speech is construed according to the meaning, the implied form being "now We have permitted you to have relations with them", the omitted part being indicated by the imperative wording which is meant as permission. On this view (الآن) is in its real sense.
(حَتَّى يَتَبَيَّنَ): one says تَبَيَّنَ الشيءُ, بَانَ, أَبَانَ and اسْتَبَانَ, all of them intransitive; أبان, استبان and تبيّن are also sometimes used transitively. (حتى) means "until" (إلى). And (مِنَ الْخَيْطِ الْأَسْوَدِ) is in the position of the accusative, because the meaning is "until the white thread separates from the black thread", as you say "the hand separated from its forearm (بانت اليد من زندها)", i.e. parted from it.
As for (مِنَ الْفَجْرِ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in (الأبيض), and it may be a tamyīz (specification). (الفجر) is originally the maṣdar of فَجَرَ يَفْجُرُ, meaning "to cleave".
(إِلَى اللَّيْلِ): (إلى) here is for the end-limit of the completing. It may also be a ḥāl of (الصيام), being attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted.
(وَأَنْتُمْ عَاكِفُونَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of a ḥāl. The meaning is: "do not have relations with them when you have intended iʿtikāf in the mosque"; what is meant is not the prohibition of having relations with them inside the mosque, because that is forbidden even outside iʿtikāf. (تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ فَلَا تَقْرَبُوهَا): the fāʾ here enters as a conjunction on something omitted, its implied form being "take heed, and do not approach them".
(كَذَلِكَ): in the position of the accusative, an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "with an explanation like this explanation He makes clear (يَبِين)".

ukberi-tibyan:188-188.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِالْبَاطِلِ وَتُدْلُوا بِهَا إِلَى الْحُكَّامِ لِتَأْكُلُوا فَرِيقًا مِنْ أَمْوَالِ النَّاسِ بِالْإِثْمِ وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ (١٨٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَيْنَكُمْ): it may be an adverbial (ẓarf) for (تأكلوا), because the meaning is "do not pass them around among yourselves".
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (الأموال), i.e. "being among you" or "circulating among you"; in meaning it is like His saying: (إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ تِجَارَةً حَاضِرَةً تُدِيرُونَهَا بَيْنَكُمْ).
And (بِالْبَاطِلِ): in the position of the accusative governed by (تأكلوا), i.e. "do not take them by a false means". It may also be a ḥāl of (الأموال), and it may be a ḥāl of the agent in (تأكلوا), i.e. "acting falsely". (وَتُدْلُوا): jussive (majzūm), conjoined to (تأكلوا). The lām in (لِتَأْكُلُوا) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (تدلوا). (تدلوا) may also be accusative, with the sense of combining, i.e. "do not combine eating and bringing (the matter) to the judges". And (بِالْإِثْمِ): like (بالباطل).

ukberi-tibyan:189-189.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْأَهِلَّةِ قُلْ هِيَ مَوَاقِيتُ لِلنَّاسِ وَالْحَجِّ وَلَيْسَ الْبِرُّ بِأَنْ تَأْتُوا الْبُيُوتَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهَا وَلَكِنَّ الْبِرَّ مَنِ اتَّقَى وَأْتُوا الْبُيُوتَ مِنْ أَبْوَابِهَا وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ (١٨٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَنِ الْأَهِلَّةِ): the majority read it with a vowel on the nūn and with the hamza kept after the lām, according to the original. In an irregular reading it is read with the nūn assimilated into the lām and the hamza dropped. The original is (الأهلة);
the vowel of the hamza was cast onto the lām so that it took a vowel, then the connecting hamza was dropped because the lām now had a vowel, so it became لَهِلَّة; when the nūn met the lām, the nūn was changed into a lām and assimilated into the other lām. Similar to it is لَحْمَر for الأَحْمَر, and it is a dialect. (وَالْحَجِّ): conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (الناس).
There is no disagreement about the nominative of «الْبِرُّ» here, because the khabar of (ليس) is «بِأَنْ تَأْتُوا», and that is fixed by the bāʾ entering it. This is not so in (لَيْسَ الْبِرَّ أَنْ تُوَلُّوا), since neither of the two is accompanied by anything that determines it as the noun or the khabar.
And (الْبُيُوتَ) is read with ḍamma on the bāʾ, which is the original in plurals on the pattern fuʿūl, the weak root being like the sound one; the first letter of this plural is given ḍamma only to match the ḍamma of the second letter and the wāw after it.
It is also read with kasra on the bāʾ (بِيُوت), because a yāʾ comes after it and kasra is of the same kind as the yāʾ. No account is taken of passing from a kasra to a ḍamma, because the ḍamma here is on the yāʾ, and the yāʾ is reckoned as two kasras, so the kasra on the bāʾ is as though it were next to a kasra. The same disagreement exists over الغُيُوب, الجُيُوب and الشُّيُوخ; and from this it became permissible in the diminutive to use ḍamma and kasra, so one says بُيَيْت and بِيَيْت.
(وَلَكِنَّ الْبِرَّ مَنِ اتَّقَى): like «وَلَكِنَّ الْبِرَّ مَنْ آمَنَ», which has already been discussed.

ukberi-tibyan:191-191.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا تُقَاتِلُوهُمْ عِنْدَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ حَتَّى يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ فِيهِ فَإِنْ قَاتَلُوكُمْ فَاقْتُلُوهُمْ كَذَلِكَ جَزَاءُ الْكَافِرِينَ (١٩١)).
All three are read with the alif (تُقَاتِلُوهُمْ، يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ، قَاتَلُوكُمْ); it is then a prohibition of the preliminaries of killing, and so indicates the prohibition of killing a fortiori; and it matches His saying «وَقَاتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ». All three are also read without the alif (تَقْتُلُوهُمْ، يَقْتُلُوكُمْ، قَتَلُوكُمْ), and it is then a prohibition of killing itself, matching His saying «وَاقْتُلُوهُمْ حَيْثُ ثَقِفْتُمُوهُمْ» and His saying «فَاقْتُلُوهُمْ». The implied form in His saying (فإن قاتلوكم) is "in it" (فيه).
(كَذَلِكَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject). And (جَزَاءُ): its khabar (predicate). (الجزاء) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its object.
It may be in the sense of the accusative, the implied form being "thus is Allah's recompensing of the disbelievers".
It may also be in the sense of the nominative, as with a verb whose agent is not named (passive), the implied form being "thus are the disbelievers recompensed". The same holds for every maṣdar resembling this one.

ukberi-tibyan:143-143.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَاكُمْ أُمَّةً وَسَطًا لِتَكُونُوا شُهَدَاءَ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ الرَّسُولُ عَلَيْكُمْ شَهِيدًا وَمَا جَعَلْنَا الْقِبْلَةَ الَّتِي كُنْتَ عَلَيْهَا إِلَّا لِنَعْلَمَ مَنْ يَتَّبِعُ الرَّسُولَ مِمَّنْ يَنْقَلِبُ عَلَى عَقِبَيْهِ وَإِنْ كَانَتْ لَكَبِيرَةً إِلَّا عَلَى الَّذِينَ هَدَى اللَّهُ وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَانَكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِالنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ (١٤٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَكَذَلِكَ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being: "and like Our guiding whom We will, We made you"; and جَعَلْنَا is equivalent to "We made into" (صَيَّرْنَا).
And (عَلَى النَّاسِ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to شُهَدَاءَ. (الْقِبْلَةَ): it is the first object, and the second object is omitted, and «الَّتِي» is an adjective of that omitted element; the implied form is: "and We did not make the qibla [to be] the qibla which…". It is also said that الَّتِي is an adjective of the qibla that is mentioned, and the second object is omitted, its implied form being: "and We did not make the qibla which you were upon a qibla [except…]". (مَنْ يَتَّبِعُ): مَنْ means "the one who" (الَّذِي) and is in the position of the accusative governed by (نَعْلَمَ); and (مِمَّنْ يَنْقَلِبُ) is attached to (نَعْلَمَ), the meaning being "so as to distinguish the one who follows from the one who turns back".
It is not permissible for (مِنْ) [Translator's note: so vowelled in the source; the discussion concerns مَنْ] to be interrogative, because that would require نَعْلَمَ to be suspended (taʿlīq) from governing; and if it were suspended from it, the مِنْ [of مِمَّنْ] would be left with nothing to be attached to, because what comes after an interrogative is not attached to what precedes it. Nor is it valid to attach it to (يَتَّبِعُ), because in meaning it is attached to (نَعْلَمَ); the meaning is not "which group follows, from among those who turn back". (عَلَى عَقِبَيْهِ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "returning". (وَإِنْ كَانَتْ): إِنْ is the one lightened from the heavy [إِنَّ], and its noun is omitted; the lām in His saying «لَكَبِيرَةً» is a compensation for what was omitted. It is also said: the lām was used to distinguish the إِنْ lightened from the heavy one from the other kinds of إِنْ.
The Kufans said: إِنْ means مَا ("not") and the lām means إِلَّا ("except"); this is very weak, in that the use of the lām in the sense of إِلَّا is supported neither by attested usage (samāʿ) nor by analogy (qiyās). The noun of كَانَ is a hidden pronoun indicated by the context, its implied form being: "and though the turning, or the prayer, or the qibla, was…".
(إِلَّا عَلَى الَّذِينَ): (عَلَى) is attached to كَبِيرَةً; إِلَّا entered for the meaning and did not change the i'rab. (وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ): the khabar (predicate) of كَانَ is omitted, and the lām is attached to that omitted element, its implied form being: "and Allah was not intending to let your faith go to waste" (وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ مُرِيدًا لِأَنْ يُضِيعُ إِيمَانَكُمْ). This recurs in the Quran; like it is: (لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ). The Kufans said: لِيُضِيعَ is the khabar, and the lām enters for emphasis (tawkīd). This is far-fetched, because the lām is the lām of the genitive (lām al-jarr), and أَنْ after it is intended, so the implied form on their view becomes: "it was not for Allah [to commit] the wasting of your faith".
(رَءُوفٌ): it is read with a wāw after the hamza, like شَكُورٍ; and it is read without wāw [رَؤُفٌ], like يَقِظٍ and فَطِنٍ. And there has come in poetry: بِالرَّؤُفِ الرَّحِيمِ ("by the Compassionate, the Merciful").

ukberi-tibyan:144-144.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَدْ نَرَى تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ فِي السَّمَاءِ فَلَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ قِبْلَةً تَرْضَاهَا فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ وَحَيْثُ مَا كُنْتُمْ فَوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُ وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ لَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ. . . . . . (١٤٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَدْ نَرَى): its wording is imperfect (future), but what is meant by it is the past.
And (فِي السَّمَاءِ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the maṣdar (verbal noun) [تَقَلُّبَ]; and if it were made a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْوَجْه, it would be permissible.
(فَوَلِّ): it is transitive to two objects; the first is «وَجْهَكَ» and the second is (شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ). It may also reach the second by means of (إِلَى), as when you say: وَلَّى وَجْهَهُ إِلَى الْقِبْلَةِ ("he turned his face toward the qibla"). Al-Naḥḥās said: شَطْرَ here is an adverb of place, because it means "direction".
(وَحَيْثُ): an adverb for (وَلُّوا); and if you make it conditional, it is accusative governed by «كُنْتُمْ», because [the verb] is made jussive by it while it is made accusative by [the verb]. (أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ): in the position of a ḥāl; something like it occurs at the beginning of the sūra.

ukberi-tibyan:145-145.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَئِنْ أَتَيْتَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ بِكُلِّ آيَةٍ مَا تَبِعُوا قِبْلَتَكَ وَمَا أَنْتَ بِتَابِعٍ قِبْلَتَهُمْ وَمَا بَعْضُهُمْ بِتَابِعٍ قِبْلَةَ بَعْضٍ وَلَئِنِ اتَّبَعْتَ أَهْوَاءَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَكَ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ إِنَّكَ إِذًا لَمِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ (١٤٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَئِنْ أَتَيْتَ): the lām prepares for the oath (tawṭiʾa li-l-qasam), and it is not obligatory, as shown by His saying: (وَإِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهُوا عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ).
(مَا تَبِعُوا): i.e. "they will not follow"; so it is a past verb with a future meaning, and «مَا» entered in accordance with the past form of the wording. The fāʾ was omitted in the apodosis (jawāb) because the verb of the condition is past. Al-Farrāʾ said: إِنْ here means لَوْ ("if [counterfactual]"), which is why «مَا» is in the apodosis; this is far-fetched, because إِنْ is for the future and لَوْ for the past. (إِذَنْ): a particle, the nūn in it being original; it is used only in a reply (jawāb), and here it governs nothing, because its governing is in a verb, and there is no verb.

ukberi-tibyan:146-146.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ يَعْرِفُونَهُ كَمَا يَعْرِفُونَ أَبْنَاءَهُمْ. . . . . . (١٤٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «يَعْرِفُونَهُ» is the khabar (predicate). It is possible for الَّذِينَ to be a badal (substitute) for الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ in the preceding verse. It is also possible for it to be a badal for الظَّالِمِينَ; then يَعْرِفُونَهُ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْكِتَابَ or from الَّذِينَ, because it contains two pronouns referring back to them. It may also be accusative with an implied "I mean" (أَعْنِي), or nominative with an implied «هُمْ» ("they are").
(كَمَا): an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), and مَا is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:147-147.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُمْتَرِينَ (١٤٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). It is also said: الْحَقُّ is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "what they concealed is the truth" (مَا كَتَمُوهُ الْحَقَّ [Translator's note: so in the source, with the accusative]), or "what they knew".
It is also said: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "they know it" or "they recite it".
And (مِنْ رَبِّكَ) is, on both views, a ḥāl (circumstantial). ʿAlī, peace be upon him, read (الْحَقَّ) in the accusative, governed by (يَعْلَمُونَ).

ukberi-tibyan:148-148.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلِكُلٍّ وِجْهَةٌ هُوَ مُوَلِّيهَا فَاسْتَبِقُوا الْخَيْرَاتِ أَيْنَ مَا تَكُونُوا يَأْتِ بِكُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعًا إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (١٤٨)).
