His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلِكُلٍّ وِجْهَةٌ): وِجْهَةٌ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and لِكُلٍّ is its khabar (predicate); the implied form is "for every group". وِجْهَةٌ has come according to the original form, whereas the regular (analogical) form is جِهَةٌ, like عِدَةٌ and زِنَةٌ.
الْوِجْهَةُ is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of "that toward which one turns", like الْخَلْقُ in the sense of "what is created". It is a maṣdar with its augment letters dropped, because the verb is تَوَجَّهَ or اتَّجَهَ, and the maṣdar is التَّوَجُّهُ or الِاتِّجَاهُ; and وَجَهَ [as a simple verb] like وَعَدَ was not used from it. (هُوَ مُوَلِّيهَا): it is read with kasra on the lām, and there are two views on هُوَ:
The first: it is the pronoun of the name of Allah, and the second object is omitted, i.e. "Allah is the one who turns that group toward that direction" (اللَّهُ مَوِّلِي تِلْكَ الْجِهَةَ ذَلِكَ الْفَرِيقَ), i.e. He commands it to [face] it. The second: it is the pronoun of كُلّ, i.e. that group turns itself toward the direction.
It is also read مَوْلَاهَا [Translator's note: so vowelled in the source; the reading described is مُوَلَّاهَا] with fatḥa on the lām. On this reading هُوَ is the pronoun of the group, and مَوْلَى is [a participle] for that whose agent is not named (passive); the first object is the nominative pronoun within it, and هَا is the pronoun of the second object, namely the pronoun of the direction (الْوِجْهَة) — and it is also said: of the turning (التَّوْلِيَة). On this reading it is not permissible for هُوَ to be the pronoun of the name of Allah, because that is impossible in meaning. The clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of وِجْهَةٌ. It was read as an irregular (shādhdh) reading: «وَلِكُلِّ وِجْهَةٍ», with كُلّ in construct with وِجْهَة; on this reading the lām is redundant (zāʾida), and the implied form is: "every direction, Allah turns its people toward it". The redundancy of the lām is made acceptable by the object coming first and by the governing word being an active participle.
(أَيْنَمَا): an adverb for (تَكُونُوا).

ukberi-tibyan:149-149.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنْ حَيْثُ خَرَجْتَ فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ وَإِنَّهُ لَلْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ. . . . . . . . (١٤٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمِنْ حَيْثُ خَرَجْتَ): حَيْثُ here cannot be conditional, because مَا is not with it, and a condition is formed with it only together with مَا. On this view مِنْ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to His saying «فَوَلِّ». And (إِنَّهُ لَلْحَقُّ): the hāʾ is the pronoun of the turning (al-tawallī).

ukberi-tibyan:150-150.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنْ حَيْثُ خَرَجْتَ فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ وَحَيْثُ مَا كُنْتُمْ فَوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُ لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَيْكُمْ حُجَّةٌ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْهُمْ فَلَا تَخْشَوْهُمْ وَاخْشَوْنِي وَلِأُتِمَّ نِعْمَتِي عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ (١٥٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَحَيْثُ مَا كُنْتُمْ): it may be conditional or non-conditional, as we mentioned in the first place. (لِئَلَّا): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, its implied form being: "We did that so that… not".
And (حُجَّةٌ) is the noun of كَانَ, and the khabar (predicate) is لِلنَّاسِ; and عَلَيْكُمْ was originally an adjective (ṣifa) of the حُجَّة, which was placed first and so became accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is not permissible for it to be attached to the حُجَّة, lest the complement (ṣila) of the maṣdar precede it.
(إِلَّا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْهُمْ): an exception from other than the first [category] (i.e. a disconnected exception), because no one had any argument against them. (وَلِأُتِمَّ): this lām is conjoined to the first lām.
(عَلَيْكُمْ): attached to أُتِمَّ; it may also be attached to something omitted, on the basis that it is a ḥāl from نِعْمَتِي.

ukberi-tibyan:151-151.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا فِيكُمْ رَسُولًا مِنْكُمْ يَتْلُو عَلَيْكُمْ آيَاتِنَا وَيُزَكِّيكُمْ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمْ مَا لَمْ تَكُونُوا تَعْلَمُونَ (١٥١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَمَا): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being: "you will be guided with a guidance like Our sending", or "a completing like Our sending", or "a favour like Our sending".
A group of the exacting scholars (al-muḥaqqiqūn) said: the implied form is: "so remember Me, as We sent"; on this view it is accusative as an adjective of the remembrance, i.e. "a remembrance like My sending". The fāʾ does not prevent that, just as it does not prevent it in the chapter of the condition. And مَا is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يُخَادِعُونَ اللَّهَ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَمَا يَخْدَعُونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ (٩)).
His saying, the Exalted: (يُخَادِعُونَ اللَّهَ): there are two views on the clause. First: it has no grammatical position.
Second: its position is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). There are two views on the owner of the ḥāl and what governs it. First: it is from the pronoun in يَقُولُ, so what governs it is يَقُولُ, the implied sense being "he says 'we believe', while deceiving". Second: it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in His saying بِمُؤْمِنِينَ, governed by the active participle, the implied sense being "and they are not believers in the state of their deceiving".
It may not be in the position of the genitive as an adjective of مُؤْمِنِينَ, because that would require negating their deception, whereas the meaning is the affirmation of deception. Nor may the clause be a ḥāl from the pronoun in آمَنَّا, because آمَنَّا is reported from them by (يَقُولُ); so if يُخَادِعُونَ were a ḥāl from the pronoun in آمَنَّا it would also be reported speech, and this is impossible for two reasons.
First: they did not say "we believe and we deceive". Second: He informed about them by saying يُخَادِعُونَ; had it been from them, it would have been نُخَادِعُ with nūn.
There is an omission in the phrase, its implied form being "(يُخَادِعُونَ) the Prophet of Allah". It is also said that it is to be taken literally, without omission.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: (وَمَا يُخَادِعُونَ): most readings are with the alif. The basic sense of the mufāʿala pattern is that it is between two parties, and it is so here, because in their deception they place themselves in the position of a stranger, the deception going back and forth between the two: they deceive themselves and their selves deceive them. It is also said that the mufāʿala here is from one party, as in your saying سَافَرَ الرَّجُلُ ("the man travelled") and عَاقَبْتُ اللِّصَّ ("I punished the thief"). It is also read يَخْدَعُونَ without alif, with fatḥa on the yāʾ;
and it is read with ḍamma on it (يُخْدَعُونَ), on the view that the agent of the deceiving is Satan, as though He said "and Satan deceives them only [about themselves]". (إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ), i.e. "about themselves". أَنْفُسَهُمْ is accusative as an object; its accusative is not as an excepted noun, because the verb has not taken its object before إِلَّا.

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ فَزَادَهُمُ اللَّهُ مَرَضًا وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْذِبُونَ (١٠)).
His saying, the Exalted: (فَزَادَهُمُ اللَّهُ): زَادَ is used intransitively, as in your saying زَادَ الْمَاءُ ("the water increased"), and is used transitively to two objects, as in your saying زِدْتُهُ دِرْهَمًا ("I gave him a dirham more"); it has come in the verse on this latter usage.
Imāla (inclining the vowel towards i) of the zāy is permitted, because it takes kasra in your saying زِدْتُهُ. This is permitted in verbs whose second radical is wāw, like خَافَ, but it is better in those whose second radical is yāʾ.
His saying, the Exalted: (أَلِيمٌ) is faʿīl with the meaning of mufʿil, because it is from your saying آلَمَ, so it is مُؤْلِمٌ ("painful"). Its plural is أُلَمَاءُ and إِلَامٌ, like شَرِيفٌ, شُرَفَاءُ and شِرَافٌ.
His saying, the Exalted: (بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْذِبُونَ) is in the position of the nominative as an adjective of أَلِيمٌ, and the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, its implied form being "painful, existing [as a consequence] of their lying", or "deserved". مَا here is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun) and its ṣila is يَكْذِبُونَ; كَانَ is not its ṣila, because it is the incomplete (nāqiṣa) kāna, from which no maṣdar is used. يَكْذِبُونَ is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كَانَ. The maṣdariyya مَا is a particle according to Sībawayh and a noun according to al-Akhfash; on both views nothing in its ṣila refers back to it.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لَا تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ قَالُوا إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُونَ (١١)).
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: (وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ): إِذَا is in the position of the accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), and what governs it is its answer, namely His saying قَالُوا. Some said what governs it is قِيلَ, and this is a mistake, because that is in the position of the genitive, إِذَا being put in a genitive construct with it, and the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern the muḍāf. The original form of قِيلَ is قُوِلَ; the kasra was felt heavy on the wāw, so it was dropped, and the qāf was given kasra so that the wāw would turn into yāʾ, as they did in أَدَلَّ and أَحَقَّ. Some of them say that they transferred the kasra of the wāw to the qāf; this is weak, because you only transfer the vowel to it [the qāf] after assuming it to be quiescent, so this requires dropping the ḍamma of the qāf, and that is a lot of work.
It is permitted to give the qāf a tinge (ishmām) of ḍamma, with the yāʾ remaining quiescent, as a pointer to the original.
Some of the Arabs say, in the like of قِيلَ and بِيعَ: قُولَ and بُوعَ, treating verbs with wāw and with yāʾ alike. They said: [those with wāw] come out on their original form, and in those with yāʾ the yāʾ is turned into wāw because it is quiescent and the letter before it has ḍamma. This is not read unless a transmission of it is established. The object standing in the place of the agent is a maṣdar (verbal noun), namely الْقَوْلُ ("saying"), and it is left implied because the clause after it explains it; the implied form is "and when a saying is said to them, namely 'do not cause corruption'". Its counterpart is (ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُا الْآيَاتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ), i.e. "an idea and an opinion appeared to them". It is also said that (لَهُمْ) is what stands in the place of the agent, because the statement is not complete with it, and what it is is explained by the clause after it [Translator's note: the reasoning here is compressed in the text and reads as given].
His saying (لَا تُفْسِدُوا) may not be what stands in the place of the agent, because a clause cannot be an agent, so it cannot stand in the place of the agent. لَهُمْ is in the position of the accusative as an object of قِيلَ.
His saying (فِي الْأَرْضِ): the hamza in الْأَرْضِ is a radical, and the root sense of the word is spaciousness; from it comes their saying أَرَضَتِ الْقُرْحَةُ ("the sore spread") when it widens [Translator's note: the text has «أَرْضَتِ»]. The saying of whoever said it was called أَرْضٌ because feet crush it (تَرُضُّهَا) amounts to nothing, because the hamza in it is a radical, and الرَّضُّ ("crushing") is not from this root.
فِي الْأَرْضِ may not be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in تُفْسِدُوا, because that would convey nothing; rather it is an adverbial attached (mutaʿalliq) to (تُفْسِدُوا).
His saying (إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ): «مَا» here restrains (kāffa) إِنَّ from governing, because it has prepared it to enter sometimes on a noun and sometimes on a verb, whereas إِنَّ only governed because it was exclusive to nouns.
(إِنَّمَا) conveys the restriction of the predicate to that to which the predicate is attributed, as in His saying (إِنَّمَا اللَّهُ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ). In some places it conveys that what is mentioned is distinguished by the mentioned quality and nothing else, as in your saying «إِنَّمَا زَيْدٌ كَرِيمٌ» ("Zayd is only generous"), i.e. of the qualities ascribed to him there is nothing in him except generosity. Of this kind is His saying, the Exalted: (إِنَّمَا أَنَا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ), because they demanded of him what human beings cannot do, so he affirmed for himself the quality of being human and negated of himself what is other than that.
His saying نَحْنُ: it is a detached pronoun noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma. Pronouns are indeclinable only because they need the overt nouns to which they refer back, so they are like particles in their need for nouns. Its last letter was given a vowel so that two quiescent letters would not meet, and the nūn was given ḍamma because the word is a nominative pronoun of the speaker, so it resembles the tāʾ in قُمْتُ. It is also said that it was given ḍamma because its position is nominative; and it is also said that the nūn resembles the wāw, so it was given the vowel homogeneous with the wāw. نَحْنُ is the pronoun of the speaker and those with him; it is used for two and for a group, and a single speaker of great standing uses it. It is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (مُصْلِحُونَ) is its khabar (predicate).

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْمُفْسِدُونَ وَلَكِنْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ (١٢)).
His saying, the Exalted: (أَلَا) is a particle with which speech is opened to alert the addressee.
It is also said that its meaning is "truly" (حَقًّا), and the one who said this allowed أَنَّ to take fatḥa after it, just as it takes fatḥa after حَقًّا; this is extremely far-fetched.
His saying (هُمُ الْمُفْسِدُونَ): هُمْ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and الْمُفْسِدُونَ its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of إِنَّ. هُمْ may also be in the position of the accusative as a tawkīd (emphasis) of the noun of إِنَّ.
It may also be a separating pronoun (faṣl) with no grammatical position, because the khabar here is definite, and a pronoun like this separates between the khabar and the adjective, marking what follows it as the khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ آمِنُوا كَمَا آمَنَ النَّاسُ قَالُوا أَنُؤْمِنُ كَمَا آمَنَ السُّفَهَاءُ أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ السُّفَهَاءُ وَلَكِنْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ (١٣)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ آمِنُوا): what stands in the place of the object [Translator's note: so in the text; "in the place of the agent" is evidently meant, as in the previous verse] is الْقَوْلُ ("the saying"), and آمِنُوا explains it, because command and prohibition are a saying.
His saying (كَمَا آمَنَ النَّاسُ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a faith like the faith of the people"; and likewise كَمَا آمَنَ السُّفَهَاءُ.
His saying (السُّفَهَاءُ أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ): there are four ways with these two hamzas. First: pronouncing both fully, which is the original.
Second: pronouncing the first fully and turning the second into a pure wāw, to escape two hamzas in succession; the second was made a wāw because the first has ḍamma. Third: softening the first, that is, making it between hamza and wāw, and pronouncing the second fully. Fourth: the same, except that the second is a wāw.
It is not permitted to make the second between hamza and wāw, because that would bring it close to alif, and alif does not occur after a ḍamma or a kasra [Translator's note: so in the text; the point is presumably that making a hamza with fatḥa "between-between" brings it close to alif]. Some have permitted it.

ukberi-tibyan:55-55.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ يَا مُوسَى لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّى نَرَى اللَّهَ جَهْرَةً فَأَخَذَتْكُمُ الصَّاعِقَةُ وَأَنْتُمْ تَنْظُرُونَ (٥٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لَكَ): He said نؤمن لك and not بك only because the meaning is "we will not believe on account of your word", or it is construed as "we will not acknowledge to you what you have claimed".
(جَهْرَةً): a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the name of Allah, i.e. "we see Him manifest, not veiled".
It has also been said: it is a ḥāl from the tāʾ and mīm in قلتم, i.e. "you said that openly".
It has also been said: it is a maṣdar made accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "you spoke out openly".
And (الصَّاعِقَةُ) is فاعلة in the sense of مُفعِلة; one says أصعقتهم الصاعقة ("the thunderbolt struck them"), so it is like their saying أورس النبت فهو وارس ("the plant turned yellow, so it is yellowed") and أعشب فهو عاشب ("[the land] became grassy, so it is grassy").

ukberi-tibyan:57-57.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَظَلَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ الْغَمَامَ وَأَنْزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَنَّ وَالسَّلْوَى كُلُوا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا وَلَكِنْ كَانُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ (٥٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَظَلَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ الْغَمَامَ): i.e. "We made it a shade"; it is not like your saying ظلّلت زيدا بظلّ ("I shaded Zayd with a shade"), because that would lead to the clouds being covered by another shade. The implied form may also be "with the clouds". And (الْغَمَامَ) is the plural of غمامة; but the correct view is to say that it is a collective (jins) noun, and when you want the single unit you add the tāʾ to it.
His saying, Exalted is He: (الْمَنَّ وَالسَّلْوَى): two collective nouns. (كُلُوا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ): «من» here is partitive or for clarifying the kind, and the object is omitted; the implied form is: "eat something of the good things". (أَنْفُسَهُمْ): the object of يظلمون; He has used أفعُل, which is one of the plurals of paucity, in the place of a plural of multitude.

ukberi-tibyan:58-58.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذْ قُلْنَا ادْخُلُوا هَذِهِ الْقَرْيَةَ فَكُلُوا مِنْهَا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمْ رَغَدًا وَادْخُلُوا الْبَابَ سُجَّدًا وَقُولُوا حِطَّةٌ نَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ خَطَايَاكُمْ وَسَنَزِيدُ الْمُحْسِنِينَ) ((٥٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هَذِهِ الْقَرْيَةَ): القرية is a naʿt (adjective) of هذه. (سُجَّدًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial); it is the plural of ساجد, and it is more expressive than السجود. (حِطَّةٌ): the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "our request is relief [from sins]", and the position of the clause is accusative by القول ("saying").
It has been read حطّةً, in the accusative, as a maṣdar, i.e. "relieve us [of our sins] with a relief". (نَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ): the answer to the command; it is in reality jussive by an omitted condition, its implied form being: "if you say that, We will forgive you". The majority pronounce the rāʾ distinctly before the lām; some assimilated it, but that is weak, because the rāʾ is a trilled letter and so counts as two letters; when it is assimilated one of them is lost, and the doubled lām has no trill in it, so the trill that stands in place of a letter is lost. It is read «تُغفَرْ لكم» with tāʾ, as a verb whose agent is not named (passive).
And with yāʾ likewise, because there is a separation between the verb and its agent, and because the femininity of الخطايا is not a true one.
(خَطَايَاكُمْ): it is the plural of خطيئة, and its original form according to al-Khalīl is خطائئ with two hamzas, the first of them with kasra, it being the one converted from the extra yāʾ in خطيئة; so it is like صحيفة and صحائف. Combining the two hamzas was found heavy, so they moved the first hamza to the position of the second, and its pattern became فعالئ. They did that only so that the one with kasra would become final and be changed into yāʾ, making it فعالى; then they replaced the kasra of the first hamza with fatḥa, and the yāʾ after it changed into alif, as they said يا لهفا and يا أسفا [for يا لهفي and يا أسفي]; so the hamza came to be between two alifs, and a yāʾ was substituted for it, because the hamza is close to the alif and they disliked the coming together of three alifs. So خطايا is فعالى, and on this view there are five changes in it: moving the last radical (lām) forward from its place, replacing the kasra with fatḥa, changing the final hamza into yāʾ, then changing it into alif, then changing the hamza which is the lām into yāʾ. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «يَا لَهَفِي، وَيَا أَسَفِي», but the point being illustrated is the change of final yāʾ to alif after fatḥa (يا لهفا، يا أسفا); translated as the argument requires, with the printed forms noted here.]
Sībawayh said: its original form is خطائئ, as al-Khalīl said, except that he changed the second hamza into yāʾ because of the kasra before it, then replaced the kasra with fatḥa, so the yāʾ changed into alif, then changed the hamza into yāʾ; so there is no transposition on his view. Al-Farrāʾ said: the singular is خطيّة, with the hamza lightened and assimilated, so it is like مطيّة and مطايا.

ukberi-tibyan:59-59.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَبَدَّلَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا قَوْلًا غَيْرَ الَّذِي قِيلَ لَهُمْ فَأَنْزَلْنَا عَلَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا رِجْزًا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ (٥٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَبَدَّلَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا قَوْلًا): there is an omission in the speech, its implied form being: "so those who did wrong exchanged what had been said to them for a saying other than what had been said to them". بدّل takes one object by itself and another by the bāʾ; the one with the bāʾ is the one abandoned, and the one without the bāʾ is the one that comes to exist, as in the saying of Abū al-Najm:
وَبَدَّلْتُ وَالدَّهْرُ ذُو تَبَدُّلٍ ... هَيْفًا دَبُورًا بِالصَّبَا وَالشَّمْأَلِ.
(And I was given in exchange — and time is full of change — a hot west wind in place of the east wind and the north wind.)
So what departed from her is «الصبا» (the east wind), and what came to her is الهيف (the hot wind); and so it is here.
It may also be that «بدّل» is construed according to the meaning, its implied form being: "so those who did wrong said a saying other than that which…", because the changing of the saying was by a saying. (مِنَ السَّمَاءِ): in the position of the accusative, attached to (أنزلنا). It may also be an adjective of رجز, and so be attached to something omitted. الرجز with kasra and with ḍamma on the rāʾ are two dialectal variants. (بِمَا كَانُوا): the bāʾ is in the sense of cause, i.e. "We punished them because of their transgression".

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذِ اسْتَسْقَى مُوسَى لِقَوْمِهِ فَقُلْنَا اضْرِبْ بِعَصَاكَ الْحَجَرَ فَانْفَجَرَتْ مِنْهُ اثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ مَشْرَبَهُمْ كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا مِنْ رِزْقِ اللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ (٦٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (اسْتَسْقَى): the alif is converted from a yāʾ, because it is from السقي ("giving water").
The alif of العصا is from a wāw, because its dual is عصوان, and you say عصوت بالعصا, i.e. "I struck with the staff". The implied form is: "so he struck [and it gushed forth]".
(فَانْفَجَرَتْ مِنْهُ اثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ): among the Arabs some make the shīn quiescent and some give it kasra, and it has been read with both; and some give it fatḥa. (مُفْسِدِينَ): an emphatic ḥāl (circumstantial), because His saying لا تعثوا means "do not cause corruption".

ukberi-tibyan:61-61.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ يَا مُوسَى لَنْ نَصْبِرَ عَلَى طَعَامٍ وَاحِدٍ فَادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخْرِجْ لَنَا مِمَّا تُنْبِتُ الْأَرْضُ مِنْ بَقْلِهَا وَقِثَّائِهَا وَفُومِهَا وَعَدَسِهَا وَبَصَلِهَا قَالَ أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ الَّذِي هُوَ أَدْنَى بِالَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ اهْبِطُوا مِصْرًا فَإِنَّ لَكُمْ مَا سَأَلْتُمْ وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذِّلَّةُ وَالْمَسْكَنَةُ وَبَاءُوا بِغَضَبٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ النَّبِيِّينَ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ ذَلِكَ بِمَا عَصَوْا وَكَانُوا يَعْتَدُونَ (٦١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُخْرِجْ لَنَا مِمَّا تُنْبِتُ الْأَرْضُ): the object of يخرج is omitted, its implied form being: "something of what the earth grows".
And «ما» is in the sense of الذي, or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective; it cannot be maṣdariyya, because the implied object cannot be described as "growing", since growing is a maṣdar (verbal noun) while what is omitted is a substance.
(مِنْ بَقْلِهَا): من here is for clarifying the kind, and its position is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted pronoun, its implied form being: "of what the earth grows, being of its herbs". It may also be a badal (substitute) from the first ما, with the preposition repeated. القثّاء, with kasra and with ḍamma on the qāf, are two dialectal variants, and it has been read with both. The hamza is radical, because of their saying أقثأت الأرض ("the land abounded in cucumbers"); its singular is قثّاءة. (أَدْنَى): its alif is converted from a wāw, because it is from دنا يدنو, when something comes near. It has two meanings: first, that the meaning is "that whose value is near because of its lowliness, and which is easy to obtain".
Second: that it is in the sense of "what is near to you", because it is in this world.
And (الَّذِي هُوَ أَدْنَى) [Translator's note: in context this appears to describe الذي هو خير, i.e. what consists in obeying Allah's command, whose benefit is deferred to the Hereafter; the text as printed reads «الذي هو أدنى»]: what consisted in obeying the command of Allah, because its benefit is deferred to the Hereafter.
It has also been said: the alif replaces a hamza, because it is taken from دنؤ يدنؤ, so he is دنيء ("base"), and the maṣdar is الدناءة, which pertains to a lowly thing; the hamza was changed to alif, as he said: «لا هناك المرتع» ("may the pasture not be wholesome for you").
It has also been said: its original form is أدون, from الشيء الدون ("the inferior thing"); the wāw was moved to the end and changed into alif, so its pattern now is أفلع.
(اهْبِطُوا): the good [reading] is kasra on the bāʾ; ḍamma is a dialectal variant, and it has been read with it. (مِصْرًا): indefinite, and for that reason it is fully declinable; the meaning is "go down to a town among the towns". It has also been said that it is definite, and is declinable because its middle letter is quiescent; leaving it undeclined is permissible, and it has been read so; it is like هند and دعد. المصر originally is the boundary between two things.
(مَا سَأَلْتُمْ): ما is in the position of the accusative as the noun of إنّ, and it is in the sense of الذي; it is weak for it to be an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective. And (بَاءُوا): the alif in باءوا is converted from a wāw, because of your saying in the imperfect يبوء.
(بِغَضَبٍ): in the position of the ḥāl, i.e. "they returned having incurred wrath".
(مِنَ اللَّهِ): in the position of the genitive as an adjective of غضب. (ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ): ذلك is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and بأنهم كانوا يكفرون is the khabar (predicate); the implied form is: "that wrath is deserved because of their disbelief". (النَّبِيِّينَ): the original of النبي has a hamza, because it is from النبأ, which is "news", since he gives news from Allah; but it was lightened by changing the hamza into a yāʾ, then the extra yāʾ was assimilated into it. It has also been said: whoever does not pronounce the hamza takes it from النبوّة, which is elevation, because the rank of the Prophet is elevated above the ranks of all other creatures. It has also been said: النبيّ is "the road", for the one who conveys from Allah is the creatures' road to Allah and His road to the creatures.
It has been read with the hamza, according to the original form. (بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in يقتلون, the implied form being: "they kill them, being in the wrong". It may also be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being: "a killing without right"; on both views it is an emphasis. (عَصَوْا): its original form is عصيُوا; when the yāʾ was vowelled and preceded by fatḥa, it was changed to alif, then the alif was omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the fatḥa remained to indicate it. The wāw here is assimilated into the wāw after it, because the letter before it has fatḥa, so it has no lengthening (madd) that would prevent assimilation; it has parallels in the Qur'an, such as His saying: فقد اهتدوا وإن تولوا. But if the letter before this wāw has ḍamma, as in آمنوا وعملوا, its assimilation is not permissible, because a wāw preceded by ḍamma has a long madd, and so it is treated as a barrier between the two letters.

ukberi-tibyan:94-94.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ إِنْ كَانَتْ لَكُمُ الدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ خَالِصَةً مِنْ دُونِ النَّاسِ فَتَمَنَّوُا الْمَوْتَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ (٩٤)).
His saying, the Exalted: (إِنْ كَانَتْ لَكُمُ الدَّارُ): الدَّارُ is the noun of كَانَ, and there are three views on the khabar (predicate). The first: it is خَالِصَةً, and عِنْدَ is an adverbial (ẓarf) of خَالِصَةً, or of the settledness contained in لَكُمْ.
It may also be that «عِنْدَ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الدَّارُ, what governs it being كَانَ or the settledness. As for لَكُمْ, on this view it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (كَانَ), because كَانَ governs prepositional phrases.
It may also be for clarification (li-l-tabyīn), its place then being after خَالِصَةً, i.e. "exclusively yours", so that it is attached to خَالِصَةً itself. It may also be an adjective of خَالِصَةً placed before it, in which case it is attached to something omitted.
The second view: that the khabar of كَانَ is لَكُمْ, with عِنْدَ اللَّهِ an adverbial and خَالِصَةً a ḥāl, what governs it being كَانَ or the settledness. The third: that عِنْدَ اللَّهِ is the khabar, and خَالِصَةً a ḥāl, what governs it being either «عِنْدَ», or what it is attached to, or «كَانَ», or «لَكُمْ». What made it acceptable for «عِنْدَ» to be the khabar of كَانَ is «لَكُمْ», since it contains specification and clarification. Its parallel is His saying: (وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ); were it not for لَهُ, it would not be correct for كُفُوًا to be the khabar. (مِنْ دُونِ): in the position of the accusative, governed by خَالِصَةً, because you say: "such-and-such was made free of such-and-such (خَلَّصَ كَذَا مِنْ كَذَا)".

ukberi-tibyan:95-95.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَنْ يَتَمَنَّوْهُ أَبَدًا بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالظَّالِمِينَ (٩٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (أَبَدًا): an adverbial (ẓarf). (بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ): i.e. "because of what [their hands] sent ahead", so it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and its meaning is close to the meaning of the mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). And (مَا) means "that which", or is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa), or is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), in which case the object of قَدَّمَتْ is omitted, i.e. "because of their hands' sending ahead evil".

ukberi-tibyan:96-96.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَتَجِدَنَّهُمْ أَحْرَصَ النَّاسِ عَلَى حَيَاةٍ وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا يَوَدُّ أَحَدُهُمْ لَوْ يُعَمَّرُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ وَمَا هُوَ بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ أَنْ يُعَمَّرَ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ (٩٦)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَلَتَجِدَنَّهُمْ): it is the [verb] transitive to two objects, the second being «أَحْرَصَ», and «عَلَى» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَحْرَصَ. (وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا): there are two views on it. The first: it is conjoined to النَّاسِ in meaning, the implied form being: "more eager than the people", i.e. those of their time, "and more eager than those who associate partners", meaning by it the Magians (al-Majūs), because when they prayed for long life they would say: "may you live a thousand Nawrūz". On this view there are two views on (يَوَدُّ). One: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا, its implied form being "one of them having wished". What shows you this is that if you said "and than those who associate partners, those of whom one wishes (الَّذِينَ يَوَدُّ أَحَدُهُمْ)", it would be correct as a description; and from here the Kufans said: this is by omission of the relative noun and retention of the ṣila (relative clause).
The second view: that you make يَوَدُّ أَحَدُهُمْ a ḥāl from the hāʾ and mīm in وَلَتَجِدَنَّهُمْ, i.e. "you will surely find them the most eager of people, one of them wishing". The second of the two views on «مِنَ الَّذِينَ» is that it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf), the implied form being: "and among those who associate partners are a people of whom one wishes", or "one of whom wishes".
The past of يَوَدُّ is وَدِدْتُ, with a kasra on the second radical; for that reason the wāw remained sound, because what follows it does not take a kasra in
the imperfect. (لَوْ يُعَمَّرُ): لَوْ here has the sense of أَنْ that puts the verb in the accusative, but it does not make it accusative; and it is not the one by which a thing is precluded because of the preclusion of something else. Two things show you this. One: that this one is necessarily attached to the future, while the other has its meaning in the past.
The second: that يَوَدُّ is transitive to one object and is not among the verbs that are suspended from governing (yuʿallaq ʿan al-ʿamal); hence it follows that لَوْ has the sense of أَنْ. And [أَنْ] has come after ((يَوَدُّ)) in His saying, the Exalted: (أَيَوَدُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَنْ تَكُونَ لَهُ جَنَّةٌ); and that is frequent in the Quran and in poetry. And يُعَمَّرُ is transitive to one object, and that has been made to stand in the place of the agent.
And (أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ): an adverbial (ẓarf). (وَمَا هُوَ بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ): there are two views on هُوَ. One: it is the pronoun of أَحَدٌ, i.e. "and that wisher is not…". بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ is the khabar (predicate) of مَا. «مِنَ الْعَذَابِ» is attached to بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ, and «أَنْ يُعَمَّرَ» is in the position of the nominative, governed by بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ, i.e. [and the man is not one whom] his long life [removes]. The other view: that هُوَ is the pronoun of the long life (al-taʿmīr), which is indicated by His saying «لَوْ يُعَمَّرُ».
And His saying أَنْ يُعَمَّرَ is a badal (substitute) of هُوَ. هُوَ cannot be the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), because what explains the pronoun of the matter is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the entry of the bāʾ in بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ prevents that.

ukberi-tibyan:97-97.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ مَنْ كَانَ عَدُوًّا لِجِبْرِيلَ فَإِنَّهُ نَزَّلَهُ عَلَى قَلْبِكَ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَهُدًى وَبُشْرَى لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ (٩٧)).
His saying, the Exalted: (مَنْ كَانَ عَدُوًّا لِجِبْرِيلَ): مَنْ is conditional, and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "let him die of rage", or the like. (فَإِنَّهُ نَزَّلَهُ): its parallel in meaning is: (مَنْ كَانَ يَظُنُّ أَنْ لَنْ يَنْصُرَهُ اللَّهُ), then He said: ((فَلْيَمْدُدْ)). ((بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ)) is in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in نَزَّلَ, which is the pronoun of جِبْرِيلَ, and it is the pronoun returning to the noun of إِنَّ. The implied form is: "his bringing it down with the permission accompanying him", or "being permitted to do so".
(مُصَدِّقًا): a ḥāl from the hāʾ in نَزَّلَهُ; and likewise «هُدًى وَبُشْرَى», i.e. "guiding and giving glad tidings".

ukberi-tibyan:98-98.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَنْ كَانَ عَدُوًّا لِلَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكَالَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَدُوٌّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ (٩٨)).
His saying, the Exalted: (عَدُوٌّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ): He put the overt noun in the place of the pronoun, because the original is: "whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels, then Allah is an enemy to him", or "to them". It has many parallels in the Quran, which will pass by you, if Allah wills.

ukberi-tibyan:100-100.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوَكُلَّمَا عَاهَدُوا عَهْدًا نَبَذَهُ فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمْ . . . . .).
His saying, the Exalted: (أَوَكُلَّمَا): the wāw is for conjunction, and the hamza before it is for interrogation in the sense of disapproval. The conjunction here is to the sense of the preceding speech in His saying: (أَفَكُلَّمَا جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ) and what follows it. It is also said that the wāw is redundant (zāʾida); and it is also said that it is «أَوْ», which is for one of two things, given a fatḥa as its vowel; it was read anomalously (shādhdh) with it quiescent.
(عَهْدًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun) not from the wording of the verb mentioned. It may also be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "they gave a covenant"; and here there is another object omitted, its implied form being: "they made a covenant with Allah" or "they made a covenant with you".

ukberi-tibyan:101-101.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ مُصَدِّقٌ لِمَا مَعَهُمْ نَبَذَ فَرِيقٌ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ كِتَابَ اللَّهِ وَرَاءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ كَأَنَّهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ (١٠١)).
His saying, the Exalted: (رَسُولٌ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ مُصَدِّقٌ): it is like His saying: (كِتَابٌ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ مُصَدِّقٌ), and it has been mentioned. (الْكِتَابَ) is the object of أُوتُوا, and «كِتَابَ اللَّهِ» is the object of نَبَذَ. (كَأَنَّهُمْ): it, together with what it governs, is in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial); what governs it is نَبَذَ, and the one it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl) is فَرِيقٌ; its implied form is "resembling the ignorant".

ukberi-tibyan:14-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا لَقُوا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قَالُوا آمَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَوْا إِلَى شَيَاطِينِهِمْ قَالُوا إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُسْتَهْزِئُونَ (١٤) اللَّهُ يَسْتَهْزِئُ بِهِمْ وَيَمُدُّهُمْ فِي طُغْيَانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ (١٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (لَقُوا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its original form is لَقِيُوا. The yāʾ was made quiescent because the ḍamma was heavy on it, then dropped because it was quiescent and the wāw after it was quiescent, and the qāf was given ḍamma to accord with the wāw.
It is also said: the ḍamma of the yāʾ was transferred to the qāf after the qāf was made quiescent, and then the yāʾ was dropped.
Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read لَاقَوُا, with an alif, fatḥa on the qāf and ḍamma on the wāw. The qāf was given fatḥa and the wāw ḍamma for the reason we shall mention on His saying (اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلَالَةَ).
His saying (خَلَوْا إِلَى): it is read with the hamza pronounced fully, which is the original.
It is also read by throwing the vowel of the hamza onto the wāw and dropping the hamza, so that the wāw takes kasra with the kasra of the hamza (خَلَوِ لَى). The original form of خَلَوْا is خَلَوُوا; the first wāw was turned into alif because it was vowelled and the letter before it had fatḥa, then dropped so that two quiescent letters would not meet, and the fatḥa remained to indicate the dropped alif.
His saying (إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ): the original is إِنَّنَا; the middle nūn was dropped, according to the correct view, as it is dropped in إِنَّ when it is lightened, as in His saying, the Exalted: (وَإِنْ كُلٌّ لَمَّا جَمِيعٌ). مَعَكُمْ is an adverbial (ẓarf) standing in the place of the khabar (predicate), i.e. "being with you".
His saying, the Exalted: (مُسْتَهْزِئُونَ): it is read with the hamza pronounced fully, which is the original; and with it turned into a yāʾ with ḍamma, because the letter before it has kasra. Some drop the yāʾ, because it resembles the radical yāʾ in a word like يَرْمُونَ, and give the zāy ḍamma (مُسْتَهْزُونَ). The same disagreement exists over softening the hamza of يَسْتَهْزِئُ بِهِمْ.
His saying, the Exalted: (يَعْمَهُونَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ and mīm in يَمُدُّهُمْ.
(فِي طُغْيَانِهِمْ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (يَمُدُّهُمْ) as well, or, if you wish, to (يَعْمَهُونَ). You may not make both of them ḥāls from [the object of] يَمُدُّهُمْ, because a single governing word does not govern two ḥāls.

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلَالَةَ بِالْهُدَى فَمَا رَبِحَتْ تِجَارَتُهُمْ وَمَا كَانُوا مُهْتَدِينَ (١٦)).
His saying, the Exalted: (اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلَالَةَ): the original is اشْتَرَيُوا. The yāʾ was turned into alif, then the alif was dropped so that two quiescent letters, the alif and the wāw, would not meet. If you say: but the wāw here is vowelled — it is answered: its vowel is accidental, so it is not taken into account; and the fatḥa of the rāʾ is an indication of the dropped alif.
It is also said: the yāʾ was made quiescent because the ḍamma was heavy on it, then dropped so that two quiescent letters would not meet.
The wāw was given ḍamma rather than another vowel only to distinguish between the wāw of the plural and the radical wāw in a case like His saying لَوِ اسْتَطَعْنَا. It is also said it was given ḍamma because ḍamma here is lighter than kasra, since it is of the same kind as wāw.
It is also said that it was given the vowel of the dropped yāʾ. It is also said that it was given ḍamma because it is an agent pronoun, so it is like the tāʾ in قُمْتُ. It is also said: it is for the plural, so it is like نَحْنُ. Some have pronounced it with hamza, likening it to a wāw with a permanent ḍamma, as in أَثْؤُبٌ.
Some of them give it fatḥa, preferring lightness; some give it kasra, according to the basic rule for the meeting of two quiescent letters; and some pronounce it with a slurred vowel (ikhtilās) and so drop it because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; this is weak, because there is a fatḥa before it, and the fatḥa does not indicate it.

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَثَلُهُمْ كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي اسْتَوْقَدَ نَارًا فَلَمَّا أَضَاءَتْ مَا حَوْلَهُ ذَهَبَ اللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمْ وَتَرَكَهُمْ فِي ظُلُمَاتٍ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ (١٧)).
His saying, the Exalted: (مَثَلُهُمْ كَمَثَلِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The kāf may be a preposition, in which case it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted; or it may be a noun meaning مِثْلَ ("like"), in which case it is not attached to anything.
His saying (الَّذِي اسْتَوْقَدَ): الَّذِي here is singular in wording while the meaning is plural, as shown by His saying «ذَهَبَ اللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمْ» and what follows it. There are two views on the singular's occurring here in the place of the plural. First: it denotes a genus, like مَنْ and مَا, so the pronoun refers back to it sometimes in the singular and sometimes in the plural.
Second: He meant الَّذِينَ, and the nūn was dropped because the expression is lengthened by the ṣila (relative clause). Its like is (وَالَّذِي جَاءَ بِالصِّدْقِ وَصَدَّقَ بِهِ), after which He said (أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُتَّقُونَ).
اسْتَوْقَدَ has the meaning of أَوْقَدَ ("kindled"), as اسْتَقَرَّ has the meaning of قَرَّ. It is also said that اسْتَوْقَدَ means "sought kindling".
His saying, the Exalted: (فَلَمَّا أَضَاءَتْ): لَمَّا here is a noun, an adverbial of time; and so it is in every place where a past-tense verb follows it and it has an answer. What governs it is its answer, as with إِذَا.
أَضَاءَتْ is transitive, so on this view «مَا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). It is also said that أَضَاءَ is intransitive — one says ضَاءَتِ النَّارُ and أَضَاءَتْ with one meaning — so on this view «مَا» is an adverbial. There are three views on «مَا». First: it has the meaning of الَّذِي.
Second: it is an indefinite noun described [by what follows], i.e. "a place around him". Third: it is redundant (zāʾida).
His saying (ذَهَبَ اللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمْ): the bāʾ here makes the verb transitive, as the hamza makes it transitive, the implied sense being أَذْهَبَ اللَّهُ نُورَهُمْ ("Allah removed their light"). Its like is frequent in the Qur'an.
The bāʾ may come in a case like this for the ḥāl (circumstance), as in your saying ذَهَبْتُ بِزَيْدٍ, i.e. "I went with Zayd accompanying me".
His saying, the Exalted: (وَتَرَكَهُمْ فِي ظُلُمَاتٍ): تَرَكَهُمْ here is transitive to two objects, because the meaning is "He made them", and what is meant by it is not the leaving that is neglect. On this view the second object may be فِي ظُلُمَاتٍ, so that the preposition is not attached to something omitted, and «لَا يُبْصِرُونَ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
It is also possible that لَا يُبْصِرُونَ is the second object, and فِي ظُلُمَاتٍ an adverbial attached to تَرَكَهُمْ or to «يُبْصِرُونَ»; or it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in يُبْصِرُونَ, or from the first object.

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ فَهُمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ) «(١٨)».
His saying, the Exalted: (صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ): the majority read it in the nominative, as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are deaf". It has been read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, in the accusative, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يُبْصِرُونَ.
His saying, the Exalted: (فَهُمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ) is a resumptive clause. It is also said that its position is that of a ḥāl; this is a mistake, because what comes after the fāʾ is not a ḥāl, since the fāʾ expresses sequence, and there is no sequence in circumstantial states.
(يَرْجِعُونَ) is an intransitive verb, i.e. "they do not desist from their falsehood", or "they do not return to the truth".
It is also said that it is transitive and its object is omitted, its implied form being "so they do not return an answer", like His saying: (إِنَّهُ عَلَى رَجْعِهِ لَقَادِرٌ) «(٨)».

ukberi-tibyan:192-192.t: Allah the Exalted says: (فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ), i.e. to them (١٩٢).

ukberi-tibyan:193-193.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَاتِلُوهُمْ حَتَّى لَا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ وَيَكُونَ الدِّينُ لِلَّهِ فَإِنِ انْتَهَوْا فَلَا عُدْوَانَ إِلَّا عَلَى الظَّالِمِينَ (١٩٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حَتَّى لَا تَكُونَ): (حتى) may mean "so that" (كي).
It may also mean "until" (إلى أن); and (كان) here is complete (tāmma). And His saying (وَيَكُونَ الدِّينُ): (كان) may be complete, or incomplete (nāqiṣa), with «لِلَّهِ» as the khabar (predicate). (إِلَّا عَلَى الظَّالِمِينَ): in the position of the nominative, the khabar of «لا»; (إلا) entered for the sake of the meaning: in the affirmative you say "hostility is against the wrongdoers", and when you bring the negation and (إلا), the i'rab remains as it was.
[Translator's note: the Arabic reads «فإذا جئت بالنفي، وإلا بقي الإعراب…», which is syntactically awkward; it has been rendered according to the evident sense.]

ukberi-tibyan:194-194.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الشَّهْرُ الْحَرَامُ بِالشَّهْرِ الْحَرَامِ وَالْحُرُمَاتُ قِصَاصٌ فَمَنِ اعْتَدَى عَلَيْكُمْ فَاعْتَدُوا عَلَيْهِ بِمِثْلِ مَا اعْتَدَى عَلَيْكُمْ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الْمُتَّقِينَ (١٩٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَمَنِ اعْتَدَى عَلَيْكُمْ): «مَنْ» may be conditional, and it may mean "the one who" (الذي). In (بِمِثْلِ) the bāʾ is not redundant, and the implied form is "with a punishment matching their aggression". It may also be redundant (zāʾida), with (مثل) being an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "an aggression like their aggression".

ukberi-tibyan:195-195.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَأَنْفِقُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلَا تُلْقُوا بِأَيْدِيكُمْ إِلَى التَّهْلُكَةِ وَأَحْسِنُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ (١٩٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِأَيْدِيكُمْ): the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); one says أَلْقَى يَدَهُ and أَلْقَى بِيَدِهِ.
Al-Mubarrad said: it is not redundant; rather it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb, as in مَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ ("I passed by Zayd"). And (التَّهْلُكَة) is on the pattern tafʿula, from الهلاك (destruction).

ukberi-tibyan:196-196.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَأَتِمُّوا الْحَجَّ وَالْعُمْرَةَ لِلَّهِ فَإِنْ أُحْصِرْتُمْ فَمَا اسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ الْهَدْيِ وَلَا تَحْلِقُوا رُءُوسَكُمْ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ الْهَدْيُ مَحِلَّهُ فَمَنْ كَانَ مِنْكُمْ مَرِيضًا أَوْ بِهِ أَذًى مِنْ رَأْسِهِ فَفِدْيَةٌ مِنْ صِيَامٍ أَوْ صَدَقَةٍ أَوْ نُسُكٍ فَإِذَا أَمِنْتُمْ فَمَنْ تَمَتَّعَ بِالْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ فَمَا اسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ الْهَدْيِ فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي الْحَجِّ وَسَبْعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعْتُمْ تِلْكَ عَشَرَةٌ كَامِلَةٌ ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ أَهْلُهُ حَاضِرِي الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ (١٩٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالْعُمْرَةَ لِلَّهِ): the majority read it in the accusative, and the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (أتموا); it is the lām of the mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). It may also be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied form being "being for Allah". It is also read in the nominative (وَالْعُمْرَةُ), as mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). (فَمَا اسْتَيْسَرَ): (ما) is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is omitted, i.e. "then upon you is…".
It may also be a khabar with the mubtadaʾ omitted, i.e. "then what is obligatory is what is easy". (ما) may also be in the position of the accusative, its implied form being "then offer…" or "then render…". (استيسر) means تَيَسَّرَ ("became easy"), and the sīn here is not for requesting.
And (الْهَدْيِ): with the yāʾ unstressed it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it means "what is offered". It is also read with a doubled yāʾ (الهَدِيّ), and that is the plural of هَدِيَّة; it has also been said: it is faʿīl in the sense of a passive participle (mafʿūl). And (الْمَحِلّ): it may be a place, and it may be a time.
(فَفِدْيَةٌ): there is an omission in the speech, its implied form being "and he shaves, then upon him is a ransom".
(مِنْ صِيَامٍ): in the position of the nominative, an adjective of (الفدية). And (أَوْ) here is for choice, according to its basic meaning.
(النُّسُك) is originally a maṣdar in the sense of the passive participle, since it is from نَسَكَ يَنْسُكُ, and what is meant by it here is the thing sacrificed. It may also be a noun, not a maṣdar; and the sīn may be given sukūn (نُسْك).
(فَإِذَا أَمِنْتُمْ): (إذا) is in the position of the accusative. (فَمَنْ تَمَتَّعَ): a conditional in the position of a mubtadaʾ.
(فَمَا اسْتَيْسَرَ): the answer to (فمن), and (من) together with its answer is the answer to (إذا). What governs (إذا) is the sense of being established, because the implied form is "then upon him is what is easy", i.e. the offering becomes established upon him at that time.
(مَن) may also mean "the one who" (الذي), with the fāʾ entering its khabar to signal that what follows it is due by virtue of the tamattuʿ. (فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ): (من) is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ.
It may be a conditional, and it may mean "the one who"; the implied form is "then upon him is a fast".
It has been read (صِيَامًا) in the accusative, on the implied form "let him fast"; the maṣdar is annexed to its adverbial in meaning, while in wording it is a direct object by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa).
(وَسَبْعَةٍ): conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (ثلاثة). It has also been read (وَسَبْعَةً) in the accusative, its implied form being "and let you fast seven" or "and fast seven".
(ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ): the lām is in its basic meaning, i.e. "that is permissible for whoever…".
It has also been said: the lām means "upon" (على), i.e. "the offering is upon whoever's family is not…", like His saying: (أُولَئِكَ لَهُمُ اللَّعْنَةُ).

ukberi-tibyan:197-197.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الْحَجُّ أَشْهُرٌ مَعْلُومَاتٌ فَمَنْ فَرَضَ فِيهِنَّ الْحَجَّ فَلَا رَفَثَ وَلَا فُسُوقَ وَلَا جِدَالَ فِي الْحَجِّ وَمَا تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ يَعْلَمْهُ اللَّهُ وَتَزَوَّدُوا فَإِنَّ خَيْرَ الزَّادِ التَّقْوَى وَاتَّقُونِ يَا أُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ (١٩٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الْحَجَّ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «أَشْهُرٌ» is the khabar (predicate); the implied form is "the pilgrimage is the pilgrimage of months".
It has also been said: He made the months the pilgrimage, by extension.
The implied form may also be "the months of the pilgrimage are months"; on both views the omission of a muḍāf is necessary.
(فَمَنْ فَرَضَ): (من) is a mubtadaʾ; it may be conditional or mean "the one who" (الذي), and the khabar is (فلا رفث) and what follows; the referring pronoun is omitted, its implied form being "then no obscenity from him".
(فَلَا رَفَثَ وَلَا فُسُوقَ وَلَا جِدَالَ) is read with fatḥa on all of them, on the view that all are the noun of the first (لا), «لا» being repeated for emphasis in meaning, and the khabar is «فِي الْحَجِّ».
It may also be that the repeated (لا) is resumptive, so that (في الحج) is the khabar of (لا جدال), and the khabars of the first and second (لا) are omitted, i.e. "no obscenity in the pilgrimage and no wickedness in the pilgrimage", the khabar of the last sufficing for them. A parallel is their saying "Zayd, ʿAmr and Bishr are standing (قائم)": (قائم) is the khabar of Bishr and the khabar of the first two is omitted; and this is better with an adverbial. They are also read with the nominative in all of them, on the view that «لا» does not govern and what follows it is mubtadaʾ and khabar. (لا) may also govern as (ليس) governs, so that (في الحج) is in the position of the accusative.
It has also been read with the first two nominative with tanwīn and the last with fatḥa (فَلَا رَفَثٌ وَلَا فُسُوقٌ وَلَا جِدَالَ); a distinction was made between them only because the meaning of (فلا رفث ولا فسوق) is "do not commit obscenity and do not commit wickedness", while the meaning of (وَلَا جِدَالَ) is "there is no doubt about the obligation of the pilgrimage".
It has also been said: (لا جدال) means "do not dispute while you are in iḥrām". The fatḥa in all of them is stronger, because of the general negation in it.
(وَمَا تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ): there are several views on (من خير), which we mentioned under His saying (مَا نَنْسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ); here we add another view, namely that (من خير) is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "whatever deed of good you do".

ukberi-tibyan:198-198.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فَإِذَا أَفَضْتُمْ مِنْ عَرَفَاتٍ فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ عِنْدَ الْمَشْعَرِ الْحَرَامِ وَاذْكُرُوهُ كَمَا هَدَاكُمْ وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الضَّالِّينَ (١٩٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا): in the position of the accusative, on the implied form "in that you seek" (في أن تبتغوا); according to those other than Sībawayh it is in the position of the genitive, as we have explained in more than one place. If the preposition appeared in the wording, it could be attached to (الجناح) itself, because of the sense of inclining and leaning in it, or because it means "sin".
It may also be in the position of the nominative as an adjective of (جناح). Some allowed the preposition to be attached to (ليس), and there is weakness in that.
(مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to (تَبْتَغُوا), and thus also be an object.
It may also be an adjective of (فضل), so that (من) is attached to something omitted.
(فَإِذَا أَفَضْتُمْ): an adverbial (ẓarf), governed by (فاذكروا); the fāʾ here does not prevent what follows it from governing what precedes it, because it is a conditional. And (عَرَفَاتٍ): a plural with which a single place was named; were it not so it would be indefinite, but it is definite. They have put a ḥāl (circumstantial) in the accusative relating to it, saying "this is ʿArafāt, blessed (مُبَارَكًا) in it", because what is meant by it is a specific spot. Similar is أَبَانَانِ, the name of a mountain or a spot.
The tanwīn in (عرفات) and in every feminine plural corresponds to the nūn in مسلمون, and is not a sign of full declension. Some Arabs drop the tanwīn and give the tāʾ kasra;
and some give it fatḥa, treating the tāʾ of the plural like the tāʾ of the singular, and it is then diptote because of definiteness and femininity. The original of (أفضتم) is أَفْيَضْتُم [Translator's note: the printed text reads «أَفْضَيْتُمْ», evidently a slip for «أَفْيَضْتُمْ», given the root فاض يفيض stated next], because it is from فَاضَ يَفِيضُ, meaning "to flow"; when people are many on a road, their walking is like the flowing of a torrent.
(عِنْدَ الْمَشْعَرِ الْحَرَامِ): it may be an adverbial, and it may be a ḥāl of the agent pronoun. In (كَمَا هَدَاكُمْ) the kāf is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun).
It may also be a ḥāl of the agent, its implied form being "then remember Him resembling to you when He guided you" [Translator's note: so in the text: «مُشْبِهِينَ لَكُمْ حِينَ هَدَاكُمْ»]; and the omission of a muḍāf must be assumed, because a body does not resemble an event. Similar to it is (كَذِكْرِكُمْ آبَاءَكُمْ): the kāf is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, or a ḥāl, its implied form being "then remember Allah, being intense (in it)".
The kāf in the first may also mean "for/upon" (على), its implied form being "then remember Allah for what He guided you to", as Allah the Exalted said: (وَلِتُكَبِّرُوا اللَّهَ عَلَى مَا هَدَاكُمْ).
(وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ): (إن) here is lightened from the heavy (إنّ), and the implied form is "indeed, you were before it astray"; we have mentioned that under His saying: (وَإِنْ كَانَتْ لَكَبِيرَةً).

ukberi-tibyan:199-199.t:
Allah the Exalted says: {ثمَّ أفيضوا من حَيْثُ أَفَاضَ النَّاس وَاسْتَغْفرُوا الله إِن الله غَفُور رَحِيم}
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَفَاضَ النَّاسُ): the majority read it with ḍamma on the sīn, and it is a plural. It has also been read (النَّاسِي), meaning Adam; it is an adjective that came to be used predominantly for him, like al-ʿAbbās and al-Ḥarth, and His saying (فَنَسِيَ وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُ عَزْمًا) indicates it.

ukberi-tibyan:154-154.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تَقُولُوا لِمَنْ يُقْتَلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَمْوَاتٌ بَلْ أَحْيَاءٌ وَلَكِنْ لَا تَشْعُرُونَ (١٥٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَمْوَاتٌ): it is put in the plural according to the meaning of مَنْ, while (يُقْتَلُ) is put in the singular according to the wording of مَنْ; had مَيِّتٌ come [in the singular], it would have been eloquent. It is nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are dead".
(بَلْ أَحْيَاءٌ): i.e. "rather, say: they are alive". And «لِمَنْ يُقْتَلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَمْوَاتٌ» is in the position of the accusative governed by His saying وَلَا تَقُولُوا, because it is reported speech (maḥkī); and بَلْ does not enter into the reported speech here.
(وَلَكِنْ لَا تَشْعُرُونَ): the object (الْمَعْفُولُ [Translator's note: so in the source, evidently for الْمَفْعُولُ]) here is omitted, its implied form being: "you do not perceive their life".

ukberi-tibyan:155-155.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُمْ بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ الْخَوْفِ وَالْجُوعِ وَنَقْصٍ مِنَ الْأَمْوَالِ وَالْأَنْفُسِ وَالثَّمَرَاتِ وَبَشِّرِ الصَّابِرِينَ (١٥٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُمْ): the reply (jawāb) to an omitted oath. The imperfect verb is made indeclinable (mabnī) with the two nūns of emphasis, and the wāw was given fatḥa because of its lightness. (مِنَ الْخَوْفِ): in the position of the genitive as an adjective (ṣifa) of شَيْءٍ.
(مِنَ الْأَمْوَالِ): in the position of the accusative as an adjective of something omitted, its implied form being: "and a decrease [by which He] decreased something of the wealth" (وَنَقَصَ شَيْئًا مِنَ الْأَمْوَالِ), because النَّقْصُ is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of نَقَصْتُ, which is transitive to one object, and the object has been omitted.
According to al-Akhfash, (مِنْ) may be redundant (zāʾida). And مِنْ may be an adjective of نَقْصٍ, being for the beginning of the extent, i.e. "a decrease arising from the wealth".

ukberi-tibyan:156-156.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ إِذَا أَصَابَتْهُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ قَالُوا إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ (١٥٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ إِذَا أَصَابَتْهُمْ): in the position of the accusative as an adjective (ṣifa) of الصَّابِرِينَ, or by an implied "I mean" (أَعْنِي). It may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with «أُولَئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَاتٌ» as its khabar (predicate); and إِذَا together with its apodosis (jawāb) is the ṣila (relative clause) of الَّذِينَ.
(إِنَّا لِلَّهِ): the majority pronounce the alif in إِنَّا with full (tafkhīm) articulation, and some have pronounced it with imāla (inclination toward i) because of how frequently this phrase is uttered. This is not according to analogy, because the alif belongs to the pronoun «نَا», and it is neither changed [from another letter] nor treated as changed.

ukberi-tibyan:157-157.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أُولَئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَاتٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَرَحْمَةٌ وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُهْتَدُونَ (١٥٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أُولَئِكَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject). And (صَلَوَاتٌ) is a second mubtadaʾ, and (عَلَيْهِمْ) is the khabar (predicate) of the second mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of أُولَئِكَ. It is also possible to make صَلَوَاتٌ nominative by the preposition phrase [as its fāʿil (agent)], because [the phrase] has been strengthened by occurring as a khabar; like it is (أُولَئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ). (وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُهْتَدُونَ): هُمْ is a mubtadaʾ, or tawkīd (emphasis), or a separating pronoun (faṣl).

ukberi-tibyan:158-158.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةَ مِنْ شَعَائِرِ اللَّهِ فَمَنْ حَجَّ الْبَيْتَ أَوِ اعْتَمَرَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَا وَمَنْ تَطَوَّعَ خَيْرًا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ (١٥٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّ الصَّفَا): the alif of الصَّفَا is substituted for a wāw, as shown by their saying in its dual صَفَوَانِ. And (مِنْ شَعَائِرِ) is the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ. There is an omitted muḍāf in the speech, its implied form being: "the circumambulation of al-Ṣafā" or "the running of al-Ṣafā". الشَّعَائِرُ is the plural of شَعِيرَةٌ, like صَحِيفَةٌ and صَحَائِفُ, and the best is to pronounce it with hamza, because the yāʾ is additional.
(فَمَنْ): in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); it is conditional, and the apodosis (jawāb) is (فَلَا جُنَاحَ).
They differed about where the statement is complete here. It is said that the statement is complete at فَلَا جُنَاحَ, and then one begins and says «عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَطَّوَّفَ» ("it is upon him to go round"), because going round is obligatory; on this view the khabar of «لَا» is omitted, i.e. "there is no sin in the ḥajj". The best on this view is for عَلَيْهِ to be a khabar and أَنْ يَطَّوَّفَ a mubtadaʾ.
It is weak to make it an incitement (ighrāʾ), because incitement has come only with the second person. Sībawayh reported from some of them: عَلَيْهِ رِجَلًا لَيْسَنِي ("let him take a man other than me").
He said: it is irregular (shādhdh) and is not taken as a basis for analogy. The original is أَنْ يَتَطَوَّفَ, and the tāʾ was changed to ṭāʾ.
Ibn ʿAbbās read أَنْ يَطَّافَ; its original is أَنْ يَتَطَافَ, and it is yaftaʿil from الطَّوَاف.
Others said: the pause is at «بِهِمَا», and عَلَيْهِ is the khabar of لَا; the implied form on this view is: "there is no sin upon him in going round (فِي أَنْ يَطَّوَفَ)". When فِي was omitted, أَنْ was placed in the position of the accusative, while according to al-Khalīl it is in the position of the genitive. And it is said [Translator's note: the source reads وَقَبْلَ, evidently for وَقِيلَ] that the implied form is: "there is no sin upon him if he does not go round them" (أَنْ لَا يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَا), because the Companions used to refrain from going round them on account of the idols that were upon them; whoever says this does not need to imply لَا.
(وَمَنْ تَطَوَّعَ): it is read in the form of the past verb; on this reading مَنْ may mean "the one who" (الَّذِي), with the khabar being «فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ» and the referent pronoun omitted, its implied form being "for him". It may also be that «مَنْ» is conditional, with the past in the sense of the future.
It was also read «يَطَّوَّعْ» in the form of the imperfect; on this reading مَنْ is conditional and nothing else, because it has made [the verb] jussive, and the tāʾ has been assimilated into the ṭāʾ. And (خَيْرًا) is accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the implied form is "with good" (بِخَيْرٍ), and when the preposition was omitted the verb reached it directly. It may also be an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a good voluntary act".
If you make مَنْ conditional, there is no omission of a pronoun in the speech, because the pronoun of مَنْ is in يَطَّوَّعْ.

ukberi-tibyan:159-159.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْتُمُونَ مَا أَنْزَلْنَا مِنَ الْبَيِّنَاتِ وَالْهُدَى مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا بَيَّنَّاهُ لِلنَّاسِ فِي الْكِتَابِ أُولَئِكَ يَلْعَنُهُمُ اللَّهُ وَيَلْعَنُهُمُ اللَّاعِنُونَ (١٥٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنَ الْبَيِّنَاتِ): «مِنَ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَا» or from the omitted referent pronoun, since the original is مَا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ. It may also be attached to (أَنْزَلْنَا), as being a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (مِنْ بَعْدِ): مِنْ is attached to (يَكْتُمُونَ), and it is not attached to (أَنْزَلْنَا), because the meaning would be corrupted: the sending down was not after the making clear; only the concealing was after the making clear.
(فِي الْكِتَابِ): فِي is attached to (بَيَّنَّا), and so is the lām; it is not prohibited for the two prepositions to be attached to it, because their meanings differ. It is also possible for «فِي» to be a ḥāl, i.e. "being in the Book". (أُولَئِكَ يَلْعَنُهُمُ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of the khabar of إِنَّ. (وَيَلْعَنُهُمُ): it may be conjoined to the first «يَلْعَنُهُمْ», and it may be resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:160-160.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا وَأَصْلَحُوا وَبَيَّنُوا. . . . (١٦٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا): a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil), in the position of the accusative; that from which the exception is made is the pronoun in يَلْعَنُهُمْ. It is also said that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), because those who concealed were cursed before they repented, and the exception came only to make clear that repentance is accepted, not because a group of those who concealed were not cursed.

ukberi-tibyan:161-161.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَمَاتُوا وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ أُولَئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ (١٦١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أُولَئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ): we have mentioned it at His saying (أُولَئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَاتٌ). Al-Ḥasan read (وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ وَالنَّاسُ أَجْمَعُونَ) in the nominative; it is conjoined to the position of the name of Allah, because it is in the position of the nominative, since the implied form is: "those — upon them is that Allah curses them", because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in construct with its agent.

ukberi-tibyan:162-162.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا لَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمُ الْعَذَابُ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ (١٦٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ and mīm in عَلَيْهِمْ.
(لَا يُخَفَّفُ): a ḥāl from the pronoun in خَالِدِينَ; it is not a second ḥāl from the hāʾ and mīm, for the reason we have mentioned in more than one place: that a single noun does not have two ḥāls in the accusative. It may also be resumptive, having no grammatical position.

ukberi-tibyan:163-163.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِلَهُكُمْ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الرَّحْمَنُ الرَّحِيمُ (١٦٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ): إِلَهٌ is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), and وَاحِدٌ is an adjective (ṣifa) of it.
The point here is the adjective, since had He said "and your God is one" (وَإِلَهُكُمْ وَاحِدٌ), that would have been what is intended; but mentioning it [i.e. إِلَهٌ] adds emphasis. This resembles the preparatory ḥāl (al-ḥāl al-muwaṭṭiʾa), as when you say مَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ رَجُلًا صَالِحًا ("I passed by Zayd, a righteous man"), and as when you say in the khabar: زَيْدٌ شَخْصٌ صَالِحٌ ("Zayd is a righteous person"). (إِلَّا هُوَ): the excepted is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) for the position of لَا إِلَهَ, because the position of لَا together with what it governs is nominative as a mubtadaʾ; had the position of the excepted been accusative, it would have been إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ.
And (الرَّحْمَنُ) is a badal for هُوَ, or the khabar of a mubtadaʾ. It is not permissible for it to be an adjective of هُوَ, because a pronoun is not qualified by an adjective; nor can it be a khabar of هُوَ, because the excepted here is not a clause.

ukberi-tibyan:62-62.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَالَّذِينَ هَادُوا وَالنَّصَارَى وَالصَّابِئِينَ مَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (٦٣)). [Translator's note: the verse number is printed as ٦٣ in the source; this is verse 62.]
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالصَّابِئِينَ): it is read with the hamza, according to the original form, and it is from صبأ يصبأ, when one inclines [away]. It is also read without hamza, by changing the hamza into alif in صبا and into yāʾ in صابي; and when it was changed into yāʾ, it was omitted because of the yāʾ of the plural.
The alif in هادوا is converted from a wāw, because it is from هاد يهود, when one repents; from this is His saying, Exalted is He: «إِنَّا هُدْنَا إِلَيْكَ». It is also said to be from الهوادة, which is submission; and it is said that its origin is yāʾ, from هاد يهيد, when something moves. In من آمن, من here is conditional, in the position of a mubtadaʾ (subject); the khabar (predicate) is آمن, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is: فلهم أجرهم; the clause is the khabar of إنّ الذين, and the referring pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, its implied form being: "whoever of them believes".
It may also be that من is in the sense of الذي, not causing the jussive, and is a badal (substitute) from the noun of إنّ, the referring pronoun being omitted as well, and the khabar of إنّ is: فلهم أجرهم.
[The pronoun] is construed according to the form of من in آمن and عمل, so the pronoun is singular, and according to its meaning in «فلهم أجرهم», so it is plural. And (أَجْرُهُمْ) is a mubtadaʾ and لهم is its khabar; according to al-Akhfash, أجرهم is nominative by the preposition [phrase]. And (عِنْدَ) is an adverbial (ẓarf), its operator being the meaning of istiqrār ("being settled").
It may also be that عند is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الأجر, its implied form being: "they have their reward, established with «their Lord»". الأجر is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun): one says أجره الله يأجره أجرا ("Allah rewarded him"); and it may be in the sense of the object, because the reward is the thing with which the obedient one is recompensed, so it is what he is rewarded with.

ukberi-tibyan:63-63.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَكُمْ وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ الطُّورَ خُذُوا مَا آتَيْنَاكُمْ بِقُوَّةٍ وَاذْكُرُوا مَا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ (٦٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَوْقَكُمُ): an adverbial (ẓarf) of رفعنا. It is weak for it to be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الطور, because the implied form would become "We raised the mountain, being high", and this is already understood from رفعنا; and because the mountain was not above them at the time of raising, but only became above them by the raising. (خُذُوا مَا آتَيْنَاكُمْ): the implied form is: "and We said: take…". The omitted saying may also be a ḥāl, the implied form being: "We raised the mountain above you, saying: take…".
(بِقُوَّةٍ): in the position of the accusative as an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara); the implied form is: "take what We have given you, resolved to be earnest in acting upon it"; the one to whom the ḥāl refers is the wāw in خذوا.
It may also be a ḥāl from the omitted pronoun; the implied form is: "take what We have given you, while it contains firmness and strictness in the injunction to act upon it".

ukberi-tibyan:64-64.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ فَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ لَكُنْتُمْ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ (٦٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَلَوْلَا): it is compounded of لو and لا. Before compounding, لو is that by which a thing is precluded because of the preclusion of something else, and لا is for negation, and preclusion is negation in meaning. So the negation by لا has entered upon one of the two preclusions of لو — and preclusion is negation in meaning — and negation, when it enters upon negation, becomes affirmation. Hence the meaning of this لولا became: that by which a thing is precluded because of the existence of something else.
And (فَضْلُ اللَّهِ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: "were it not that the grace of Allah is present". The omission of the khabar is obligatory because it is known and because the speech is lengthened by the answer of لولا. If أنّ occurs after لولا, the khabar appears, as in His saying, Exalted is He: (فَلَوْلَا أَنَّهُ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُسَبِّحِينَ), for the khabar is overt [there] for أنّ. [Translator's note: the sentence «فالخبر في اللفظ لأنّ» appears truncated in the source; translated as given.]
The Kufans held that the noun occurring after this لولا is the agent of لولا.

ukberi-tibyan:65-65.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ الَّذِينَ اعْتَدَوْا مِنْكُمْ فِي السَّبْتِ فَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ كُونُوا قِرَدَةً خَاسِئِينَ (٦٥)).
His saying: (عَلِمْتُمُ الَّذِينَ اعْتَدَوْا): علمتم here is in the sense of عرفتم ("you knew/recognized"), so it takes one object. And (مِنْكُمْ) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الذين اعتدوا, i.e. "the transgressors, being from among you". And (فِي السَّبْتِ) is attached to (اعتدوا). السبت is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun): one says سبت يسبت سبتا, when one cuts off; then the day was named سبت. One may also say يوم السبت, so that it comes out as a maṣdar according to its original state; and they have said اليومَ السبتُ ("today is the Sabbath"), making اليوم a predicate of السبت, as one says اليومَ القتالُ ("today is the fighting"). So according to what we have mentioned, there is an omission in the speech, its implied form being: "on the day of the Sabbath". (خَاسِئِينَ): the verb from it is خسأ, when one is abased; it is intransitive, the reflexive counterpart (muṭāwiʿ) of خسأته ("I drove him away"); so its intransitive and transitive forms have one wording, like زاد الشيء وزدته ("the thing increased, and I increased it") and غاض الماء وغضته ("the water subsided, and I made it subside").
It is an adjective of قردة; it may also be a second khabar (predicate), or a ḥāl from the agent of كان, the operator in it being كان.

ukberi-tibyan:66-66.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَجَعَلْنَاهَا نَكَالًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا وَمَا خَلْفَهَا وَمَوْعِظَةً لِلْمُتَّقِينَ (٦٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَجَعَلْنَاهَا): the pronoun refers to the punishment, or the transformation, or the community. And (نَكَالًا) is a second object.

ukberi-tibyan:67-67.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَى لِقَوْمِهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَنْ تَذْبَحُوا بَقَرَةً قَالُوا أَتَتَّخِذُنَا هُزُوًا قَالَ أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ الْجَاهِلِينَ (٦٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَأْمُرُكُمْ): the majority read it with ḍamma on the rāʾ, and it has been read with it made quiescent, because the kāf is vowelled and there is a vowel before the rāʾ, so they made the middle one quiescent, likening it to عضُد, and treated what is separate as if it were joined. Some pronounce the vowel very briefly (ikhtilās) and do not make it quiescent. The good [practice] is to pronounce its hamza.
It has been read with alif, by changing the hamza into alif because it is quiescent and preceded by fatḥa; similar to it are الراس and الباس. (أَنْ تَذْبَحُوا): in the position of the accusative on the assumption that the preposition has been dropped, its implied form being بأن تذبحوا; according to the view of al-Khalīl it is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ.
It is also possible for al-Khalīl to say that here it is in the position of the accusative, أمرت being made transitive by itself, as [the poet] said: أمرتك الخيرَ فافعل ("I commanded you [to do] good, so do it"). (هُزُوًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it has three dialectal forms: with hamza and ḍamma on the zāy; with hamza and the zāy quiescent; and with the hamza changed into wāw and ḍamma on the zāy; and sometimes the zāy is also made quiescent.
It is the second object of اتّخذ, and there is an omitted muḍāf in it, its implied form being: "do you take us as objects of mockery?" (dhawī huzuʾ).
It may also be a maṣdar in the sense of the passive participle, its implied form being: "mocked at".
The answer to the question, in meaning, is: «أعوذ بالله أن أكون», because the meaning is that the one who mocks is ignorant; as if he said: "I do not mock".

ukberi-tibyan:102-102.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاتَّبَعُوا مَا تَتْلُو الشَّيَاطِينُ عَلَى مُلْكِ سُلَيْمَانَ وَمَا كَفَرَ سُلَيْمَانُ وَلَكِنَّ الشَّيَاطِينَ كَفَرُوا يُعَلِّمُونَ النَّاسَ السِّحْرَ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَى الْمَلَكَيْنِ بِبَابِلَ هَارُوتَ وَمَارُوتَ وَمَا يُعَلِّمَانِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ حَتَّى يَقُولَا إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ فِتْنَةٌ فَلَا تَكْفُرْ فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مِنْهُمَا مَا يُفَرِّقُونَ بِهِ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَزَوْجِهِ وَمَا هُمْ بِضَارِّينَ بِهِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مَا يَضُرُّهُمْ وَلَا يَنْفَعُهُمْ وَلَقَدْ عَلِمُوا لَمَنِ اشْتَرَاهُ مَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَاقٍ وَلَبِئْسَ مَا شَرَوْا بِهِ أَنْفُسَهُمْ لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ (١٠٢)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَاتَّبَعُوا): it is conjoined to «وَأُشْرِبُوا», or to «نَبَذَهُ فَرِيقٌ».
(تَتْلُو): in the sense of تَلَتْ ("recited"). (عَلَى مُلْكِ): i.e. "in the time of the kingship"; the muḍāf was omitted, and the meaning is "in the time of".
And (سُلَيْمَانَ) is a diptote, and there are three causes in it: foreignness, definiteness, and the alif and nūn. He repeated its mention as an overt noun for magnification; this is likewise done with proper names and with generic nouns too, as in the saying of the poet:
لَا أَرَى الْمَوْتَ يَسْبِقُ الْمَوْتَ شَيْءٌ ... بَغَّضَ الْمَوْتُ ذَا الْغِنَى وَالْفَقِيرَا
("I see nothing that outstrips death; death has made the rich and the poor alike hate [it]")
(وَلَكِنَّ الشَّيَاطِينَ): it is read with a doubled nūn and the noun in the accusative.
It is read with it light, and the noun in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), because it has become one of the particles that begin a nominal clause.
Al-Ḥasan read: ((الشَّيَاطُونَ)), which is like an error; in it he likened the yāʾ before the nūn to the yāʾ of the sound plural.
(يُعَلِّمُونَ النَّاسَ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in كَفَرُوا. Some allowed it to be a ḥāl from الشَّيَاطِينَ, but that is nothing, because لَكِنْ does not govern a ḥāl.
(وَمَا أُنْزِلَ): «مَا» means "that which", and it is in the position of the accusative by conjunction with السِّحْرَ, i.e. "and they teach that which was sent down". It is also said that it is conjoined to تَتْلُو. It is also said that «مَا» is in the position of the genitive by conjunction with مُلْكِ سُلَيْمَانَ, i.e. "and in the era of that which was sent down upon the two angels".
It is also said that مَا is negating, i.e. "sorcery was not sent down upon the two angels", or "the permission of sorcery was not sent down". The majority read with a fatḥa on the lām of الْمَلَكَيْنِ, and it was read with a kasra [i.e. الْمَلِكَيْنِ, "the two kings"].
And (هَارُوتَ وَمَارُوتَ) are two badals (substitutes) of الْمَلَكَيْنِ.
It is also said that they are two tribes of the devils; on this view they are not badals of الْمَلَكَيْنِ, and that only fits, under one of the two views, the reading of those who put a kasra on the lām.
