(بِبَابِلَ): it may be an adverbial (ẓarf) of أُنْزِلَ. It may also be a ḥāl from الْمَلَكَيْنِ, or from the pronoun in أُنْزِلَ.
(حَتَّى يَقُولَا): i.e. "until they say", and the meaning is that they refrain from teaching sorcery until they say (إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ فِتْنَةٌ). It is also said that حَتَّى means إِلَّا ("except"), i.e. "and they do not teach anyone except that they say".
And (أَحَدٍ) here may be the one used for generality, as when you say: "there is no one in the house (مَا بِالدَّارِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ)"; it may also here mean "one" or "a person". (فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مِنْهُمَا): it is conjoined to يُعَلِّمَانِ and does not come within the negation, because the negation there reverts to affirmation, since the meaning is: "they teach people sorcery after their saying ((نَحْنُ فِتْنَةٌ))", ((فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ)). It is also said that the implied form is: "so they come and learn".
((وَمِنْهُمَا)): the pronoun of the two angels; it may also be the pronoun of sorcery and of what was sent down upon the two angels.
It is also said that it is conjoined to يُعَلِّمُونَ النَّاسَ السِّحْرَ, so that on this view مِنْهُمَا refers to the sorcery and what was sent down upon the two angels, or is the pronoun of the two tribes of devils. It is also said that it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf). It could not be made accusative as the answer to the prohibition, because the meaning is not "if you disbelieve, they will learn". (مَا يُفَرِّقُونَ): «مَا» may mean "that which", and may be an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa); it cannot be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), because the pronoun in «بِهِ» returns to «مَا», and no pronoun returns to the maṣdariyya.
(بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ): the majority keep the hamza after the rāʾ. It was read with a doubled rāʾ without hamza [i.e. الْمَرِّ]; its justification is that he cast the vowel of the hamza onto the rāʾ, then intended a pause on it doubled, as they said: هَذَا خَالِدٌّ [i.e. with the doubled pause-form], and then they treated continuous speech as pause.
His saying, the Exalted: (إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl — from the agent if you wish, or from the object if you wish — the implied form being: "and they do not harm anyone with sorcery except that Allah knows of it"; or the implied form is: "except joined with Allah's permission". (وَلَا يَنْفَعُهُمْ): it is conjoined to the verb before it, and «لَا» entered for negation. It may also be resumptive, i.e. "while it does not benefit them", so that it is a ḥāl. It is not correct to conjoin it to مَا, because a verb is not conjoined to a noun.
(لَمَنِ اشْتَرَاهُ): the lām here is the one that prepares the way for an oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam), like the one in His saying: ((لَئِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهِ الْمُنَافِقُونَ)). And (مَنْ) is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and it is conditional; the answer of the oath is (مَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَاقٍ). It is also said that (مَنْ) means "the one who". On both views the position of the clause is the accusative, governed by (عَلِمُوا); and «عَلِمُوا» does not govern the wording of «مَنْ», because the condition and the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ) have the head of the sentence.
(وَلَبِئْسَ مَا): the answer of an omitted oath. (لَوْ كَانُوا): the answer of لَوْ is omitted, its implied form being: "if they had benefited from their knowledge, they would have refrained from buying sorcery".

ukberi-tibyan:103-103.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ آمَنُوا وَاتَّقَوْا لَمَثُوبَةٌ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ (١٠٣)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ آمَنُوا): أَنَّ with what it governs is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the nominative, governed by an omitted verb, because «لَوْ» requires a verb; its implied form is "if it had occurred from them that they believed", i.e. their belief. It does not put the verb in the jussive by لَوْ, because لَوْ connects a past verb with a past verb, and the condition is contrary to that.
(لَمَثُوبَةٌ): the answer of لَوْ. مَثُوبَةٌ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ» is its adjective, and «خَيْرٌ» is its khabar (predicate).
It was also read مَثْوَبَةٌ, with a sukūn on the thāʾ and a fatḥa on the wāw; they made it analogous to the sound forms among its parallels, such as مَقْتَلَةٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:104-104.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَقُولُوا رَاعِنَا . . . . . . . . (١٠٤)).
His saying, the Exalted: (رَاعِنَا): an imperative verb, and the position of the clause is the accusative, governed by (تَقُولُوا).
It was read anomalously (shādhdh) «رَاعِنًا» with tanwīn, i.e. "do not say a foolish saying (قَوْلًا رَاعِنًا)".

ukberi-tibyan:236-236.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِنْ طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ مَا لَمْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ أَوْ تَفْرِضُوا لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً وَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ عَلَى الْمُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُ وَعَلَى الْمُقْتِرِ قَدَرُهُ مَتَاعًا بِالْمَعْرُوفِ حَقًّا عَلَى الْمُحْسِنِينَ (٢٣٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا لَمْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ): (مَا) is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and the time with it is omitted, its implied form being: "in the time of leaving off touching them".
It has also been said: مَا is conditional, i.e. "if you have not touched them". (تَمَسُّوهُنَّ) is read with fatḥa on the tāʾ and without an alif, on the basis that the act belongs to the men.
It is also read «تُمَاسُّوهُنَّ» with ḍamma on the tāʾ and an alif after the mīm; this is from the pattern of mufāʿala (reciprocity). It may carry the meaning of the first reading, and it may be on the basis of attributing the act to both the men and the women, like mujāmaʿa (intercourse) and mubāshara (contact); for the act is from the man, and the yielding is from the woman, as is the inviting as well, and from this she is called zāniya (adulteress). (فَرِيضَةً): it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), or it may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and this is the better view; faʿīla here has the sense of mafʿūla (passive participle), and the described noun is omitted, its implied form being: "a prescribed provision (mutʿa mafrūḍa)". (وَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ): conjoined to an omitted verb, its implied form being: "so divorce them and provide for them". (عَلَى الْمُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُ): the majority read it in the nominative, and the clause is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent), its implied sense being: "according to the measure of capacity". In the clause there is an omission, its implied form being: "upon the affluent among you". The clause may also be resumptive, having no grammatical position.
(قَدَرَهُ) is also read in the accusative, and it is an object according to the meaning, because the meaning of «مَتِّعُوهُنَّ» is: let each of you render the measure of his capacity. Better than this is that the implied form be: "so impose upon the affluent his measure". Qadar and qadr are two dialectal forms, and it has been read with both. It has also been said: qadr with sukūn is capacity, and with the vowel (qadar) it is the amount.
(مَتَاعًا): a noun of the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar); the maṣdar is tamtīʿ, and the ism al-maṣdar is treated like it.
(حَقًّا): a maṣdar of "ḥaqqa dhālika ḥaqqan" (that was due, truly). And (عَلَى) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) what puts the maṣdar in the accusative.

ukberi-tibyan:237-237.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِنْ طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ وَقَدْ فَرَضْتُمْ لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً فَنِصْفُ مَا فَرَضْتُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ يَعْفُونَ أَوْ يَعْفُوَ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ عُقْدَةُ النِّكَاحِ وَأَنْ تَعْفُوا أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَى وَلَا تَنْسَوُا الْفَضْلَ بَيْنَكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ (٢٣٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَقَدْ فَرَضْتُمْ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). (فَنِصْفُ): i.e. "then upon you is half", or "then what is obligatory is half".
Had it been read in the accusative, its explanation would be: "then render half of what you prescribed".
(إِلَّا أَنْ يَعْفُونَ): أَنْ and the verb are in the position of the accusative, and the implied sense is: "then upon you is half of what you prescribed, except in the state of pardoning". Its like has preceded, at greater length than this, in His saying «إِلَّا أَنْ يَخَافَا».
The nūn in «يَعْفُونَ» is the pronoun of the group of women, and the wāw before it is the final radical (lām) of the word, because the verb here is indeclinable (mabnī); so it is like yakhrujna and yaqʿudna. As for your saying "al-rijālu yaʿfūna" (the men pardon), it is like "al-nisāʾu yaʿfūna" (the women pardon) in wording, but differs from it in underlying form: "al-rijālu yaʿfūna" is originally yaʿfuwūna, like yakhrujūna; the wāw that is the final radical of the verb was dropped, and the wāw of the pronoun remained, and the nūn is the sign of the nominative. In your saying "al-nisāʾu yaʿfūna", nothing has been dropped from it, as we have explained. (وَأَنْ تَعْفُوا): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (أَقْرَبُ) is its khabar (predicate), and (لِلتَّقْوَى) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أَقْرَبُ.
Outside the Quran, "aqrabu mina al-taqwā" and "aqrabu ilā al-taqwā" are permissible, except that the lām here indicates a meaning other than the meaning of ilā and other than the meaning of min. The meaning of the lām is: pardoning is nearer for the sake of piety; so the lām indicates the cause of the nearness of pardoning. If you say "aqrabu ilā al-taqwā", the meaning would be "close to piety", as you say "you are nearer to me (aqrabu ilayya)". And "aqrabu mina al-taqwā" would require that pardoning and piety both be near, but pardoning be more intensely near than piety. The meaning of the verse is not according to this, but according to the meaning of the lām.
The tāʾ of al-taqwā is substituted for a wāw, and its wāw is substituted for a yāʾ, because it is from waqaytu (I guarded).
(وَلَا تَنْسَوُا الْفَضْلَ): in «وَلَا تَنْسَوْا» there are readings, and their explanation is what we mentioned in «اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلَالَةَ».
(بَيْنَكُمْ): an adverb (ẓarf) of تَنْسَوْا, or a ḥāl of الْفَضْلَ. It has also been read «وَلَا تَنْسَوُا الْفَضْلَ» on the pattern of mufāʿala, and it is in the sense of mutāraka (mutually leaving off), not in the sense of forgetfulness. «[Translator's note: the text as given prints this variant identically to the standard reading; the mufāʿala variant intended is presumably «وَلَا تَنَاسَوُا».]»

ukberi-tibyan:238-238.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (حَافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ وَالصَّلَاةِ الْوُسْطَى وَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قَانِتِينَ (٢٣٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حَافِظُوا): it may be from the mufāʿala that occurs from one party, like "ʿāqabtu al-liṣṣa" (I punished the thief) and "ʿāfāhu Allāhu" (Allah granted him well-being); or it may be from the mufāʿala that occurs from two parties, the obligation of repeated guarding being treated like an agent, since the obligation urges toward the act; so it is as if it were a partner of the guarding agent, just as they said regarding His saying (وَإِذْ وَاعَدْنَا مُوسَى): the promise was from Allah and the acceptance from Moses, and the acceptance was made like the promise.
In حَافِظُوا there is a meaning not found in iḥfaẓū; namely, repetition of guarding. «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «لَا يَجُودُ»; presumably «لَا يُوجَدُ» (not found) is intended, and it is translated accordingly.]»
(وَالصَّلَاةِ الْوُسْطَى): it is singled out for mention, even though it is included in the prayers, to show its superiority.
Al-wusṭā is fuʿlā from al-wasaṭ (the middle). (لِلَّهِ): the lām may be attached to قُومُوا, or, if you wish, to «قَانِتِينَ».

ukberi-tibyan:239-239.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ فَرِجَالًا أَوْ رُكْبَانًا فَإِذَا أَمِنْتُمْ فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَمَا عَلَّمَكُمْ مَا لَمْ تَكُونُوا تَعْلَمُونَ (٢٣٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَرِجَالًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) of something omitted, its implied form being: "then pray on foot (rijālan)", or "then stand on foot". Rijālan is the plural of rājil (one on foot), like ṣāḥib and ṣiḥāb; and it has many plurals which this is not the place to mention. (كَمَا عَلَّمَكُمْ): in the position of the accusative, i.e. "a remembrance like what He taught you".
Its like has preceded in His saying (كَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا) and in His saying (وَاذْكُرُوهُ كَمَا هَدَاكُمْ).

ukberi-tibyan:240-240.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَالَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنْكُمْ وَيَذَرُونَ أَزْوَاجًا وَصِيَّةً لِأَزْوَاجِهِمْ مَتَاعًا إِلَى الْحَوْلِ غَيْرَ إِخْرَاجٍ فَإِنْ خَرَجْنَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي مَا فَعَلْنَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِنَّ مِنْ مَعْرُوفٍ وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ (٢٤٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنْكُمْ): الَّذِينَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: "they bequeath a bequest"; this is according to the reading of those who put «وَصِيَّةً» in the accusative. For those who read الْوَصِيَّة in the nominative, the implied form is: "and upon them is a bequest", and the implied «عَلَيْهِمُ» is a khabar for وَصِيَّة.
And (لِأَزْوَاجِهِمْ) is a naʿt (adjective) of the bequest. It has also been said: it is the khabar of the bequest, and «عَلَيْهِمْ» is a second khabar or a clarification (tabyīn).
It has also been said: الَّذِينَ is the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb, its implied form being: "let those who are taken in death bequeath a bequest"; this is according to the reading of those who put وَصِيَّةً in the accusative. (مَتَاعًا إِلَى الْحَوْلِ): a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the bequest indicates "they bequeath", and "they bequeath" has the sense of "they provide". It may also be a badal (substitute) of the bequest according to the reading of those who put it in the accusative, or an adjective of وَصِيَّة.
And إِلَى الْحَوْلِ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) مَتَاع, or is an adjective of it. It has also been said: مَتَاعًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "providing" or "possessors of provision".
(غَيْرَ إِخْرَاجٍ): غَيْرَ here is in the accusative the way a maṣdar is, according to al-Akhfash, its implied form being: "not an expulsion". Someone else said: it is a ḥāl. It has also been said: it is an adjective of مَتَاع. And it has been said: the implied form is "without (min ghayri) expulsion".

ukberi-tibyan:241-241.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلِلْمُطَلَّقَاتِ مَتَاعٌ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ حَقًّا عَلَى الْمُتَّقِينَ (٢٤١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلِلْمُطَلَّقَاتِ مَتَاعٌ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).
And (حَقًّا) is a maṣdar (verbal noun). Its like has been mentioned before.

ukberi-tibyan:242-242.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (كَذَلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ آيَاتِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ (٢٤٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَذَلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ): it has been discussed in the verse on fasting.

ukberi-tibyan:243-243.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا مِنْ دِيَارِهِمْ وَهُمْ أُلُوفٌ حَذَرَ الْمَوْتِ فَقَالَ لَهُمُ اللَّهُ مُوتُوا ثُمَّ أَحْيَاهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ (٢٤٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ): the original of tarā is tarʾā, like tarʿā, except that the Arabs agreed on dropping the hamza in the imperfect for lightening; it is not taken as a model for analogy, and it sometimes occurs in its original form under poetic necessity. When the hamza was dropped, the end of the verb remained an alif, so it was dropped in the jussive; the alif is converted from a yāʾ. As for the past tense, the hamza is not dropped.
It is made transitive here with ilā only because its meaning is "has your knowledge not reached such-and-such?"; seeing here is in the sense of knowing. The hamza in «أَلَمِ» is interrogative, and when interrogation enters upon a negation it becomes an affirmation and a confirmation (taqrīr), and neither the interrogation nor the negation remains in the meaning. (ثُمَّ أَحْيَاهُمْ): conjoined to an omitted verb, its implied form being: "so they died, then He gave them life".
It has also been said: the meaning of the imperative here is a statement, because His saying «فَقَالَ لَهُمُ اللَّهُ مُوتُوا» means "so He caused them to die", so the conjoining is according to the meaning.
The alif of أَحْيَا is converted from a yāʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:244-244.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَاتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ (٢٤٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَقَاتِلُوا): what it is conjoined to is omitted, its implied form being: "so obey and fight", or "so do not be wary of death as those before them were wary of it, and the wariness did not benefit them".

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فِيهِ ظُلُمَاتٌ وَرَعْدٌ وَبَرْقٌ يَجْعَلُونَ أَصَابِعَهُمْ فِي آذَانِهِمْ مِنَ الصَّوَاعِقِ حَذَرَ الْمَوْتِ وَاللَّهُ مُحِيطٌ بِالْكَافِرِينَ (١٩)).
His saying, the Exalted: (أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ): there are four views on «أَوْ». First: it is for doubt, and the doubt goes back to the one observing the state of the hypocrites: he does not know whether to liken them to the one who kindled a fire or to the people caught in the rainstorm; as in His saying (إِلَى مِائَةِ أَلْفٍ أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ), i.e. whoever sees them is in doubt about the size of their number. Second: it is for choice, i.e. liken them to whichever of the two groups you wish. Third: it is for permission. Fourth: it is for vagueness, i.e. some people liken them to the one who kindled a fire and some to the people of the rainstorm; and its like is His saying, the Exalted: (كُونُوا هُودًا أَوْ نَصَارَى), i.e. the Jews said "be Jews" and the Christians said "be Christians". According to most of the Basrans, «أَوْ» may not be taken in the sense of the wāw or of «بَلْ» so long as there is an alternative to that. The kāf is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the kāf in His saying (كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي).
It may also be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "or their likeness is as the likeness of a rainstorm".
There is an omission in the phrase, its implied form being "or like the people of a rainstorm", and to this omitted element the pronoun in His saying يَجْعَلُونَ refers back. The meaning requires this, because the hypocrites are likened to people struck by rain in which there is darkness, thunder and lightning, not to the rain itself. The original form of «صَيِّبٍ» is صَيْوِبٌ on the pattern fayʿil; the wāw was replaced by yāʾ and the first [yāʾ] was assimilated into it; its like is مَيِّتٌ and هَيِّنٌ. The Kufans said: its original form is صَوِيبٌ on the pattern faʿīl; this is a mistake, because if it were so the wāw would have remained sound, as it remained sound in طَوِيلٌ and عَوِيلٌ.
(مِنَ السَّمَاءِ) is in the position of the accusative, and (مِنْ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to صَيِّبٍ, because the implied wording is "like rain pouring (صَيِّبٍ) from the sky", and this descriptive word governs as the verb does; مِنْ is for the beginning of the extent.
It may also be in the position of the genitive as an adjective of صَيِّبٍ, in which case مِنْ is attached to something omitted, i.e. "like a rainstorm existing from the sky".
The hamza in السَّمَاءِ is a substitute for a wāw, turned into hamza because it occurs at the end of the word after an extra alif; its counterparts are judged by analogy with it. (فِيهِ ظُلُمَاتٌ): the hāʾ refers back to صَيِّبٍ, and ظُلُمَاتٌ is put in the nominative by the preposition and its genitive noun, because it has been strengthened by being an adjective of صَيِّبٍ. ظُلُمَاتٌ may also be a mubtadaʾ with فِيهِ a khabar placed first; on this view there is a pronoun in فِيهِ, and the clause is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of صَيِّبٍ. The majority read it with ḍamma on the lām; it has been read with the lām quiescent for lightness; and there is another dialectal form with fatḥa on the lām.
الرَّعْدُ is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of رَعَدَ يَرْعُدُ [Translator's note: the text vocalises it «رَعِدَ يَرْعَدُ»], and الْبَرْقُ is a maṣdar too; on this view both are singular here. الرَّعْدُ and الْبَرْقُ may also have the meaning of الرَّاعِدُ ("the thundering") and الْبَارِقُ ("the flashing"), as in their saying رَجُلٌ عَدْلٌ ("a just man") and صَوْمٌ ("a fasting man").
(يَجْعَلُونَ) may be in the position of the genitive as an adjective of أَصْحَابِ صَيِّبٍ, or it may be resumptive. It is also said that it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in فِيهِ, with the element referring back to the hāʾ omitted, its implied form being "from its thunderbolts"; this is far-fetched, because omitting the element referring back to the owner of the ḥāl is like omitting it from the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and Sībawayh counts that as irregular. (مِنَ الصَّوَاعِقِ), i.e. from the sound of the thunderbolts.
(حَذَرَ الْمَوْتِ) is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). It is also said to be a maṣdar, i.e. "with a fear like the fear of death".
The maṣdar here is put in a genitive construct with its direct object.
(مُحِيطٌ): its original form is مُحْوِطٌ, because it is from حَاطَ يَحُوطُ; the kasra of the wāw was transferred to the ḥāʾ, and the wāw turned into yāʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَكَادُ الْبَرْقُ يَخْطَفُ أَبْصَارَهُمْ كُلَّمَا أَضَاءَ لَهُمْ مَشَوْا فِيهِ وَإِذَا أَظْلَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ قَامُوا وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَذَهَبَ بِسَمْعِهِمْ وَأَبْصَارِهِمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (٢٠)).
His saying, the Exalted: (يَكَادُ) is a verb indicating that the occurrence of the verb after it is near; for that reason أَنْ does not enter on it [the following verb], because أَنْ makes the verb purely future. Its second radical is wāw; the original is يَكْوَدُ, like خَافَ يَخَافُ; and كُدْتُ with ḍamma on the kāf has been heard. When a particle of negation enters on it, it indicates that the verb after it did occur; and when there is no particle of negation, the verb after it did not occur but came near to occurring.
The position of (يَخْطَفُ) is accusative, because it is the khabar (predicate) of كَادَ; the meaning is "the lightning came near to snatching the sight".
The majority read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the ṭāʾ and sukūn on the khāʾ; its past tense is خَطِفَ, as in His saying, the Exalted: (إِلَّا مَنْ خَطِفَ الْخَطْفَةَ فَأَتْبَعَهُ شِهَابٌ). There are irregular (shādhdh) readings of it. First: kasra on the ṭāʾ (يَخْطِفُ), on the basis that its past tense is خَطَفَ with fatḥa on the ṭāʾ. Second: with fatḥa on the yāʾ, the khāʾ and the ṭāʾ, and the ṭāʾ doubled (يَخَطَّفُ); the original is يَخْتَطِفُ, and a ṭāʾ was substituted for the tāʾ [and assimilated], and the khāʾ was given the vowel of the tāʾ. Third: the same, except that it is with kasra on the ṭāʾ, according to what it deserves in the less common usage [Translator's note: so in the text]. Fourth: the same, except that it also has kasra on the khāʾ, by harmony (itbāʿ).
Fifth: with kasra on the yāʾ as well, also by harmony. Sixth: with fatḥa on the yāʾ, sukūn on the khāʾ and a doubled ṭāʾ; this is weak, because it combines two quiescent letters. (كُلَّمَا) here is an adverbial (ẓarf), and likewise in every place where it has an answer.
«مَا» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun) and the time-word is omitted, i.e. "every time of shining".
It is also said that «مَا» here is an indefinite noun described [by what follows], meaning "time", and the element referring back is omitted, i.e. "every time in which it shone for them". What governs كُلَّ is its answer. (فِيهِ), i.e. in its light; the meaning is "by its light". It may also be an adverbial in its original sense.
The meaning is that the light surrounds them.
(شَاءَ): its alif is converted from a yāʾ, because they say in its maṣdar شِئْتُ شَيْئًا; and they said شَيَّأْتُهُ, i.e. "I induced him to will". (لَذَهَبَ بِسَمْعِهِمْ), i.e. He would have done away with the faculty by which they hear. (وَعَلَى كُلِّ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «قَدِيرٌ» and is in the position of the accusative.

ukberi-tibyan:68-68.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّنْ لَنَا مَا هِيَ قَالَ إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لَا فَارِضٌ وَلَا بِكْرٌ عَوَانٌ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ فَافْعَلُوا مَا تُؤْمَرُونَ (٦٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَادْعُ لَنَا): the good dialect is ḍamma on the ʿayn; the wāw is omitted as a sign of indeclinability (bināʾ) according to the Basrans, and of the jussive according to the Kufans.
Among the Arabs there are some who give the ʿayn kasra; the rationale for it is that he regarded the ʿayn as quiescent, as if it were the end of the verb, then gave it kasra because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the dāl before it.
(مَا لَوْنُهَا): ما is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and لونها is the khabar (predicate); the clause is in the position of the accusative by (يبيّن). If it were read لونَها in the accusative, it would have a rationale, namely that you make ما redundant (zāʾida), as it is in His saying: (أَيَّمَا الْأَجَلَيْنِ قَضَيْتُ), and the implied form would be: "that He make clear to us its colour".
As for (مَا هِيَ), it is a mubtadaʾ and khabar and nothing else, since ما cannot be made redundant, because ((هي)) is not fit to be the object of يبيّن.
(لَا فَارِضٌ): an adjective of بقرة, and «لا» does not prevent that, because it entered for the meaning of negation; so it is like your saying: مررت برجل لا طويلٍ ولا قصيرٍ ("I passed by a man neither tall nor short"). If you wish, you may make it the khabar of a mubtadaʾ, i.e. "she is not old". (وَلَا بِكْرٌ) is like it, and likewise ((عوان)).
(بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ): i.e. "between the two"; since ((ذلك)) is suitable for the dual and the plural, it is permissible for ((بين)) to enter upon it, and it suffices. (مَا تُؤْمَرُونَ): i.e. "[what you are commanded] with", or "what you are commanded"; ما is in the sense of الذي, and it is weak for it to be an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, because the meaning is general, and it more closely resembles الذي.

ukberi-tibyan:69-69.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّنْ لَنَا مَا لَوْنُهَا قَالَ إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ صَفْرَاءُ فَاقِعٌ لَوْنُهَا تَسُرُّ النَّاظِرِينَ (٦٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَاقِعٌ لَوْنُهَا): if you wish, you may make ((فاقع)) an adjective with لونها nominative by it; and if you wish, it is a fronted khabar (predicate), and the clause is an adjective.
(تَسُرُّ) is also an adjective. It has also been said that ((فاقع)) is an adjective of البقرة, لونها is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and تسرّ is its khabar. اللون is treated as feminine for two reasons. First: that the colour here is yellowness, so it is construed according to the meaning. Second: that اللون is annexed to a feminine noun, so it is treated as feminine, as [the poet] said ذهبت بعض أصابعه ("some of his fingers went"), and (تَلْتَقِطْهُ بَعْضُ السَّيَّارَةِ).

ukberi-tibyan:70-70.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّنْ لَنَا مَا هِيَ إِنَّ الْبَقَرَ تَشَابَهَ عَلَيْنَا وَإِنَّا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَمُهْتَدُونَ (٧٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّ الْبَقَرَ): the majority read البقر without alif; it is the collective noun (jins) of بقرة. It was read irregularly (shādhdh) «إنّ الباقر», which is a quasi-plural (ism jamʿ) of بقرة; similar to it is الجامل ("herd of camels").
(تَشَابَهَ): the majority read it with the shīn undoubled and fatḥa on the hāʾ, because البقر is treated as masculine and the verb is past. It is read with ḍamma on the hāʾ with the undoubled [shīn], treating البقر as feminine, since it is like a plural.
It is also read with ḍamma on the hāʾ and doubling of the shīn; its original form is تتشابه, then the second tāʾ was changed to shīn and assimilated. It is also read likewise but with yāʾ, treating it as masculine.
(إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ): the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is إنّ and what it governs, according to Sībawayh; that is permissible because the condition is in the middle. The khabar (predicate) of إنّ is the apodosis in meaning, and it came after it, so the implied form becomes: "if Allah wills our guidance, we will be guided"; the object is omitted, namely هدايتنا ("our guidance").
Al-Mubarrad said: the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the clause, because the condition is parenthetical, so it is intended to come later; thus it becomes like your saying: أنت ظالم إن فعلت ("you are a wrongdoer if you do [it]").

ukberi-tibyan:71-71.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لَا ذَلُولٌ تُثِيرُ الْأَرْضَ وَلَا تَسْقِي الْحَرْثَ مُسَلَّمَةٌ لَا شِيَةَ فِيهَا قَالُوا الْآنَ جِئْتَ بِالْحَقِّ فَذَبَحُوهَا وَمَا كَادُوا يَفْعَلُونَ (٧١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا ذَلُولٌ): when فعول occurs as an adjective, the hāʾ of the feminine does not enter it; you say امرأة صبور شكور ("a patient, grateful woman"), and it is a form of intensiveness. ذلول is nominative as an adjective of البقرة, or as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, in which case the clause is an adjective.
(تُثِيرُ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in ذلول, its implied form being: "not made tractable in the state of its ploughing up [the earth]". It may also be nominative, following ذلول.
It has also been said: it is resumptive, i.e. "she ploughs up"; this is the view of those who said that the cow used to plough the land but did not water the crops. This view is far from correct for two reasons. First: that He conjoined to it (وَلَا تَسْقِي الْحَرْثَ), negating the conjoined element, so what it is conjoined to must likewise [be negated], because in meaning they are one. Do you not see that you do not say مررت برجل قائم ولا قاعد ("I passed by a man standing and not sitting"); rather you say لا قاعد without the wāw? So it must be the same here.
Second: that if she ploughed the land she would be tractable (ذلول), and He has negated that.
On the view of those who affirm this interpretation, it is permissible for تثير to be in the position of the nominative as an adjective of البقرة.
(وَلَا تَسْقِي الْحَرْثَ): it may also be an adjective, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. Likewise (مُسَلَّمَةٌ) and «لا شية فيها»; the better view is that it is an adjective.
The original form of (شِيَةَ) is وِشْيَة, because it is from وشى يشي; when the wāw was omitted in the verb, it was omitted in the maṣdar (verbal noun), and the tāʾ was made a compensation for what was omitted; its pattern now is عِلَة. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «(شِيَةَ وَشِيَةَ)», with the original form inside the parentheses.]
فيها is the khabar of لا, in the position of the nominative. (قَالُوا الْآنَ): the alif and lām in الآن are redundant (zāʾida), and it is indeclinable (mabnī). Al-Zajjāj said: it is indeclinable because it contains the meaning of the demonstrative particle, as if you said "this time".
Abū ʿAlī said: it is indeclinable because it contains the meaning of the lām of definiteness, since the alif and lām that are pronounced do not make it definite, nor is it a proper name, nor a pronoun, nor any of the categories of definite nouns; so its definiteness must be by an implied lām. The lām here is redundant with a permanent redundancy, as it is permanent in الذي and in the name of Allah.
In الآن there are four ways [of reading]. First: full pronunciation of the hamza, which is the original.
Second: casting the vowel of the hamza onto the lām and omitting the hamza; the alif of the lām [i.e. the connective hamza of the article] is omitted in these two ways because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the lām originally, because the vowel of the lām here is accidental.
Third: likewise, except that they omitted the alif of the lām when the lām was vowelled, so the wāw in قالوا appears. Fourth: keeping the wāw in pronunciation and making the alif of the lām disjunctive; this is far-fetched.
(بِالْحَقِّ): it may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the implied form being: "you have brought the truth", or "you have mentioned the truth". It may also be a ḥāl from the tāʾ, its implied form being: "you have come with the truth accompanying you".

ukberi-tibyan:105-105.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَا يَوَدُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ وَلَا الْمُشْرِكِينَ أَنْ يُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَاللَّهُ يَخْتَصُّ بِرَحْمَتِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ . . . . . . (١٠٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَلَا الْمُشْرِكِينَ): in the position of the genitive by conjunction with أَهْلِ. If it has been read «وَلَا الْمُشْرِكُونَ» with the nominative, then it is conjoined to the fāʿil (agent).
(أَنْ يُنَزَّلَ): in the position of the accusative, governed by (يَوَدُّ). (مِنْ خَيْرٍ): مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida). And (مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ) is
for the beginning of the extent of the sending down. It may also be an adjective of خَيْرٍ, either genitive according to the wording of خَيْرٍ, or nominative according to the position of «مِنْ خَيْرٍ». (يَخْتَصُّ بِرَحْمَتِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ): i.e. "whomever He wills to single out"; the muḍāf was omitted, leaving مَنْ يَشَاؤُهُ, then the pronoun was omitted. It may also be that يَشَاؤُهُ means يَخْتَارُهُ ("He chooses him"), so that there is no omission of a muḍāf in it.

ukberi-tibyan:106-106.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَا نَنْسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ أَوْ نُنْسِهَا نَأْتِ بِخَيْرٍ مِنْهَا أَوْ مِثْلِهَا . . . . . . . . . . . . (١٠٦)).
His saying: (مَا نَنْسَخْ): مَا is conditional, putting نَنْسَخْ in the jussive, and its position is accusative, governed by (نَنْسَخْ), like His saying: (أَيًّا مَا تَدْعُوا). The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is: ((نَأْتِ بِخَيْرٍ مِنْهَا)).
And (مِنْ آيَةٍ) is in the position of the accusative as a tamyīz (specification), and what is specified is «مَا». The implied form is: "whatever thing We abrogate in the way of a verse". It is not good to take the implied form as "whatever verse We abrogate", because you do not combine this with the specification by آيَةٍ. It [i.e. مِنْ] may also be redundant (zāʾida), with آيَةٍ a ḥāl (circumstantial), the meaning being: "whatever thing We abrogate, little or much".
آيَةٌ has come as a ḥāl in His saying, the Exalted: (هَذِهِ نَاقَةُ اللَّهِ لَكُمْ آيَةً). It is also said that «مَا» here is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun) and آيَةٌ a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the implied form being: "whatever abrogation by which We abrogate a verse".
«نَنْسَخْ» is read with a fatḥa on the nūn, its past being نَسَخَ; and it is read with a ḍamma on the nūn and a kasra on the sīn [i.e. نُنْسِخْ], its past being أُنْسِخَتْ [Translator's note: so printed; the corresponding past is أَنْسَخَ]. One says: أَنْسَخْتُ الْكِتَابَ, i.e. "I submitted the book for copying".
(أَوْ نَنْسَأْهَا): conjoined to نَنْسَخْ.
It is read without hamza, on substituting an alif for the hamza.
It is read تُنْسَهَا without alif or hamza, and نُنْسِهَا with a ḍamma on the nūn and a kasra on the sīn; both are from نَسِيَ when it means "to leave". It may also be from نَسَأَ when it means "to defer", except that the hamza was replaced by an alif.
Whoever read with a ḍamma on the nūn took it in the sense of "We command you to leave it or to defer it"; and in it there is an omitted object, the implied form being: نُنْسِكَهَا ("We make you forget it").

ukberi-tibyan:107-107.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا لَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ وَلَا نَصِيرٍ (١٠٧)).
His saying, the Exalted: (لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the khabar of أَنَّ.
According to al-Akhfash, مُلْكُ may be made nominative by the adverbial phrase (al-ẓarf). And الْمُلْكُ means the thing owned; one says: "so-and-so has a great مُلْك", i.e. what he owns is much. And الْمِلْكُ with the kasra also means what is owned, except that the form with a ḍamma on the mīm is not used in every place, but in places of abundance and breadth of dominion. (مِنْ وَلِيٍّ): مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida), and وَلِيٍّ is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with لَكُمْ its khabar.
And (نَصِيرٍ) is conjoined to the wording of وَلِيٍّ; in ordinary speech its nominative is permissible, according to the position of وَلِيٍّ.
And (مِنْ دُونِ) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from وَلِيٍّ or from نَصِيرٍ. The implied form is: "of a protector other than Allah"; when the adjective of the indefinite noun was put before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:108-108.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَمْ تُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَسْأَلُوا رَسُولَكُمْ كَمَا سُئِلَ مُوسَى مِنْ قَبْلُ وَمَنْ يَتَبَدَّلِ الْكُفْرَ بِالْإِيمَانِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ (١٠٨)).
His saying, the Exalted: (أَمْ تُرِيدُونَ): أَمْ here is disjoined (munqaṭiʿa), since there is no hamza in the speech that occupies its place [as its counterpart], the place of أَمْ being "which of the two". The hamza in His saying «أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ» has nothing to do with أَمْ.
The implied form is: "nay, do you want «أَنْ تَسْأَلُوا»?"; so by أَمْ He moved from one speech to another.
The original form of تُرِيدُونَ is تُرْوِدُونَ [Translator's note: printed «تَرْوِدُونَ»], because it is from رَادَ يَرُودُ [Translator's note: printed «يَرْوِدُ»].
(كَمَا): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a questioning like that"; and مَا is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun). The majority read «سُئِلَ» with a hamza; it was also read سِيلَ with a yāʾ, according to the dialect of those who say سِلْتَ تَسَالُ without a hamza, like خِفْتَ تَخَافُ; the yāʾ is converted from a wāw, because of their saying سِوَالٌ and سَاوَلْتُهُ. And «سُيِلَ» is read by making the hamza "between-between" (bayna bayna), i.e. between the hamza and the yāʾ, because its vowel is of the yāʾ's kind.
(بِالْإِيمَانِ): the bāʾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْكُفْرَ, its implied form being: "in exchange for belief". It may also be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (يَتَبَدَّلِ), the bāʾ being for cause, as when you say: "I bought the garment for a dirham". ((سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ)): سَوَاءَ is an adverbial (ẓarf) meaning the middle of the way, and its most even part. And السَّبِيلُ is treated as both masculine and feminine.

ukberi-tibyan:109-109.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَدَّ كَثِيرٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ لَوْ يَرُدُّونَكُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ إِيمَانِكُمْ كُفَّارًا حَسَدًا مِنْ عِنْدِ أَنْفُسِهِمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الْحَقُّ فَاعْفُوا وَاصْفَحُوا حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ اللَّهُ بِأَمْرِهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (١٠٩)).
His saying, the Exalted: (لَوْ يَرُدُّونَكُمْ): لَوْ has the sense of the maṣdariyya أَنْ, and mention of it has preceded.
And (كُفَّارًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf and mīm. It may also be a second object, because يَرُدُّ means يُصَيِّرُ ("to turn into").
(حَسَدًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); what governs it is (وَدَّ) or (يَرُدُّونَكُمْ).
(مِنْ عِنْدِ أَنْفُسِهِمْ): مِنْ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to حَسَدًا, i.e. the envy originates from themselves. It may also be attached to (وَدَّ) or to (يَرُدُّونَكُمْ).
(حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ اللَّهُ بِأَمْرِهِ): i.e. "pardon up to this limit".

ukberi-tibyan:110-110.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ وَمَا تُقَدِّمُوا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ تَجِدُوهُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ . . . . . . . . . . . . (١١٠)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَمَا تُقَدِّمُوا): مَا is conditional, in the position of the accusative, governed by (تُقَدِّمُوا).
And (مِنْ خَيْرٍ) is like His saying مِنْ آيَةٍ in مَا نَنْسَخْ.
(تَجِدُوهُ): [i.e. you will find] its reward; the muḍāf was omitted. And (عِنْدَ اللَّهِ) is an adverbial (ẓarf) of تَجِدُوا, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

ukberi-tibyan:200-200.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَإِذَا قَضَيْتُمْ مَنَاسِكَكُمْ فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَذِكْرِكُمْ آبَاءَكُمْ أَوْ أَشَدَّ ذِكْرًا فَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَقُولُ رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا وَمَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَاقٍ (٢٠٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَنَاسِكَكُمْ): its singular is مَنْسَك, with fatḥa or kasra on the sīn (مَنْسِك).
The majority pronounce the first kāf distinctly, and some assimilated it, likening the case vowel to an indeclinable vowel and so dropping it. (أَوْ أَشَدَّ): (أو) here is for choice and permission. (أشد) may be genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (ذكركم), its implied form being "or like a more intense", i.e. "or like a more intense remembrance". It may also be accusative, conjoined to the kāf, i.e. "or a more intense remembrance".
And (ذِكْرًا): a tamyīz (specification), and it is in a problematic position. That is because afʿal (the elative) is annexed to what follows it when that is of the same kind as what precedes it, as you say "your remembrance is the most intense remembrance (أشدُّ ذكرٍ)" and "your face is the most beautiful face", i.e. the most intense of remembrances and the most beautiful of faces.
When you put what follows it in the accusative, it is something other than what precedes it, as you say "Zayd is finer as to slave (أفرهُ عبدًا)": the fineness belongs to the slave, not to Zayd. What is mentioned before (أشد) here is the remembrance, and remembrance is not itself a rememberer such that one could say "the remembrance is more intense in remembering"; one only says "the remembrance is the most intense remembrance" with annexation, because the second is the first. What Abū ʿAlī, Ibn Jinnī and others said is that He made the remembrance a rememberer figuratively, as you say "Zayd is more intense in remembrance than ʿAmr". In my view, the speech is construed according to the meaning, and the implied form is "or be more intense in remembrance of Allah than you are of your fathers", this meaning being indicated by His saying, Exalted is He, (فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ), i.e. "be rememberers of Him". This is easier than construing it figuratively.

ukberi-tibyan:201-201.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ (٢٠١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً): (في) may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to (آتنا), and it may be an adjective of (حسنة) that has been placed before it and so become a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَقِنَا): its fāʾ (first radical) was dropped, as it is dropped in the imperfect when you say يَقِي; its lām (last radical) was dropped for the jussive; and the connecting hamza was dispensed with because the letter it begins with has a vowel.

ukberi-tibyan:203-203.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ فِي أَيَّامٍ مَعْدُودَاتٍ فَمَنْ تَعَجَّلَ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ فَلَا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ وَمَنْ تَأَخَّرَ فَلَا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ لِمَنِ اتَّقَى وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّكُمْ إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ (٢٠٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي أَيَّامٍ مَعْدُودَاتٍ): if it is said: the singular of (الأيام) is يوم, and the singular of (المعدودات) is مَعْدُودَة, and يوم is not described with معدودة, because the adjective here is feminine while the thing described is masculine; the proper way would be to say أيام معدودة, describing the plural with a feminine.
The answer is that He made (معدودات) follow the wording of (أيام) and matched plural with plural figuratively, the original being معدودة, as He said: (لَنْ تَمَسَّنَا النَّارُ إِلَّا أَيَّامًا مَعْدُودَةً).
And if it were said that days comprise hours, and the hour (الساعة) is feminine, so the plural was permitted in the sense of "the hours of the days" — with a hint in it at the command to remember (Allah) in all the hours of these days, or in most of them — that would be a sound answer. Parallel to this are "the month", "the summer" and "the winter": they are given as answers to "how many/how long" (كم), whereas (كم) is answered only with a number, and the words for these things are not numbers but names for counted things; so they served as an answer in this respect. (فَلَا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ): the majority keep the hamza.
It has been read «فَلِثْمَ»; its rationale is that when he blended (لا) with the noun, he dropped the hamza because of its resemblance to the alif, and then dropped the alif of (لا) because of its sukūn and the sukūn of the thāʾ after it.
(لِمَنِ اتَّقَى): the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "the permissibility of hastening and delaying is for whoever fears (Allah)".

ukberi-tibyan:204-204.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يُعْجِبُكَ قَوْلُهُ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَيُشْهِدُ اللَّهَ عَلَى مَا فِي قَلْبِهِ وَهُوَ أَلَدُّ الْخِصَامِ (٢٠٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَنْ يُعْجِبُكَ): (مَن) is an indefinite noun that is described. And (فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا): attached (mutaʿalliq) to (القول), the implied form being "concerning the affairs of this world"; it may also be attached to (يُعْجِبُكَ). (وَيُشْهِدُ اللَّهَ): it may be conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (يعجبك).
It may also be a clause in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in (يعجبك), i.e. "he pleases you while he calls Allah to witness". It may also be a ḥāl of the hāʾ in «قَوْلُهُ», governed by (القول), the implied form being "it pleases you that he speaks about worldly matters, swearing to it". The majority read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ, kasra on the hāʾ and the name of Allah in the accusative.
It has also been read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the hāʾ and the name of Allah in the nominative (وَيَشْهَدُ اللَّهُ), and that is clear.
(وَهُوَ أَلَدُّ): the clause may be an adjective conjoined to (يعجبك).
It may be a ḥāl conjoined to «وَيُشْهِدُ».
And it may be a ḥāl of the pronoun in (يشهد).
And (الْخِصَامِ) here is the plural of خَصْم, like كَعْب and كِعَاب.
It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun), with the omission of a muḍāf in the speech, i.e. "the most intense of those given to quarrelling".
(الخصام) here may also be a maṣdar in the sense of the active participle, just as one describes with a maṣdar when you say "a just (عَدْل) man" and "an adversary (خَصْم)".
The afʿal here may also be not for comparison, so that it can properly be annexed to the maṣdar, its implied form being "and he is severe in quarrelling". It may also be that (هو) is the pronoun of the maṣdar, namely «قَوْلُهُ» — his speech is quarrelling — the implied form being "his quarrelling is the most fierce of quarrelling".

ukberi-tibyan:205-205.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذَا تَوَلَّى سَعَى فِي الْأَرْضِ لِيُفْسِدَ فِيهَا وَيُهْلِكَ الْحَرْثَ وَالنَّسْلَ وَاللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الْفَسَادَ (٢٠٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِيُفْسِدَ): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (سعى).
(وَيُهْلِكَ): with ḍamma on the yāʾ, kasra on the lām and fatḥa on the kāf, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (يفسد); this is the well-known reading. It has also been read with ḍamma on the kāf (وَيُهْلِكُ), as a resumption, or by implying a mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "and he destroys".
It has also been said: it is conjoined to (يعجبك). And it has been said: it is conjoined to the sense of (سعى), because the implied form is "and when he turns away, he strives".
It is also read with fatḥa on the yāʾ, kasra on the lām, ḍamma on the kāf and (الحرث) in the nominative (وَيَهْلِكُ الْحَرْثُ), the implied form being "and the tillage perishes through his striving". It has also been read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the lām (يَهْلَك), and that is a very weak dialect.
And (الْحَرْثَ): the maṣdar (verbal noun) of حَرَثَ يَحْرُثُ; here it means "what is tilled".
(وَالنَّسْلَ): likewise, meaning "what is begotten".

ukberi-tibyan:206-206.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُ اتَّقِ اللَّهَ أَخَذَتْهُ الْعِزَّةُ بِالْإِثْمِ فَحَسْبُهُ جَهَنَّمُ وَلَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ (٢٠٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الْعِزَّةُ بِالْإِثْمِ): (بالإثم) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (العزة), the implied form being "pride seized him, bound up with sin". It may also be a ḥāl of the hāʾ, i.e. "pride seized him while sinning".
The bāʾ may also be causal, so that it is an object, i.e. "pride seized him because of sin".
(فَحَسْبُهُ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (جَهَنَّمُ) its khabar (predicate).
It has also been said: (جهنم) is the fāʿil (agent) of (حسبه), because (حسبه) has the sense of an active participle, i.e. "sufficing for him". It has been read with the fāʾ that links the clause to what precedes it, the agent standing in place of the khabar; (حسب) is a maṣdar in the position of an active participle. (وَلَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ): the one specified for blame is omitted, i.e. "and how evil a resting place is Hell".

ukberi-tibyan:207-207.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَشْرِي نَفْسَهُ ابْتِغَاءَ مَرْضَاةِ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ رَءُوفٌ بِالْعِبَادِ (٢٠٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ابْتِغَاءَ مَرْضَاةِ اللَّهِ): the majority pronounce (مرضاة) with tafkhīm (full, open alif).
It has also been read with imāla (inclination of the alif towards ī), to harmonise with the kasra of the tāʾ. When Ḥamza is forced to pause here, he pauses on the tāʾ, and there are two views on this: the first: it is a dialect in pausing on the feminine tāʾ wherever it occurs.
The second: that by pausing on the tāʾ he indicates that the muḍāf ilayhi is intended, so it is as though it were in continuous reading.

ukberi-tibyan:208-208.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ادْخُلُوا فِي السِّلْمِ كَافَّةً وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَانِ إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ (٢٠٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي السِّلْمِ): it is read with kasra and with fatḥa on the sīn with sukūn on the lām, and with fatḥa on both the sīn and the lām (السَّلَم); it means peace, and it is treated as masculine and feminine; from it is His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِنْ جَنَحُوا لِلسَّلْمِ فَاجْنَحْ لَهَا). Some said: the kasra means Islam, and the fatḥa means peace.
(كَافَّةً): a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent in (ادخلوا). It has also been said: it is a ḥāl of (السلم), i.e. "into peace in all its aspects".

ukberi-tibyan:210-210.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ فِي ظُلَلٍ مِنَ الْغَمَامِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ وَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ وَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الْأُمُورُ (٢١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ): its wording is that of a question and its meaning is negation; for this reason (إلا) came after it. (فِي ظُلَلٍ): it may be an adverbial (ẓarf), and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial); (الظلل) is the plural of ظُلَّة.
It is also read (فِي ظِلَالٍ); it has been said that it is the plural of ظِلّ, and it has also been said that it too is the plural of ظُلَّة, like خُلَّة/خِلَال and قُلَّة/قِلَال. (مِنَ الْغَمَامِ): it may be a description of (ظلل); and (من) may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to (يأتيهم), i.e. "comes to them from the direction of the clouds". (الغمام) is the plural of غَمَامَة. (وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ): read in the nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the name of Allah, and in the genitive (وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ), conjoined to (ظلل); it may also be conjoined to (الغمام).

ukberi-tibyan:164-164.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ وَالْفُلْكِ الَّتِي تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ بِمَا يَنْفَعُ النَّاسَ وَمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مِنْ مَاءٍ فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِنْ كُلِّ دَابَّةٍ وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّيَاحِ وَالسَّحَابِ الْمُسَخَّرِ بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَآيَاتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ (١٦٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالْفُلْكِ): it is singular and plural with one and the same form. Of the plural is this place and His saying (حَتَّى إِذَا كُنْتُمْ فِي الْفُلْكِ وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِمْ); and of the singular is (الْفُلْكِ الْمَشْحُونِ).
The view of the exacting scholars (al-muḥaqqiqūn) is that the ḍamma on the fāʾ, when it is plural, is other than the ḍamma that is in the singular. The proof of that is that the ḍamma of the plural occurs in words whose singular does not have ḍamma, such as أُسْدٌ and كُتُبٌ, whose singulars are أَسَدٌ and كِتَابٌ. A parallel to this is the ḍamma on the ṣād of مَنْصُورٌ when you truncate it (tarkhīm) according to the dialect of those who say يَا حَارِ: it is a newly arising ḍamma; whereas according to those who say يَا حَارِ, the ḍamma in يَا مَنْصُ is the ḍamma that is in مَنْصُورٌ. [Translator's note: the source gives the same form يَا حَارِ for both dialects; the first is evidently meant to be يَا حَارُ, the truncation in which the dropped letter is not taken into account.] (مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مِنْ مَاءٍ): the first مِنْ is for the beginning of the extent, and the second is for specifying the genus, since He sends down from the sky water and other things. (وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِنْ كُلِّ دَابَّةٍ): the object of بَثَّ is omitted, its implied form being: "and He spread therein creatures of every kind of creature". It is also possible, according to the school of al-Akhfash, for مِنْ to be redundant (zāʾida), because he permits it in affirmative statements.
(وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّيَاحِ): it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in construct with its object. It may also be put in construct with its agent, with the object omitted, the implied form being: "and the winds' turning about of the clouds", because the winds drive the clouds and turn them about. (الرِّيَاحِ) is read in the plural because of the differing kinds of wind, and in the singular as denoting the genus, or by putting the singular in place of the plural. The yāʾ of (الرِّيحِ) is substituted for a wāw, because it is from رَاحَ يَرُوحُ and رَوَّحْتُهُ [Translator's note: the source has رَوْحَتُهُ], and the plural is أَرْوَاحٌ.
As for الرِّيَاحُ, the yāʾ in it is substituted for a wāw because it is a plural whose first letter has kasra, after whose weak letter there is an additional alif, and whose singular has a quiescent middle radical; so it is like سَوْطٌ and سِيَاطٌ, except that the wāw of الرِّيحُ was changed to yāʾ because it is quiescent and preceded by kasra.
(بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ): it may be an adverb for الْمُسَخَّرِ, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in الْمُسَخَّرِ. There is no complete pause (waqf tāmm) in this verse, because the noun of the إِنَّ at its beginning is at its end.

ukberi-tibyan:165-165.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَتَّخِذُ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَنْدَادًا يُحِبُّونَهُمْ كَحُبِّ اللَّهِ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَشَدُّ حُبًّا لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ يَرَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا إِذْ يَرَوْنَ الْعَذَابَ أَنَّ الْقُوَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعَذَابِ (١٦٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَنْ يَتَّخِذُ): مَنْ is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective; it may also mean "the one who" (الَّذِي). (يُحِبُّونَهُمْ): in the position of the accusative as an adjective (ṣifa) of الْأَنْدَاد; it may also be in the position of the nominative as an adjective of مَنْ, if you make it indefinite.
Both views are permissible because the clause contains two pronouns, one for مَنْ and the other for the rivals (al-andād). The rivals are referred to with (هُمْ), as rational beings are referred to with it, because they treated them as rational beings.
The kāf is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of the omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a love like the love of Allah"; and the maṣdar is put in construct with its object, its implied form being: "like their love of Allah", or "like the believers' love of Allah".
(وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَشَدُّ حُبًّا لِلَّهِ): what «أَشَدُّ» is attached to is omitted, its implied form being: "in love for Allah, than the love of these for the rivals". (وَلَوْ يَرَى): the apodosis (jawāb) of لَوْ is omitted, and that is more forceful in promise and threat, because when the one promised or threatened knows the extent of the blessing or the punishment, his mind stops at that specified thing; but when he does not know it, his imagination goes to what is greater than that. The implied apodosis is: "they would know that the power…", or "they would know that the rivals neither harm nor benefit". The majority read يَرَى with yāʾ, and يَرَى here is from mental seeing (ruʾyat al-qalb), so it requires two objects, and «أَنَّ الْقُوَّةَ» stands in place of both. It is also said that the two objects are omitted and أَنَّ الْقُوَّةَ is governed by the apodosis of لَوْ, i.e. "if the disbelievers knew their rivals do not benefit, they would know that the power in benefit and harm belongs to Allah".
It is also possible for يَرَى to be in the sense of "knew" (عَلِمَ) [in the sense of عَرَفَ], transitive to one object; then the implied form is: "if those who did wrong recognized the falsehood of their worship of the idols", or "if they recognized the measure of the punishment, they would know that the power…", or "if they recognized that the power belongs to Allah, they would not have worshipped the idols".
It is also said that يَرَى here is from physical sight (ruʾyat al-baṣar), i.e. "if they witnessed the traces of Allah's power"; then أَنَّ and what it governs are the object of يَرَى. It is also possible for the object of يَرَى to be omitted, its implied form being: "if they witnessed the punishment, they would know that the power…", this omitted element being indicated by His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ يَرَوْنَ الْعَذَابَ).
And يَرَوْنَ الْعَذَابَ is from physical sight, because the one that means knowledge is transitive to two objects, and when one of them is mentioned the other must be mentioned. It may also be in the sense of recognizing, i.e. "when they recognize the severity of the punishment". It results from what we have mentioned that the apodosis of لَوْ may be implied before إِنَّ الْقُوَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا, or implied after it.
«لَوْ» is followed by the past verb, but the imperfect form was put in its place, either as a vivid representation of the situation (ḥikāyat al-ḥāl), or because the report of Allah the Exalted is truth, so that what has not yet happened, by His reporting of it, has the status of what has happened.
As for (إِذْ), it is an adverb of time, and here it occurs with a future meaning, whereas it was coined to indicate the past; but that is permissible for the reason we mentioned, that Allah's report of the future is like the past, or as a vivid representation of the situation by means of إِذْ, just as it is represented by the verb.
It is also said: He put إِذْ in the place of إِذَا, just as the past verb is put in the place of the future, because of the closeness between them. And it is said that the time of the Hereafter is joined to the time of this world, so He made its future like the past, since what is adjacent to a thing takes its place. This recurs often in the Quran, as in His saying: «وَلَوْ تَرَى إِذْ وُقِفُوا عَلَى النَّارِ», «وَلَوْ تَرَى إِذْ وُقِفُوا عَلَى رَبِّهِمْ», and «وَإِذِ الْأَغْلَالُ فِي أَعْنَاقِهِمْ» [Translator's note: the Quranic wording is إِذِ الْأَغْلَالُ فِي أَعْنَاقِهِمْ (Ghāfir 40:71), without wāw].
(وَإِذْ يَرَوْنَ): an adverb for the first يَرَى. It was read وَلَوْ تَرَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا with tāʾ, and this is from seeing with the eye, i.e. "if you saw them at the time of their being punished". And يَرَوْنَ is read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and with ḍamma [يُرَوْنَ], and it is clear in i'rab and meaning.
The majority read the hamza with fatḥa in «أَنَّ الْقُوَّةَ» and «وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعَذَابِ».
It is also read with kasra in both, as a new beginning (istiʾnāf), or with the implied form "they would say: indeed the power belongs to Allah".
And (جَمِيعًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the preposition phrase, and what governs it is the meaning of settledness (al-istiqrār).

ukberi-tibyan:166-167.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ تَبَرَّأَ الَّذِينَ اتُّبِعُوا مِنَ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوا وَرَأَوُا الْعَذَابَ وَتَقَطَّعَتْ بِهِمُ الْأَسْبَابُ (١٦٦) وَقَالَ الَّذين اتبعُوا لَو أَن لنا كرة فنتبرأ مِنْهُم كَمَا تبرؤوا منا كَذَلِك يُرِيهم الله أَعْمَالهم حسرات عَلَيْهِم وَمَا هم بِخَارِجِينَ من النَّار).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ تَبَرَّأَ): this إِذْ is a badal (substitute) for the first إِذْ, or an adverb for His saying (شَدِيدُ الْعَذَابِ), or the object of [an implied] "remember". تَبَرَّأَ means يَتَبَرَّأُ ("will disown"). (وَرَأَوُا الْعَذَابَ): conjoined to تَبَرَّأَ.
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), with قَدْ intended with it, and what governs it is تَبَرَّأَ, i.e. "they disowned, having seen the punishment". (وَتَقَطَّعَتْ بِهِمُ): the bāʾ here is causal, and the implied form is: "and [the ties] were cut because of their disbelief".
(الْأَسْبَابُ): [the ties] by which they used to hope for salvation.
The bāʾ may also be for the ḥāl, i.e. "the ties were cut while connected with them", as when you say خَرَجَ زَيْدٌ بِثِيَابِهِ ("Zayd went out with his clothes on"). It is also said that بِهِمْ means "from them" (عَنْهُمْ). And it is said that the bāʾ is for making transitive (taʿdiya), and the implied form is: "the ties cut them off", as you say تَفَرَّقَتْ بِهِمُ الطُّرُقُ ("the roads dispersed them"), i.e. separated them; and of this is His saying, Exalted is He: (فَتَفَرَّقَ بِكُمْ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ).
(كَرَّةً): the maṣdar (verbal noun) of كَرَّ يَكِرُّ, when one returns.
(فَنَتَبَرَّأَ): accusative by an implied أَنْ, its implied form being: "if only we had [the chance] to return and to disown". On this view the apodosis (jawāb) of لَوْ is omitted, its implied form being: "we would disown them", or something similar.
It is also said: لَوْ here is for wishing (tamannī), so فَنَتَبَرَّأَ is accusative as the reply to the wish, and the meaning is: "would that we had a return, so that we might disown". (كَذَلِكَ): the kāf is in the position of the nominative, i.e. "the matter is thus".
It may also be accusative as an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "He shows them a showing like that", or "He gathers them like that", or "He requites them", and the like. And (يُرِيهِمُ) is from seeing with the eye, so it is transitive here to two objects by means of the hamza of transfer; and «حَسَرَاتٍ» on this view is a ḥāl. It is also said that يُرِيهِمْ means "He makes them know", so حَسَرَاتٍ is a third object.
And (عَلَيْهِمْ) is an adjective of حَسَرَاتٍ, i.e. "being upon them".
It may also be attached (mutaʿalliq) to حَسَرَاتٍ itself, on the basis that there is an omitted muḍāf in the speech, its implied form being: "over their negligence", as you say: تَحَسَّرُ عَلَى تَفْرِيطِهِمْ ("[one] grieves over their negligence").

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ (٢١)).
His saying, the Exalted: (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ): أَيُّ is a vague noun (mubham), since it applies to everything. It is brought in the vocative as a means of addressing what has the alif and lām, since «يَا» does not come directly before the alif and lām. It is indeclinable (mabnī) because it is a single, specifically intended noun. هَا is inserted for drawing attention, because originally «يَا» would come directly before النَّاسُ; when أَيٌّ was put between them, «هَا» was given in compensation for that. النَّاسُ is a naʿt (adjective) of أَيٌّ that cannot be dispensed with, because it is the one addressed in meaning; hence it is nominative, its nominative being made to correspond to the ḍamma of indeclinability. Al-Māzinī allowed it to be accusative, just as he allows يَا زَيْدُ الظَّرِيفَ ("O Zayd, the witty one"); this is weak, for the reason we gave that it must be mentioned, whereas an adjective need not be mentioned. (مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ): مِنْ here is for the beginning of the extent in time; the implied wording is "and those whom He created before your creation"; so "creation" was omitted and the pronoun put in its place. (لَعَلَّكُمْ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) in meaning to (اعْبُدُوا), i.e. "worship, so that hope of piety may validly be held of you". The original form [of تَتَّقُونَ] is تَوْتَقِيُونَ; tāʾ was substituted for the wāw and assimilated into the other tāʾ, and the yāʾ was made quiescent and then dropped; its counterparts have preceded. So its pattern now is taftaʿūn.

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ فِرَاشًا وَالسَّمَاءَ بِنَاءً وَأَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَخْرَجَ بِهِ مِنَ الثَّمَرَاتِ رِزْقًا لَكُمْ فَلَا تَجْعَلُوا لِلَّهِ أَنْدَادًا وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ (٢٢)).
His saying, the Exalted: (الَّذِي جَعَلَ) is in the position of the accusative, governed by (تَتَّقُونَ); or as a badal (substitute) for رَبَّكُمْ; or as a repeated adjective; or by implying أَعْنِي ("I mean").
It may also be in the position of the nominative by implying "He is the one who" (هُوَ الَّذِي). جَعَلَ here is transitive to one object, namely الْأَرْضَ, and (فِرَاشًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and likewise (وَالسَّمَاءَ بِنَاءً).
جَعَلَ may also have the meaning of صَيَّرَ ("made into"), so that it is transitive to two objects, namely الْأَرْضَ and فِرَاشًا; and its like is وَالسَّمَاءَ بَنَاهَا. (وَلَكُمْ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (جَعَلَ), i.e. "for your sake". (مِنَ السَّمَاءِ) is attached to أَنْزَلَ, and it is for the beginning of the extent in place.
It may also be a ḥāl, the implied wording being "water existing from the sky"; when the preposition was placed first it became a ḥāl and is attached to something omitted. The original form of مَاءٌ is مَوَهٌ, because they say مَاهَتِ الرَّكِيَّةُ تَمُوهُ ("the well had plenty of water"), and in the plural أَمْوَاهٌ. Since the wāw was vowelled and the letter before it had fatḥa, it was turned into alif; then they substituted a hamza for the hāʾ, and this is not according to regular analogy.
(مِنَ الثَّمَرَاتِ) is attached to أَخْرَجَ, so that «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent. It may also be in the position of a ḥāl, its implied form being "a provision existing from the fruits".
(لَكُمْ), i.e. "for your sake". الرِّزْقُ here has the meaning of the passive participle (الْمَرْزُوقُ, "what is provided"), and is not a maṣdar (verbal noun).
(فَلَا تَجْعَلُوا), i.e. "do not make" or "do not name", so it is transitive to two objects.
الْأَنْدَادُ is the plural of نِدٌّ and نَدِيدٌ ("rival, equal"). (وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of a ḥāl. The object of تَعْلَمُونَ is omitted, i.e. "you know the falsity of that".
The noun in أَنْتُمْ is «أَنْ»; the tāʾ is for address and the mīm for the plural, and both are particles carrying meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ فِي رَيْبٍ مِمَّا نَزَّلْنَا عَلَى عَبْدِنَا فَأْتُوا بِسُورَةٍ مِنْ مِثْلِهِ وَادْعُوا شُهَدَاءَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ (٢٣)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ): the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is «فَأْتُوا بِسُورَةٍ». «إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ» is also a condition, whose apodosis is omitted, the apodosis of the first condition making it unnecessary, i.e. "if you are truthful, then do that". The conditional إِنْ does not enter on a verb that is past in meaning, except on كَانَ, because of its frequent use and because it does not indicate an event. (مِمَّا نَزَّلْنَا) is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of رَيْبٍ, i.e. "a doubt arising from what We sent down".
The element referring back to «مَا» is omitted, i.e. نَزَّلْنَاهُ; «مَا» has the meaning of الَّذِي, or is an indefinite noun described [by what follows]. «مِنْ» may also be attached (mutaʿalliq) to رَيْبٍ, i.e. "if you doubt because of what We sent down".
(فَأْتُوا): its original form is ائْتِيُوا. Its past tense is أَتَى, so the first radical of the word is a hamza. When you form the imperative you add to it the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) with kasra, so two hamzas come together, the second quiescent; the second was then replaced by yāʾ so that two hamzas would not be combined, and the yāʾ was [chosen] because of the kasra before it [Translator's note: the text reads «وَكَانَتِ الْيَاءُ الْأُولَى لِلْكَسْرَةِ قَبْلَهَا»; perhaps «أَوْلَى», "more appropriate", is meant]. When something is joined before it, the connecting hamza is dropped, being no longer needed, and then the yāʾ is pronounced as hamza, because you have returned it to its original, the cause requiring its change having gone.
This hamza may be turned into alif when the letter before it has fatḥa, as in this verse (فَاتُوا); into yāʾ when the letter before it has kasra, as in His saying الَّذِي إِيتُمِنَ [Translator's note: the text has «إِيتَمَنَ»], so that you make it a yāʾ in pronunciation; and into wāw when the letter before it has ḍamma, as in His saying يَا صَالِحُ أُوتِنَا. Some of them say ذَنْ لِي [for ائْذَنْ لِي]. (مِنْ مِثْلِهِ): the hāʾ refers back to the Prophet ﷺ, in which case مِنْ is for the beginning [of the extent]; or it may refer back to the Qur'an, in which case مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida); or it may refer back to الْأَنْدَادُ in the singular form, as in His saying, the Exalted: (وَإِنَّ لَكُمْ فِي الْأَنْعَامِ لَعِبْرَةً نُسْقِيكُمْ مِمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ مِنْ بَيْنِ فَرْثٍ وَدَمٍ لَبَنًا خَالِصًا سَائِغًا لِلشَّارِبِينَ).
(وَادْعُوا): the final radical of the word is dropped, because it is dropped in the singular as an indication of the sukūn that in a declinable word is the jussive (jazm). This wāw is the pronoun of the group.
(مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ) is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الشُّهَدَاءَ, and what governs it is omitted, its implied form being "your witnesses, apart from Allah", or "apart from the helpers of Allah".

ukberi-tibyan:278-278.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَذَرُوا مَا بَقِيَ مِنَ الرِّبَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ (٢٧٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا بَقِيَ): the majority read it with fatḥa on the bāʾ, and it has been read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, with sukūn on it. Its justification is that he lightened it by dropping the vowel from the yāʾ after a kasra. Al-Mubarrad said: making the yāʾ of the manqūṣ noun quiescent in the accusative is among the best of poetic licences (ḍarūra) — and this is despite its being declinable (muʿrab), so in the past verb it is even better.

ukberi-tibyan:279-279.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُوا فَأْذَنُوا بِحَرْبٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَإِنْ تُبْتُمْ فَلَكُمْ رُءُوسُ أَمْوَالِكُمْ لَا تَظْلِمُونَ وَلَا تُظْلَمُونَ (٢٧٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَأْذَنُوا): it is read with the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) and fatḥa on the dhāl; its past is أَذِنَ, and the meaning is: "then be certain of a war". It is also read with the disjunctive hamza (hamzat al-qaṭʿ), with madd and kasra on the dhāl; its past is آذِنْ [Translator's note: so in the text; the past form would be آذَنَ], i.e. "inform", and the object is omitted, i.e. "then inform others than yourselves". It has also been said that the meaning is: "become knowing of the war".
(لَا تَظْلِمُونَ وَلَا تُظْلَمُونَ): it is read with the agent named (active voice) in the first and the agent unnamed (passive) in the second. Its justification is that forbidding them from wronging is more important, so it was put first.
It is also read the other way round; the justification for it is that He put first what would set their souls at rest, namely the negation of wrong being done to them, and then forbade them from doing wrong. It is also possible that the two readings have one meaning, because the wāw does not impose order.

ukberi-tibyan:280-280.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِنْ كَانَ ذُو عُسْرَةٍ فَنَظِرَةٌ إِلَى مَيْسَرَةٍ وَأَنْ تَصَدَّقُوا خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ (٢٨٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِنْ كَانَ ذُو عُسْرَةٍ): كان here is the complete (tāmma) one, i.e. "if there occurs one in difficulty". It has also been said that it is the deficient (nāqiṣa) one, and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: "and if one in difficulty is someone against whom you have a claim", or something similar. Had he put it in the accusative, saying ذا عسرة, then the one who owes the debt would have to be someone meant by a previous mention, and that is not in the wording — unless one strains to supply it. العُسرة and العُسر have the same meaning.
النَّظِرة, with kasra on the ẓāʾ, is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning "deferment". The majority read it with kasra, and it is read with sukūn, preferring lightness, like فَخِذ and فَخْذ, and كَتِف and كَتْف.
It is also read فناظرةٌ with an alif, and that is a maṣdar like العاقبة and العافية. And it is read فناظِرْهُ as an imperative, as you say: سَاهِلْهُ ("be lenient with him") by deferment. (إِلَى مَيْسَرَةٍ): i.e. until the time of ease, or the existence of ease.
The majority read it with fatḥa on the sīn and with the feminine [ending].
It has been read with ḍamma on the sīn, making the hāʾ a pronoun. That is an irregular pattern of which only مَكْرُم and مَعْوُن occur — and even these have been interpreted as plurals of مَكْرُمة and مَعُونة.
After that, the reading admits two possibilities:
The first: that it is the plural of مَيْسُرة, as they said regarding the [other] two patterns.
The second: that he meant مَيْسُورة, and dropped the wāw, content with the ḍamma indicating it. The nominative of نظرة is by being the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar is omitted, i.e. "then upon you is a deferment"; and إلى is attached (mutaʿalliq) to نظرة.
(وَأَنْ تَصَدَّقُوا): it is read with doubling (tashdīd); its origin is تتصدّقوا, then the second tāʾ was changed into ṣād and assimilated. It is also read without doubling, on the basis that the tāʾ was simply dropped.

ukberi-tibyan:281-281.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاتَّقُوا يَوْمًا تُرْجَعُونَ فِيهِ إِلَى اللَّهِ ثُمَّ تُوَفَّى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَا كَسَبَتْ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ (٢٨١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تُرْجَعُونَ فِيهِ): the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of يوم.
It is read with fatḥa on the tāʾ, with the agent named (active voice), and with ḍamma on it, with the agent unnamed (passive), on the basis that it is from رَجَعْتُهُ, i.e. "I returned him". It is transitive on this view; were it not so, it would not have been made passive.
It is also read with yāʾ, in the third person: (وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «كل», because it carries the meaning of a plural.
And it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in يرجعون on the reading with yāʾ, on the basis that He moved from second-person address to the third person, as in His saying: (حَتَّى إِذَا كُنْتُمْ فِي الْفُلْكِ وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِمْ).

ukberi-tibyan:111-111.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالُوا لَنْ يَدْخُلَ الْجَنَّةَ إِلَّا مَنْ كَانَ هُودًا أَوْ نَصَارَى تِلْكَ أَمَانِيُّهُمْ قُلْ هَاتُوا بُرْهَانَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ (١١١)).
His saying, the Exalted: (إِلَّا مَنْ كَانَ): in the position of the nominative, governed by (يَدْخُلَ), because the verb is left free (mufarragh) for what comes after إِلَّا. «كَانَ» is construed according to the wording of مَنْ, in the singular. And (هُودًا) is the plural of هَائِدٌ, like عَائِذٌ and عُوذٌ; it is from هَادَ يَهُودُ when one repents, and from it is His saying, the Exalted: (إِنَّا هُدْنَا إِلَيْكَ). Al-Farrāʾ said: its original is يَهُودُ, and the yāʾ was dropped; but that is very far-fetched. It was put in the plural according to the meaning of مَنْ. And (أَوْ) here is for detailing what was stated summarily. That is, the Jews said: "None will enter the Garden except one who is a Jew", and the Christians said: "None will enter the Garden except one who is a Christian"; and neither party said: "None will enter the Garden except one who is a Jew or a Christian". So since He did not detail it in His saying «وَقَالُوا», He brought أَوْ for detailing, since it is set for one of two things.
And (نَصَارَى) is the plural of نَصْرَانٌ, like سَكْرَانٌ and سُكَارَى.
(هَاتُوا): a verb whose third radical is weak. You say in the past هَاتَا [Translator's note: so printed; the past is هَاتَى], يُهَاتِي, مُهَاتَاةً, like رَامَى [Translator's note: printed «رَامِي»] يُرَامِي مُرَامَاةً; and هَاتُوا is like رَامُوا. Its original form is هَاتِيُوا; then the yāʾ was made quiescent and dropped, for the reason we mentioned at His saying اشْتَرَوْا and its parallels. You say to a man in the imperative: هَاتِ, like رَامِ, and to a woman: هَاتِي, like رَامِي; and on this measure the remaining inflections of this word. هَاتُوا is a verb transitive to one object, and its implied sense is أَحْضِرُوا ("bring").
(بُرْهَانَكُمْ): the nūn in بُرْهَانٌ is radical according to some, because of their saying بَرْهَنْتُ, so the nūn is kept in the verb; and it is added according to others, because it is from «الْبَرَهُ», which is cutting, and الْبُرْهَانُ is the decisive proof.

ukberi-tibyan:112-112.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (بَلَى مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُ لِلَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌ فَلَهُ أَجْرُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (١١٢)).
His saying, the Exalted: (بَلَى): an answer to a negation, as we mentioned at His saying: (بَلَى مَنْ كَسَبَ). And (أَسْلَمَ), (وَجْهَهُ) and «هُوَ» are all construed according to the wording of مَنْ, and likewise (فَلَهُ أَجْرُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ); while His saying (وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ) is construed according to its meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:113-113.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَتِ الْيَهُودُ لَيْسَتِ النَّصَارَى عَلَى شَيْءٍ وَقَالَتِ النَّصَارَى لَيْسَتِ الْيَهُودُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ وَهُمْ يَتْلُونَ الْكِتَابَ كَذَلِكَ قَالَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ فَاللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فِيمَا كَانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ (١١٣)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَهُمْ يَتْلُونَ الْكِتَابَ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and what governs it is قَالَتْ. The original form of يَتْلُونَ is يَتْلُوُونَ; the wāw was made quiescent, then dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
(كَذَلِكَ قَالَ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) made accusative by (قَالَ); it is a maṣdar placed before the verb, and the implied form is: "a saying like the saying of the Jews and the Christians, said those who do not act (لَا يَعْمَلُونَ)" [Translator's note: so printed here and below («يَعْمَلُونَ»); the verse has لَا يَعْلَمُونَ, "do not know", which the sentence closing this discussion follows]. On this view (مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ) is accusative, governed by (يَعْمَلُونَ) or by (قَالَ), as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). It may also be that the kāf is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause after it being a khabar (predicate) about it, with the pronoun returning to the mubtadaʾ omitted, its implied form being: "said it (قَالَهُ)". On this view His saying (مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ) is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, or an object of يَعْمَلُونَ.
And the meaning is: like the saying of the Jews and the Christians, those who do not know the belief of the Jews and the Christians said.
مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ cannot be the object of قَالَ, because it has already taken its object in full, namely the omitted pronoun. And (فِيهِ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (يَخْتَلِفُونَ).

ukberi-tibyan:114-114.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنْ مَنَعَ مَسَاجِدَ اللَّهِ أَنْ يُذْكَرَ فِيهَا اسْمُهُ وَسَعَى فِي خَرَابِهَا أُولَئِكَ مَا كَانَ لَهُمْ أَنْ يَدْخُلُوهَا إِلَّا خَائِفِينَ لَهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا خِزْيٌ وَلَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ (١١٤)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ): مَنْ is an interrogative in the sense of negation; it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and أَظْلَمُ is its khabar (predicate). The meaning is: "no one is more unjust". (مِمَّنْ مَنَعَ): مَنْ is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa), or means "the one who". «أَنْ يُذْكَرَ»: there are three views on it.
