The first: it is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) of مَسَاجِدَ, a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), its implied form being: "the mentioning of His name in them". The second: that it is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), its implied form being: "out of dislike that it be mentioned".
The third: that it is in the position of the genitive, its implied form being "from that it be mentioned (مِنْ أَنْ يُذْكَرَ)". When مِنْ is overt, it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to مَنَعَ, as in your saying: "I prevented him from such-and-such".
When the preposition is omitted with أَنْ [Translator's note: printed «أَنَّ»], the genitive remains; it is also said that it comes to be in the position of the accusative. We have mentioned that at His saying: (لَا يَسْتَحْيِي أَنْ يَضْرِبَ).
(وَسَعَى فِي خَرَابِهَا): خَرَابٌ is a noun for "ruining" (al-takhrīb), as السَّلَامُ is a noun for "greeting with peace" (al-taslīm); it is not a noun for the physical [ruin]. The noun of the maṣdar has been put in construct with the object, because it governs as the maṣdar (verbal noun) governs.
(إِلَّا خَائِفِينَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يَدْخُلُوهَا. (لَهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا): a resumptive clause (jumla mustaʾnafa), not a ḥāl like خَائِفِينَ, because their deserving of disgrace is established in every state, not specifically in the state of their entering the mosques.

ukberi-tibyan:115-115.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلِلَّهِ الْمَشْرِقُ وَالْمَغْرِبُ فَأَيْنَمَا تُوَلُّوا فَثَمَّ وَجْهُ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ (١١٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَلِلَّهِ الْمَشْرِقُ وَالْمَغْرِبُ): they are the place of rising and of setting.
(فَأَيْنَمَا): conditional, and (تُوَلُّوا) is jussive (majzūm) by it, and it is what puts أَيْنَ in the accusative; the apodosis is (فَثَمَّ). In the anomalous readings (al-shādhdh) it was read تَوَلَّوْا with a fatḥa on the tāʾ, and there are two views on it. One: it too is imperfect, its implied form being تَتَوَلَّوْا, the second tāʾ having been dropped.
The second: that it is past, the pronoun being for the absent (third person), the implied form being: "wherever they turn".
It is also said that it may be a past that has already occurred, and أَيْنَ is not a condition in wording, but in
meaning, as you say: "whatever you did, I did (مَا صَنَعْتَ صَنَعْتُ)", when you intend the past. This is weak, because أَيْنَ is either interrogative or conditional, and it has no third meaning. And (ثَمَّ) is a noun for the place far from you; it is indeclinable (mabnī) because it includes the sense of the demonstrative particle.
It is also said that it is indeclinable because it includes the sense of the particle of address, because you say for the present هُنَا and for the absent هُنَاكَ, and ثَمَّ stands in for هُنَاكَ.

ukberi-tibyan:116-116.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالُوا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَدًا سُبْحَانَهُ بَلْ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ كُلٌّ لَهُ قَانِتُونَ (١١٦)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَقَالُوا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَدًا): it is read with the wāw, conjoined to His saying: (وَقَالُوا لَنْ يَدْخُلَ الْجَنَّةَ).
It is read without the wāw, as a resumption. (كُلٌّ لَهُ): its implied form is "each one of them" or "all of them", because the basic use of كُلٌّ is in construct; and from here the majority of grammarians held that the alif and lām may not enter كُلٌّ, because its specification is by what it is put in construct with, so when that is not pronounced it is in the status of what is pronounced. He construed the khabar (predicate) according to the meaning of كُلٌّ, so He put it in the plural in His saying قَانِتُونَ; had He said قَانِتٌ, it would have been permissible according to the wording of كُلٌّ.

ukberi-tibyan:168-168.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ كُلُوا مِمَّا فِي الْأَرْضِ حَلَالًا طَيِّبًا وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَانِ إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ (١٦٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كُلُوا مِمَّا فِي الْأَرْضِ): the original of كُلْ is أُأْكُلْ; the first hamza is the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) and the second is the first radical (fāʾ) of the word. But they dropped the fāʾ and so dispensed with the connecting hamza, since what follows it now has a vowel. The omission here is not according to analogy; it has occurred only in كُلْ, خُذْ and مُرْ.
(حَلَالًا): the object of كُلُوا, so مِنْ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (كُلُوا), and it is for the beginning of the extent.
It is also possible for مِنْ to be attached to something omitted, being a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (حَلَالًا); the implied form is: "eat what is lawful from what is on the earth", and when the adjective was placed first it became a ḥāl. As for (طَيِّبًا), it is an adjective (ṣifa) of حَلَالًا on the first view; and on the second view it is [also] an adjective of حَلَالًا, but its [proper] position is after the preposition and its genitive noun, so that the ḥāl and the one it describes (dhū al-ḥāl) are not separated by the adjective.
It is also possible for «مِمَّا» to be a ḥāl whose [proper] position is after طَيِّبًا, because they were originally adjectives and it was placed before the indefinite noun. On this view طَيِّبًا may be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being: "eat the lawful of what is on the earth, a good eating". It is also possible for حَلَالًا to be accusative (يَنْتَصِتَ [Translator's note: so in the source, evidently for يَنْتَصِبَ]) as a ḥāl from مَا, which then means "that which" (الَّذِي), with طَيِّبًا an adjective of the ḥāl. It is also possible for حَلَالًا to be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a lawful eating"; on this view the object of كُلُوا is omitted, i.e. "eat something" or "provision", and «مِنْ» is an adjective of the omitted element. According to the school of al-Akhfash, مِنْ may be redundant (zāʾida).
(خُطُوَاتِ): it is read with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ, making the ḍamma follow the ḍamma (itbāʿ), and with sukūn on it for lightness; outside the Quran fatḥa on it is permissible. It was read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, with the wāw pronounced as hamza because it is adjacent to the ḍamma, and this is weak. And it is read irregularly with fatḥa on the khāʾ and the ṭāʾ, on the basis that the singular is خَطْوَةٌ. الْخَطْوَةُ with fatḥa is the maṣdar of خَطَوَاتٍ [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably the maṣdar of خَطَوْتُ "I stepped" is meant], and with ḍamma [الْخُطْوَةُ] it is what is between the two feet. It is also said that they are two dialectal forms with one meaning.
(إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ): the hamza was given kasra only because the intention was to declare his state, and this is more forceful than fatḥa, because if the hamza were given fatḥa the implied form would become: "do not follow him because he is to you [an enemy]", whereas following him is forbidden even if he were not an enemy to us.
Like it is: لَبَّيْكَ، إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ لَكَ ("Here I am at Your service; indeed praise is Yours"): kasra on the hamza is better, because the kasra indicates that He deserves praise in every state; and likewise [it serves as] an alert.
الشَّيْطَانُ here denotes the genus; what is meant by it is not a single one.

ukberi-tibyan:169-169.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّمَا يَأْمُرُكُمْ بِالسُّوءِ وَالْفَحْشَاءِ وَأَنْ تَقُولُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ (١٦٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَنْ تَقُولُوا): in the position of the genitive, conjoined to بِالسُّوءِ, i.e. "and to your saying" (وَبِأَنْ تَقُولُوا).

ukberi-tibyan:170-170.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اتَّبِعُوا مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ قَالُوا بَلْ نَتَّبِعُ مَا أَلْفَيْنَا عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَنَا أَوَلَوْ كَانَ آبَاؤُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ (١٧٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: بَلْ نَتَّبِعُ: بَلْ here is for turning away (iḍrāb) from the first [statement], i.e. "we will not follow what Allah has sent down"; it is not a departure from one story to another.
And (أَلْفَيْنَا) means "we found" (وَجَدْنَا), transitive to one object; it may also be transitive to two objects, like وَجَدْتُ, and here it admits both. The first object is آبَاءَنَا, and عَلَيْهِ is either a ḥāl (circumstantial) or a second object. The final radical (lām) of أَلْفَيْنَا is a wāw, because the rule for final radicals whose origin is unknown is that they be wāw [Translator's note: the source reads فِيمَا لَوْ جَهِلَ, evidently for فِيمَا جُهِلَ]. (أَوَلَوْ): the wāw is for conjunction and the hamza is interrogative with the sense of rebuke; the apodosis (jawāb) of لَوْ is omitted, its implied form being: "would they then follow them?"

ukberi-tibyan:171-171.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي يَنْعِقُ بِمَا لَا يَسْمَعُ إِلَّا دُعَاءً وَنِدَاءً صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ فَهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ (١٧١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): مَثَلُ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي يَنْعِقُ) is its khabar (predicate). There is an omitted muḍāf in the speech, its implied form being: "the caller of those who disbelieve", i.e. "the likeness of the one who calls them to guidance is like the likeness of the one who shouts at sheep". This was implied only so that the comparison would be sound: so the caller of those who disbelieve (فَادَّعَى [Translator's note: so in the source, evidently for فَدَاعِي]) is like the one shouting at the sheep, and the likeness of those who disbelieve is like the sheep that are shouted at. Sībawayh said: since He intended to compare the disbelievers and their caller to the sheep and their caller, He set one of the two things against the other without detailing it, relying on the meaning being understood.
It is also said that the implied form is: "the likeness of those who disbelieve, in your calling them".
And it is said that the implied form is: "the likeness of the disbelievers in their calling upon the idols is like the likeness of the one who shouts at sheep".
(إِلَّا دُعَاءً): accusative governed by (يَسْمَعُ); the governing word before إِلَّا has been left free (furrigha) [i.e. it has no other object, so it governs what follows إِلَّا].
It is also said that إِلَّا is redundant (zāʾida), since the meaning is "it does not hear a call"; this is weak. The meaning is: "at what hears nothing but a sound". (صُمٌّ): i.e. "they are deaf".

ukberi-tibyan:172-172.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُلُوا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ (١٧٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كُلُوا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ): the object is omitted, i.e. "eat your provision"; and according to al-Akhfash مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida).

ukberi-tibyan:173-173.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةَ وَالدَّمَ وَلَحْمَ الْخِنْزِيرِ وَمَا أُهِلَّ بِهِ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ بَاغٍ وَلَا عَادٍ فَلَا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (١٧٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةَ): الْمَيْتَةَ is read in the accusative, in which case مَا here is the restraining (kāffa) مَا, and the agent is Allah.
It is also read in the nominative, on the basis that مَا means "that which" (الَّذِي) and الْمَيْتَةُ is the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ, the referent pronoun being omitted, its implied form being: "[that which] Allah has forbidden". It is also read حُرِّمَ in the passive (for that whose agent is not named); on this reading «مَا» may mean "that which", with الْمَيْتَةُ the khabar of إِنَّ; or it may be the restraining مَا, with الْمَيْتَةُ the object standing in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)).
The original is الْمَيِّتَةُ with doubling, because its pattern is fayʿila, and the original is مَيْوِتَةٌ; when the yāʾ and the wāw came together and the first of them was preceded [Translator's note: i.e. came first] with sukūn, the wāw was changed to yāʾ and assimilated. Whoever reads with doubling gives it according to the original, and whoever lightens it has dropped the wāw, which is the middle radical (ʿayn); like it are سَيْدٌ and هَيْنٌ for سَيِّدٌ and هَيِّنٌ.
The final radical (lām) of (وَالدَّمَ) is an omitted yāʾ, dropped without a [phonological] cause.
The nūn in (خِنْزِيرٍ) is original, and it is on an unusual pattern. It is also said that it is additional, the word being taken from الْخَزَرُ (narrowness of the eyes). (فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ): مَنْ is in the position of the nominative, and it is conditional; اضْطُرَّ is in the position of the jussive by it, and the apodosis (jawāb) is «فَلَا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ». It is also possible for مَنْ to mean "the one who" (الَّذِي).
It is read with kasra on the nūn [فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ], according to the basic rule for the meeting of two quiescent letters, and with ḍamma on it [فَمَنُ اضْطُرَّ], following the ḍamma of the ṭāʾ, since the intervening letter is not a strong barrier, being quiescent. The ṭāʾ has ḍamma according to the original, because the original is اضْطُرِرَ.
It is also read with kasra on the ṭāʾ [اضْطِرَّ], and its justification is that the kasra of the rāʾ was transferred to it.
(غَيْرَ بَاغٍ): accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(وَلَا عَادٍ): conjoined to بَاغٍ; and had it come outside the Quran in the accusative, conjoined to the position of غَيْرَ, it would be permissible.

ukberi-tibyan:245-245.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا فَيُضَاعِفَهُ لَهُ أَضْعَافًا كَثِيرَةً وَاللَّهُ يَقْبِضُ وَيَبْسُطُ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ (٢٤٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي): مَنْ is interrogative, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); ذَا is its khabar (predicate), and الَّذِي is a naʿt (adjective) of ذَا, or a badal (substitute) of it.
And (يُقْرِضُ) is the ṣila (relative clause) of الَّذِي. It is not permissible for (مَنْ) and (ذَا) to be treated as a single noun, as "مَاذَا" was, because "مَا" is more vague than "مَنْ", since مَنْ is for rational beings. Its like is (مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ). Al-qarḍ is a noun of the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar); the maṣdar (verbal noun) in reality is al-iqrāḍ.
It is also possible that al-qarḍ here is in the sense of the thing lent, like al-khalq in the sense of al-makhlūq (the created), so it would be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «[Translator's note: the text reads «الْمُقْرِضِ» (the lender); the sense of the argument requires «الْمُقْرَض» (the thing lent), and it is translated accordingly.]» And (حَسَنًا): it may be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being: "who is it that will lend Allah wealth, a goodly lending?"
It may also be an adjective of the wealth, and it would then be in the sense of "wholesome" or "abundant".
(فَيُضَاعِفَهُ): it is read in the nominative, conjoined to يُقْرِضُ, or as resumption, i.e. "then Allah multiplies it".
It is also read in the accusative, and there are two views on it. The first: that it is conjoined in meaning to the maṣdar of يُقْرِضُ, and that is only valid by implying أَنْ, so that it becomes a maṣdar conjoined to a maṣdar, its implied form being: "who is it from whom there will be a loan, and then a multiplication from Allah?"
The second view: that it is the answer to the interrogative according to the meaning, because what is asked about, although it is the lender in wording, concerns the lending in meaning; so it is as if He said: "Will anyone lend Allah, so that He multiplies it?" It is not permissible for it to be the answer to the interrogative according to the wording, because what is asked about in the wording is the lender, not the loan.
If it is said: why is it not conjoined to the maṣdar that is قَرْضًا, just as a verb is conjoined to a maṣdar by implying أَنْ, as in the poet's saying:
لَلُبْسُ عَبَاءَةٍ وَتَقَرُّ عَيْنِي.
(Wearing a coarse cloak while my eye is content [is dearer to me…].)
The reply is: this is not valid for two reasons. The first: قَرْضًا here is an emphatic maṣdar, and the emphatic maṣdar is not construed as أَنْ plus the verb.
The second: conjoining it to it would require it to be governed by يُقْرِضُ, and this is not valid in meaning, because the multiplication is not something lent; rather it is an act of Allah.
It is also read يُضَعِّفُهُ with shadda and without alif, and (yuḍāʿifuhu) without shadda and with alif; their meaning is one, and the shadda may be for intensification.
And يُضَاعِفُ is from the mufāʿala that occurs from one party, as we mentioned regarding حَافِظُوا.
And (أَضْعَافًا) is the plural of ḍiʿf; the ḍiʿf is the thing itself (the concrete double), not the maṣdar; the maṣdar is al-iḍʿāf or al-muḍāʿafa. On this basis it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in يُضَاعِفُهُ.
It may also be a second object according to the meaning, because the meaning of يُضَاعِفُهُ is "He makes it into multiples".
It may also be the plural of ḍiʿf, where ḍiʿf is a noun placed in the position of the maṣdar, like al-ʿaṭāʾ; for it is a noun for the thing given, yet it has been used in the sense of giving (al-iʿṭāʾ). Al-Quṭāmī said:
أَكُفْرًا بَعْدَ رَدِّ الْمَوْتِ عَنِّي ... وَبَعْدَ عَطَائِكَ الْمِائَةَ الرِّتَاعَا.
(Ingratitude, after you warded death from me, and after your giving of the hundred grazing camels?)
So أَضْعَافًا would be in the accusative as a maṣdar. If it is said: then how is it pluralised? The reply is: because of the differing aspects of the multiplying, according to the difference in sincerity, the amount lent, and the differing kinds of reward. (وَيَبْسُطُ): it is read with sīn, which is the original, and with ṣād, by substituting it for the sīn so that it harmonises with the ṭāʾ in elevation (istiʿlāʾ).

ukberi-tibyan:246-246.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الْمَلَإِ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مُوسَى إِذْ قَالُوا لِنَبِيٍّ لَهُمُ ابْعَثْ لَنَا مَلِكًا نُقَاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ قَالَ هَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ إِنْ كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِتَالُ أَلَّا تُقَاتِلُوا قَالُوا وَمَا لَنَا أَلَّا نُقَاتِلَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَقَدْ أُخْرِجْنَا مِنْ دِيَارِنَا وَأَبْنَائِنَا فَلَمَّا كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقِتَالُ تَوَلَّوْا إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِنْهُمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالظَّالِمِينَ (٢٤٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ): مِنْ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted, because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "being from the Children of Israel". And (مِنْ بَعْدِ) is attached to the first preposition, or to what the first is attached to; the implied form is: "after the death of Moses". And (إِذْ) is a badal (substitute) of "بَعْدِ", because both are times. "نُقَاتِلْ": the majority read it with nūn, and the jussive is as the answer to the imperative. It has been read in the nominative in an anomalous (shādhdh) reading, as resumption; it has been read with yāʾ and the nominative, on the basis that it is an adjective of مَلِك; and it has been read with yāʾ and the jussive as well, as the answer. Its like is "فَهَبْ لِي مِنْ لَدُنْكَ وَلِيًّا يَرِثُنِي" in the nominative and the jussive. (عَسَيْتُمْ): the majority read it with fatḥa on the sīn, because it is on the pattern faʿala: you say ʿasā like ramā.
It is also read with kasra on it, and that is a dialect; the verb from it is ʿasiya like khashiya, and the active participle is ʿasin like ʿamin, as Ibn al-Aʿrābī reported. The khabar (predicate) of عَسَى is (أَلَّا تُقَاتِلُوا), and the condition is parenthetical between them.
(وَمَا لَنَا): مَا is interrogative, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and لَنَا is the khabar. The wāw entered to indicate the linking of this speech to what precedes it; had it been dropped, it could have been cut off from it. It is interrogative in wording and a disavowal (inkār) in meaning. (أَلَّا نُقَاتِلَ): its implied form is "in that we not fight", i.e. "in leaving off fighting"; so "فِي" is attached to the notion of being settled (al-istiqrār), or to the preposition itself, and so أَنْ لَا نُقَاتِلَ is in the position of the accusative according to Sībawayh, and of the genitive according to al-Khalīl. Al-Akhfash said: أَنْ is redundant (zāʾida), and the clause is a ḥāl, its implied form being: "what is with us, not fighting?", like His saying (مَا لَكَ لَا تَأْمَنَّا); and he made "أَنْ" operative although it is redundant.
(وَقَدْ أُخْرِجْنَا): a clause in the position of a ḥāl, and the governing word is نُقَاتِلُ.
(وَأَبْنَائِنَا): conjoined to دِيَارِنَا, and in it there is omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being: "and from among our sons".

ukberi-tibyan:247-247.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَالَ لَهُمْ نَبِيُّهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ بَعَثَ لَكُمْ طَالُوتَ مَلِكًا قَالُوا أَنَّى يَكُونُ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ عَلَيْنَا وَنَحْنُ أَحَقُّ بِالْمُلْكِ مِنْهُ وَلَمْ يُؤْتَ سَعَةً مِنَ الْمَالِ قَالَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفَاهُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَزَادَهُ بَسْطَةً فِي الْعِلْمِ وَالْجِسْمِ وَاللَّهُ يُؤْتِي مُلْكَهُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ (٢٤٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (طَالُوتَ): it is a foreign, definite name; for that reason it is a diptote. It is not derived from al-ṭūl (height), just as Isḥāq is not derived from al-saḥq; these are only words that resemble Arabic words.
And (مَلِكًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). And (أَنَّى) is in the sense of "where" or in the sense of "how", and its position is accusative as a ḥāl of al-mulk (the kingship); the governing word in it is «يَكُونُ». Neither of the two adverbial phrases governs it, because each is an abstract (maʿnawī) governor, so the ḥāl cannot precede it. And (يَكُونُ) may be the incomplete (nāqiṣa) kāna, so that the khabar (predicate) is «لَهُ»,
and «عَلَيْنَا» is a ḥāl of al-mulk, the governing word in it being يَكُونُ or the khabar. It is also possible that the khabar is عَلَيْنَا, and لَهُ is a ḥāl. It may also be the complete (tāmma) kāna, so that لَهُ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يَكُونُ, and عَلَيْنَا is a ḥāl, the governing word in it being يَكُونُ.
(وَنَحْنُ أَحَقُّ): in the position of a ḥāl, and the yāʾ and مِنْ are attached to أَحَقّ. «[Translator's note: «الْيَاءُ» is presumably a misprint for «الْبَاءُ» (the bāʾ of بِالْمُلْكِ).]»
The original of al-saʿa is wasaʿa, with fatḥa on the wāw; its due in the original is kasra. It was dropped in the maṣdar only because it was dropped in the imperfect, and its original in the imperfect is kasra, which is your saying yasaʿu; were it not for that, it would not have been dropped, just as it was not dropped in yawjalu and nawjalu. It was given fatḥa only because of the guttural letter, so the fatḥa is incidental, and the rule of the kasra was applied to it; then it was made fatḥa in the maṣdar to agree with the verb. What shows you this is that in your saying waʿada yaʿidu, its maṣdar is ʿida with kasra, since it came out on its original. «[Translator's note: as printed, the passage says the wāw is the original with fatḥa while its due is kasra; the intended point is that the vowel after the dropped wāw (the sīn) is properly a kasra, made fatḥa because of the guttural ʿayn. The text also prints «يَعِدُّ» with shadda.]»
And (مِنَ الْمَالِ) is a naʿt (adjective) of al-saʿa. (فِي الْعِلْمِ): it may be an adjective of al-basṭa, or it may be attached to it.
And (وَاسِعٌ): it has been said that it is in the sense of attribution (nasab), i.e. "He is possessor of vastness".
It has also been said: it came with the omission of the augment, the original being awsaʿa, so He is muwassiʿ.
And it has been said: it is the active participle (fāʿil) of wasiʿa; so the implied form on this view is "vast in forbearance", because you say "His forbearance encompassed us (wasiʿanā ḥilmuhu)".

ukberi-tibyan:248-248.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَالَ لَهُمْ نَبِيُّهُمْ إِنَّ آيَةَ مُلْكِهِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَكُمُ التَّابُوتُ فِيهِ سَكِينَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَبَقِيَّةٌ مِمَّا تَرَكَ آلُ مُوسَى وَآلُ هَارُونَ تَحْمِلُهُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ (٢٤٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ يَأْتِيَكُمُ): the khabar (predicate) of «أَنْ». «[Translator's note: i.e. of إِنَّ.]»
The tāʾ in (التَّابُوتُ) is radical, and its pattern is fāʿūl; no derivation of it is known. There is another dialectal form of it, al-tābūh, with hāʾ, and it has been read with it anomalously (shādhdh); so the two may be two dialectal forms, or the hāʾ may be a substitute for the tāʾ.
If it is said: why can it not be faʿlūt from tāba yatūbu (to repent)?
The reply is: the meaning does not support it, and derivation is only made when the meaning is sound.
(فِيهِ سَكِينَةٌ): the clause is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise «تَحْمِلُهُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ».
And (مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ) is a naʿt (adjective) of al-sakīna. And (مِمَّا تَرَكَ) is a naʿt of بَقِيَّة.
The original of (بَقِيَّةٌ) is baqyiya, and the final radical of the word is yāʾ. There is no proof in baqiya, because of the kasra before it; do you not see that shaqiya is originally from wāw?

ukberi-tibyan:249-249.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَلَمَّا فَصَلَ طَالُوتُ بِالْجُنُودِ قَالَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مُبْتَلِيكُمْ بِنَهَرٍ فَمَنْ شَرِبَ مِنْهُ فَلَيْسَ مِنِّي وَمَنْ لَمْ يَطْعَمْهُ فَإِنَّهُ مِنِّي إِلَّا مَنِ اغْتَرَفَ غُرْفَةً بِيَدِهِ فَشَرِبُوا مِنْهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِنْهُمْ فَلَمَّا جَاوَزَهُ هُوَ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ قَالُوا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا الْيَوْمَ بِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِ قَالَ الَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُمْ مُلَاقُو اللَّهِ كَمْ مِنْ فِئَةٍ قَلِيلَةٍ غَلَبَتْ فِئَةً كَثِيرَةً بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ (٢٤٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِالْجُنُودِ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "he set out, and with him were the troops".
The yāʾ in (مُبْتَلِيكُمْ) is a substitute for a wāw, because it is from balāhu yablūhu (he tested him).
And (بِنَهَرٍ): with fatḥa on the hāʾ and with sukūn on it are two dialectal forms; the well-known reading has fatḥa, and Ḥumayd ibn Qays read it with sukūn. The root sense of al-nahr and al-nahār is breadth (ittisāʿ), and from it is "anhara al-dama" (he made the blood flow freely).
(إِلَّا مَنِ اغْتَرَفَ): an exception from the same genus, and its position is accusative. You have the choice: if you wish, make it an exception from the first «مَنِ», and if you wish, from the second «مَنِ». And اغْتَرَفَ is transitive.
And (غُرْفَةً) is with fatḥa on the ghayn and with ḍamma; it has been read with both, and they are two dialectal forms. On this basis al-ghurfa may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), or it may be the thing scooped. It has also been said: al-gharfa with fatḥa is the single act, and with ḍamma it is the amount the hand carries.
And (بِيَدِهِ) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) اغْتَرَفَ; it may also be a naʿt (adjective) of al-ghurfa, and so be attached to something omitted.
(إِلَّا قَلِيلًا): accusative as an exception from an affirmative statement.
It has been read anomalously in the nominative, and we have mentioned its explanation in His saying, Exalted is He: «ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِنْكُمْ». The middle radical (ʿayn) of al-ṭāqa is wāw, because it is from al-ṭawq, which is ability; you say "ṭawwaqtuhu al-amra" (I made him able to bear the matter).
The khabar (predicate) of لَا is (لَنَا). It is not permissible for al-ṭāqa to govern (الْيَوْمَ) or «بِجَالُوتَ», since if that were so it would be given nunation; rather, what governs them is the notion of being settled (al-istiqrār). It is also possible that the khabar is بِجَالُوتَ, so it is attached to something omitted.
And (لَنَا) would then be a clarification (tabyīn) or an adjective of ṭāqa, and الْيَوْمَ is governed by al-istiqrār.
And Jālūt is like Ṭālūt. (كَمْ مِنْ فِئَةٍ): كَمْ here is khabariyya (declarative, of quantity), and its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject).
And (غَلَبَتْ) is its khabar, and مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida). It may also be in the position of the nominative as an adjective of كَمْ, as you say: "I have a hundred, of dirhams and dinars". The original of fiʾa is fayʾa, because it is from fāʾa yafīʾu, when one returns; so what is omitted is its middle radical. It has also been said: its original is fiʾwa, because it is from faʾawtu raʾsahu, when you split it; so the fiʾa is a section of people.
(بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, and the implied form is "with Allah's permission to them"; and if you wish, you may make it a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

ukberi-tibyan:250-250.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَمَّا بَرَزُوا لِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِ قَالُوا رَبَّنَا أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًا وَثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَنَا وَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ (٢٥٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِجَالُوتَ): the lām is attached to (mutaʿalliq) بَرَزُوا; it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "they went forth, heading for Jālūt".

ukberi-tibyan:251-251.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَهَزَمُوهُمْ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَقَتَلَ دَاوُدُ جَالُوتَ وَآتَاهُ اللَّهُ الْمُلْكَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَعَلَّمَهُ مِمَّا يَشَاءُ وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النَّاسَ بَعْضَهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ لَفَسَدَتِ الْأَرْضُ وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ (٢٥١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَهَزَمُوهُمْ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ): it is read with fatḥa on the dāl without alif, and it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its agent, and «النَّاسَ» is its object. And «بَعْضَهُمْ» is a badal (substitute) of النَّاس, a substitute of part for whole. It is also read دِفَاع (difāʿ), with kasra on the dāl and with alif; it may also be a maṣdar of dafaʿtu, or it may be a maṣdar of dāfaʿtu. (بِبَعْضٍ): it is the second object, to which the verb is made transitive by the preposition.

ukberi-tibyan:211-211.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (سَلْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ كَمْ آتَيْنَاهُمْ مِنْ آيَةٍ بَيِّنَةٍ وَمَنْ يُبَدِّلْ نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْهُ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ (٢١١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سَلْ): there are two dialectal forms of it, سَلْ and اسْأَلْ. The past tense of اسْأَلْ is سَأَلَ with the hamza, so in the imperative a connecting hamza was needed because of the sukūn of the sīn. On سَلْ there are two views: the first, that the vowel of the hamza was cast onto the sīn, so the connecting hamza was dispensed with because the sīn now had a vowel.
The second: that it is from سَالَ يَسَالُ [Translator's note: the printed text has «سَأَلَ يَسْأَلُ» with hamza, but the comparison with خَافَ يَخَافُ shows that the hamza-less form is meant], like خَافَ يَخَافُ, and that is a dialect in it.
There is a third dialectal form, اسَلْ, reported by al-Akhfash; its rationale is that he cast the vowel of the hamza onto the sīn and dropped the hamza, but took no account of the vowel because it is incidental, and therefore brought the connecting hamza, as they said لَحْمَر.
(كَمْ آتَيْنَاهُمْ): the clause is in the position of the accusative, because it is the second object of (سل); (سل) does not govern (كم), because it is interrogative. On the position of (كم) there are two views: the first, accusative, because it is the second object of (آتيناهم), the implied form being "was it twenty signs that We gave them?" The second: it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with (آتيناهم) as its khabar (predicate) and the referring pronoun omitted, the implied form being آتَيْنَاهُمُوهَا or آتَيْنَاهُمْ إِيَّاهَا; and this is weak according to Sībawayh.
And (مِنْ آيَةٍ): a tamyīz (specification) of (كم). When (كم) is separated from its specifier, it is best to bring (مِن).
(وَمَنْ يُبَدِّلْ): in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; the referring element is the pronoun in (يبدل). It has also been said: the referring pronoun is omitted, its implied form being "severe in punishment to him".

ukberi-tibyan:212-212.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (زُيِّنَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا وَيَسْخَرُونَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَالَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا فَوْقَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَاللَّهُ يَرْزُقُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ (٢١٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (زُيِّنَ): the tāʾ (of the feminine) was dropped only because of the separation between the verb and what it is predicated of (its nāʾib fāʿil), and because the femininity of (الحياة) is not real; and that is good when there is separation.
The pause is on (آمنوا). (وَالَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (فَوْقَهُمْ) its khabar (predicate).

ukberi-tibyan:213-213.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (كَانَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ النَّبِيِّينَ مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنْذِرِينَ وَأَنْزَلَ مَعَهُمُ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ فِيمَا اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ وَمَا اخْتَلَفَ فِيهِ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ أُوتُوهُ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ بَغْيًا بَيْنَهُمْ فَهَدَى اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لِمَا اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ مِنَ الْحَقِّ بِإِذْنِهِ وَاللَّهُ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ (٢١٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنْذِرِينَ): two ḥāls (circumstantial). (وَأَنْزَلَ مَعَهُمُ): «مَعَهُمْ» is in the position of a ḥāl of (الكتاب), i.e. "and He sent down the Book as a witness for them and a support". (الكتاب) is a genus, or a singular in place of a plural.
(وَبِالْحَقِّ): in the position of a ḥāl of (الكتاب), i.e. "comprising the truth and blended with the truth". (لِيَحْكُمَ): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (أنزل), and the agent of (يَحْكُمُ) is Allah; it may also be (الكتاب).
(مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْهُمُ): (من) is attached to (اختلف), and (إلا) does not prevent that, as you say "none stood except Zayd on Friday". And (بَغْيًا): a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose), governed by (اختلف).
(مِنَ الْحَقِّ) is in the position of a ḥāl of the hāʾ in «فِيهِ»; it may also be a ḥāl of (ما).
(بِإِذْنِهِ): a ḥāl of (الذين آمنوا), i.e. "being permitted".
It may also be an object of (هدى), i.e. "He guided them by His command".

ukberi-tibyan:214-214.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَنْ تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ وَلَمَّا يَأْتِكُمْ مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ مَسَّتْهُمُ الْبَأْسَاءُ وَالضَّرَّاءُ وَزُلْزِلُوا حَتَّى يَقُولَ الرَّسُولُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ مَتَى نَصْرُ اللَّهِ أَلَا إِنَّ نَصْرَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ (٢١٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ): (أم) is equivalent to (بل) plus the hamza, so it is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) أم.
And (أَنْ تَدْخُلُوا): (أن) together with what it governs takes the place of the two objects according to Sībawayh.
According to al-Akhfash the second object is omitted. (وَلَمَّا) here is (لم) with «مَا» added to it, its jussive effect remaining.
(مَسَّتْهُمُ): a resumptive clause with no grammatical position, explaining their circumstances.
You may also imply (قد) with it, so that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(حَتَّى يَقُولَ الرَّسُولُ): read in the accusative, the implied form being "until the Messenger says", so it is an end-limit. The verb here is future in form, relating their situation, while the meaning is past, the implied form being "until the Messenger said". It is also read in the nominative (حَتَّى يَقُولُ), the implied form being "and they were shaken, so the Messenger said"; the shaking was the cause of the saying, and both verbs are past, so (حتى) does not govern it.
(مَتَى نَصْرُ اللَّهِ): the clause and what follows it are in the position of the accusative governed by the saying. There is concision in this speech; its detail is that the followers of the Messenger said "When is the help of Allah?", and the Messenger said "Indeed the help of Allah is near". The position of (متى) is nominative, because it is the khabar (predicate) of the maṣdar (verbal noun); according to al-Akhfash its position is accusative as an adverbial, and (نصر) is nominative by it.

ukberi-tibyan:215-215.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَا يُنْفِقُونَ قُلْ مَا أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَلِلْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ وَالْيَتَامَى وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ وَمَا تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِهِ عَلِيمٌ (٢١٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَسْأَلُونَكَ): you may cast the vowel of the hamza onto the sīn and drop it (يَسَلُونَكَ); and whoever says سَالَ, making it an alif substituted from [the hamza], would say يَسَالُونَكَ, like يَخَافُونَكَ. [Translator's note: the printed text here is defective: «ومن قال سأل فجعلها ألفا مبدلة من ولو قال يسألونك مثل يخافونك»; it has been rendered according to the evident sense.] (مَاذَا يُنْفِقُونَ): the Arabs have two ways with (ماذا). The first: to make (ما) interrogative, meaning "what thing", and (ذا) meaning "the one which" (الذي), with (ينفقون) its ṣila (relative clause) and the referring pronoun omitted; so (ما) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (ذا) with its ṣila is the khabar (predicate). According to the Basrans, (ذا) is made to mean (الذي) only with «مَا»; the Kufans allowed that with other than (ما).
The second way: to make «مَا» and «ذَا» one interrogative noun; its position here is accusative, governed by (ينفقون), and the position of the clause is accusative, governed by (يسألون), on both views.
(مَا أَنْفَقْتُمْ): «مَا» is conditional, in the position of the accusative governed by the verb after it.
And (مِنْ خَيْرٍ): its i'rab has been given before. (فَلِلْوَالِدَيْنِ) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (ما) may also mean "that which", and so be a mubtadaʾ, the referring pronoun being omitted, with (من خير) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted pronoun and (فللوالدين) the khabar. As for «وَمَا تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ», it is conditional without any doubt.

ukberi-tibyan:216-216.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِتَالُ وَهُوَ كُرْهٌ لَكُمْ وَعَسَى أَنْ تَكْرَهُوا شَيْئًا وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ وَعَسَى أَنْ تُحِبُّوا شَيْئًا وَهُوَ شَرٌّ لَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ وَأَنْتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ (٣١٦)). [Translator's note: the verse number is printed as ٣١٦; it is verse 216.]
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَهُوَ كُرْهٌ لَكُمْ): the clause is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); it has also been said: in the position of an adjective. It is read with ḍamma and with fatḥa on the kāf (كَرْه), and they are two dialectal forms with one meaning.
It has also been said: the fatḥa means "aversion", so it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and the ḍamma is the noun of the maṣdar.
It has also been said: the ḍamma means "hardship". Or, if it is a maṣdar, the meaning may be "fighting has been prescribed, as a compulsion upon you", so that (هو) refers to the prescribing and the writing; it may also refer to the fighting, so that (الكره) means "what is disliked".
(وَعَسَى أَنْ تَكْرَهُوا): (أن) and the verb are in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of (عَسَى), and there is no pronoun in (عسى). (وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ): a clause in the position of the accusative; it may be an adjective of (شيء), the entry of the wāw being acceptable because the form of the clause here is like its form when it is a ḥāl. It may also be a ḥāl of the indefinite noun, because the meaning requires it.

ukberi-tibyan:217-217.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الشَّهْرِ الْحَرَامِ قِتَالٍ فِيهِ قُلْ قِتَالٌ فِيهِ كَبِيرٌ وَصَدٌّ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَكُفْرٌ بِهِ وَالْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ وَإِخْرَاجُ أَهْلِهِ مِنْهُ أَكْبَرُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَالْفِتْنَةُ أَكْبَرُ مِنَ الْقَتْلِ وَلَا يَزَالُونَ يُقَاتِلُونَكُمْ حَتَّى يَرُدُّوكُمْ عَنْ دِينِكُمْ إِنِ اسْتَطَاعُوا وَمَنْ يَرْتَدِدْ مِنْكُمْ عَنْ دِينِهِ فَيَمُتْ وَهُوَ كَافِرٌ فَأُولَئِكَ حَبِطَتْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ وَأُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ (٢١٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قِتَالٍ فِيهِ): it is a badal (substitute) of (الشهر), a substitute of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), because the fighting occurs in the month. Al-Kisāʾī said: it is genitive by repetition, meaning that the implied form is "about fighting in it"; and that is the meaning of al-Farrāʾ's statement, since he said: it is genitive by an implied (عن). This is very weak, because a preposition's effect does not remain after it is omitted in normal (non-poetic) usage.
Abū ʿUbayda said: it is genitive by proximity (ʿalā al-jiwār); and this is further off than the view of those two, because proximity belongs to the cases of poetic necessity and irregularity, and nothing is construed on it when there is a way to avoid it.
(فيه) may be a naʿt (adjective) of (قتال), and it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to it, as it would be attached to (قاتِل).
It has been read in the nominative (قِتَالٌ) in an irregular (shādhdh) reading; its rationale is that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject) accompanied by the interrogative hamza, its implied form being "is fighting in it permissible?"
(قُلْ قِتَالٌ فِيهِ كَبِيرٌ): mubtadaʾ and khabar; beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted because it has been described by His saying (فيه).
If it is said: when an indefinite noun is repeated, it is repeated with the definite article, as in His saying (فَعَصَى فِرْعَوْنُ الرَّسُولَ) — the reply is: what is meant is not to declare grave the particular fighting mentioned and asked about, so that it would be repeated with the article; rather what is meant is to declare grave any fighting whatsoever in the sacred month. On this view the second (قتال) is other than the first.
(وَصَدٌّ): a mubtadaʾ. And (عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): an adjective of it, or attached to it. (وَكُفْرٌ): conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (صد). (وَإِخْرَاجُ أَهْلِهِ): also conjoined, and the khabar of the three nouns is (أَكْبَرُ).
It has also been said: the khabar of (صد) and (كفر) is omitted, the khabar of (إخراج أهله) sufficing for it. On this view the omitted word must be (أكبر), not (كبير) as some have supplied it, because that would require that expelling the people of the Mosque from it be greater than disbelief, which is not so.
As for the genitive of (الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ), it has been said: it is conjoined to (الشهر الحرام). This has been judged weak on the grounds that the people did not ask about the Sacred Mosque, since they had no doubt about its sanctity; they only asked about fighting in the sacred month, because it had occurred on their part without their realising that the month had begun, so they feared sin; and the idolaters had reproached them for it. It has also been said: it is conjoined to the hāʾ in (به), but this is not permissible according to the Basrans unless the preposition is repeated.
It has also been said: it is conjoined to (السبيل); this is not permissible, because that is governed by the maṣdar (verbal noun), and the conjunction with His saying «وَكُفْرٌ بِهِ» would separate the ṣila from what it belongs to. The good view is that it is attached to an omitted verb indicated by (الصد), its implied form being "and they turn (people) away from the Mosque", as Allah the Exalted said: (هُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوكُمْ عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ).
(حَتَّى يَرُدُّوكُمْ): (حتى) may mean "so that" (كي), and it may mean "until" (إلى); on both views it is attached to (يقاتلونكم). The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of (إِنِ اسْتَطَاعُوا) is omitted, «وَلَا يَزَالُونَ» standing in its place.
(فَيَمُتْ): conjoined to (يرتدد). (يرتدد) is pronounced without assimilation: since the second dāl was given sukūn, the first could not be given sukūn, lest two quiescent letters meet. In Arabic it may also be يَرْتَدّ; it has been read both ways in al-Māʾida, and there the two readings will be explained, if Allah wills.
(منكم) is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the latent agent.
«وَمَنْ» is in the position of a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is the clause, namely His saying (فَأُولَئِكَ حَبِطَتْ).

ukberi-tibyan:282-282.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا تَدَايَنْتُمْ بِدَيْنٍ إِلَى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى فَاكْتُبُوهُ وَلْيَكْتُبْ بَيْنَكُمْ كَاتِبٌ بِالْعَدْلِ وَلَا يَأْبَ كَاتِبٌ أَنْ يَكْتُبَ كَمَا عَلَّمَهُ اللَّهُ فَلْيَكْتُبْ وَلْيُمْلِلِ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِ الْحَقُّ وَلْيَتَّقِ اللَّهَ رَبَّهُ وَلَا يَبْخَسْ مِنْهُ شَيْئًا فَإِنْ كَانَ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِ الْحَقُّ سَفِيهًا أَوْ ضَعِيفًا أَوْ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ يُمِلَّ هُوَ فَلْيُمْلِلْ وَلِيُّهُ بِالْعَدْلِ وَاسْتَشْهِدُوا شَهِيدَيْنِ مِنْ رِجَالِكُمْ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُونَا رَجُلَيْنِ فَرَجُلٌ وَامْرَأَتَانِ مِمَّنْ تَرْضَوْنَ مِنَ الشُّهَدَاءِ أَنْ تَضِلَّ إِحْدَاهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَاهُمَا الْأُخْرَى وَلَا يَأْبَ الشُّهَدَاءُ إِذَا مَا دُعُوا وَلَا تَسْأَمُوا أَنْ تَكْتُبُوهُ صَغِيرًا أَوْ كَبِيرًا إِلَى أَجَلِهِ ذَلِكُمْ أَقْسَطُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَأَقْوَمُ لِلشَّهَادَةِ وَأَدْنَى أَلَّا تَرْتَابُوا إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ تِجَارَةً حَاضِرَةً تُدِيرُونَهَا بَيْنَكُمْ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَلَّا تَكْتُبُوهَا وَأَشْهِدُوا إِذَا تَبَايَعْتُمْ وَلَا يُضَارَّ كَاتِبٌ وَلَا شَهِيدٌ وَإِنْ تَفْعَلُوا فَإِنَّهُ فُسُوقٌ بِكُمْ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ (٢٨٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَى أَجَلٍ): it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to تداينتم, and it may be a naʿt (adjective) of دين, i.e. deferred and postponed.
The alif of (مُسَمًّى) is converted from a yāʾ; and likewise every alif occurring in fourth position or beyond, when it is a converted one, is converted from a yāʾ — then one looks into the origin of the yāʾ.
(بِالْعَدْلِ): attached to His saying «وليكتب», i.e. let him write with the truth. So it may be [Translator's note: a word appears to be missing here in the text, presumably "a ḥāl (circumstantial)"], i.e. "and let him write, being just"; and it may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "because of justice". It has been said that the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), the implied form being: "and let him write justice".
It has also been said that it is attached to كاتب, i.e. a scribe described by justice, or [one who is] chosen.
(كَمَا عَلَّمَهُ اللَّهُ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), and it belongs to the completion of أن يكتب.
It has also been said that it is attached to His saying «فليكتب», the speech having been completed at His saying أن يكتب, the implied form being: "so let him write as Allah has taught him".
(وَلْيُمْلِلِ): the past of this verb is أَمَلَّ, and there is another dialectal form, أَمْلَى, from which is His saying: (فَهِيَ تُمْلَى عَلَيْهِ); there is discussion of it that will come in its place, if Allah wills.
(مِنْهُ شَيْئًا): من may be attached to يبخس, and it is then for the starting point of the diminishing.
And the implied form may be: شيئًا منه; when it was placed first it became a ḥāl (circumstantial). The hāʾ refers to the right (al-ḥaqq).
(أَنْ يُمِلَّ): «هو» here is tawkīd (emphasis), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (muḍmar). The majority read it with ḍamma on the hāʾ, because it is a word detached from what precedes it, so it is started with.
It has been read with sukūn on it, on the basis that he treated the detached [word] like that joined to wāw, fāʾ or lām, as in وَهْوَ, فَهْوَ, لَهْوَ. (بِالْعَدْلِ): like the first one. (مِنْ رِجَالِكُمْ): it may be a naʿt of شهيدين, and it may be attached to استشهدوا.
(فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُونَا): the alif is the pronoun of the two witnesses.
(فَرَجُلٌ): the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "then the one called to witness is a man and two women". It has been said that it is a fāʿil, i.e. "then let a man be called to witness". And it has been said that the khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "a man and two women [shall] witness".
Had it been read in the accusative, the implied form would have been: "then call to witness".
It has been read, among the irregular (shādhdh) readings, وامرأْتان with a quiescent hamza. Its justification is that he lightened the hamza, so it came close to the alif, and that which is brought close to the alif takes its ruling — which is why it is not started with. Then, when it had become like the alif, he turned it into a quiescent hamza, just as they said خأْتم and عأْلم.
Ibn Jinnī said: It is not permissible [to say] that he made the hamza quiescent, because a vowel bearing fatḥa is not made quiescent, owing to the lightness of the fatḥa. If it were said that he made the hamza quiescent because of a succession of vowels — and a succession of vowels is avoided even if the vowel is a fatḥa, just as they made the bāʾ of ضربْتَ quiescent — it would be good. (مِمَّنْ تَرْضَوْنَ): it is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of رجل and امرأتان, its implied sense being "approved ones".
It has been said that it is a naʿt of شهيدين, but that is weak because of the separation occurring between them.
It has also been said that it is a badal (substitute) from «من رجالكم». The origin of ترضون is ترضَوُون, because the final radical (lām) of الرضا is wāw, from your saying الرضوان.
(مِنَ الشُّهَدَاءِ): it may be a ḥāl from the omitted pronoun, i.e. "whom you approve as being among the witnesses"; and it may be a badal from «مَن».
(أَنْ تَضِلَّ): it is read with fatḥa on the hamza, on the basis that it is the maṣdar-forming [أن] that puts the verb in the subjunctive, and it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), its implied form being: "so that one of them goes astray". (فَتُذَكِّرَ): in the subjunctive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. If you say: the purpose of calling two women to witness along with the man is not that one of them should go astray, so how can it be supplied with the lām [of purpose]?
The answer is what Sībawayh said: this is speech construed according to the meaning. It is the habit of the Arabs to put first that in which lies the cause, and it is placed in the position of the effect, because it leads to it. Similar to it is your saying: "I prepared this beam that the wall should lean, so I prop it with it." It is known that you did not intend by preparing the beam that the wall should lean; the meaning is only "that I may prop the wall with it if it leans". So too is the verse: "so that one of them may remind the other if she goes astray", or "because of her going astray".
And it is not permissible for the implied form to be "for fear that she go astray", because فتذكر has been conjoined to it, so the meaning would become "for fear that one of them remind the other if she goes astray", and that is the reverse of what is intended.
(فَتُذَكِّرُ) is also read in the nominative, as a resumption (istiʾnāf). And (إِنْ) is read with kasra on the hamza, on the basis that it is conditional; the fatḥa of the lām [in تضلَّ] on this view is an indeclinable vowel (ḥarakat bināʾ) owing to the meeting of two quiescent letters, and فتذكر is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the verb being nominative because the fāʾ has entered the apodosis.
It is read with doubling of the kāf and without doubling; one says ذكّرتُه and أذكرتُه. «إحداهما» is the fāʿil and «الأخرى» the mafʿūl (object). The reverse is valid in meaning, except that it is barred in i'rab according to the apparent statement of the grammarians, because when the mark of declension does not appear on the fāʿil and the mafʿūl, they require the fāʿil to come first in every place where confusion is feared. On this basis, when confusion is ruled out, it is permissible to put the mafʿūl first, as in your saying كسر عيسى العصا ("Jesus broke the stick"). This verse is of that kind, because forgetting and reminding are not fixed on either one of them; rather it is indeterminate. It is known from His saying «فتذكر» that the one who reminds is the one who remembers, and the one who is reminded is the one who forgets — just as it is known from the word "broke" who is capable of breaking. On this basis it is permissible to make إحداهما the fāʿil and الأخرى the mafʿūl, and to reverse it.
If it is said: why did He not say فتذكّرها الأخرى? It is said: there are two views on this. The first: that He repeated the overt noun to indicate the indeterminacy in remembering and forgetting; had He used a pronoun, its referring back to the one mentioned would have been fixed. The second: that He put the overt noun in place of the pronoun, its implied form being فتذكّرها; and this indicates that the second إحداهما is a mafʿūl placed first, and it cannot be the fāʿil on this view, because the pronoun is the very same as the overt noun, and the first overt noun is the fāʿil of تضل; so if the pronoun were made to refer to that overt noun, the one who forgets would be the one who reminds, and that is absurd.
The second object of تذكر is omitted, its implied form being: "the testimony" and the like. Likewise the object of «يأب», its implied form being: "and let the witnesses not refuse giving testimony and taking on testimony".
(إِذَا) is an adverb (ẓarf) for يأب, and it may be an adverb for the omitted object.
(أَنْ تَكْتُبُوهُ) is in the position of the accusative by تسأموا; تسأموا is transitive by itself, and it has been said: by means of a preposition. (صَغِيرًا أَوْ كَبِيرًا): two ḥāls from the hāʾ.
(إِلَى) is attached to تكتبوه, and it may also be a ḥāl from the hāʾ.
(عِنْدَ اللَّهِ) is an adverb for أقسط. The lām in His saying (لِلشَّهَادَةِ) is attached to أقوم; the afʿal [elative] pattern operates on adverbs and prepositions. The wāw in «أقوم» remained sound just as it remained sound in the verb of wonder (fiʿl al-taʿajjub), because of its being frozen (jāmid) and treated like frozen nouns.
(أَقْوَمُ) may be from the transitive أقام, but the extra hamza was dropped and then the hamza of afʿal was brought, as in His saying, Exalted is He: (أَيُّ الْحِزْبَيْنِ أَحْصَى); the meaning would then be "more firm for your establishing of the testimony". And it may be from the intransitive قام, the meaning being "that is more firm for the standing of the testimony" — قامت الشهادة meaning "it was established". The alif of (أَدْنَى) is converted from a wāw, because it is from دنا يدنو.
(أَلَّا تَرْتَابُوا) is in the position of the accusative, its implied form being: "and nearer so that you not doubt", or "nearer to your not doubting". (تِجَارَةً): it is read in the nominative on the basis that تكون is the complete (tāmma) one, and (حَاضِرَةً) is its naʿt.
And it may be the deficient (nāqiṣa) one, its noun being تجارة, حاضرة its naʿt, «تديرونها» the khabar, and «بينكم» an adverb for تديرونها.
It has been read in the accusative on the basis that the noun of the agent [Translator's note: so in the text: «اسم الفاعل»; the sense requires "the noun of كان (ism kāna)"] is latent in it, its implied form being: "unless the transaction be trade". The excepted clause is in the position of the accusative because it is an exception from the same genus (istithnāʾ min al-jins), since He commanded calling witnesses in every dealing and excepted from it present trade; the implied form is: "except in the case of the trade being present".
The fāʾ entered «فليس» to signal that what follows it is connected to what precedes it.
(أَلَّا تَكْتُبُوهَا): its implied form is "in not writing it"; the disagreement over its position in i'rab has already been mentioned in more than one place.
(وَلَا يُضَارَّ كَاتِبٌ): there are various readings of it, which were mentioned at His saying (لَا تُضَارَّ وَالِدَةٌ). Here it has been read with sukūn on the rāʾ together with doubling, which is weak, because in its underlying form it combines three quiescent letters. Yet it has a justification: the alif, because of its length, is treated like a vowelled letter, so two quiescent letters remain, and pausing on it is possible; then he treated continuous speech like the pause, or he paused on it with a brief pause. This has occurred in rhymes. The hāʾ in (فَإِنَّهُ) refers to the refusal or the causing of harm. (بِكُمْ) is attached to an omitted [word], its implied form being: "attaching to you". (وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ اللَّهُ): resumptive, with no position.
It has been said that its position is a ḥāl from the fāʿil in اتقوا, its implied form being: "and fear Allah, being guaranteed instruction or guidance". It may also be an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara).

ukberi-tibyan:117-117.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (بَدِيعُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَإِذَا قَضَى أَمْرًا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ (١١٧)).
His saying, the Exalted: (بَدِيعُ السَّمَاوَاتِ): i.e. their Originator (مُبْدِعُهَا), as in their saying سَمِيعٌ in the sense of مُسْمِعٌ. The genitive construct here is pure (maḥḍa), because the originating of them is past.
(وَإِذَا قَضَى): إِذَا is an adverbial (ẓarf), and what governs it is what the answer indicates, its implied form being: "and when He decrees a matter, it comes to be".
His saying, the Exalted: (فَيَكُونُ): the majority read the nominative, by conjunction with يَقُولُ, or as a resumption, i.e. "then it comes to be". It was read with the accusative as the answer to the imperative form, and that is weak for two reasons.
The first: that كُنْ is not an imperative in reality, since there is no one addressed by it; rather the meaning is the swiftness of coming into being. What indicates this is that the address to come into being does not apply to what exists, because what exists has already come into being; nor does it apply to the non-existent, because it is not a thing. So nothing remains but the imperative form, and the imperative form occurs without the reality of a command being intended, as in His saying: (أَسْمِعْ بِهِمْ وَأَبْصِرْ) and His saying: (فَلْيَمْدُدْ لَهُ الرَّحْمَنُ).
The second reason: that the answer to an imperative must differ from the imperative, either in the verb or in the agent or in both. An example of that is your saying: "Go, and Zayd will benefit you (اذْهَبْ يَنْفَعُكَ زَيْدٌ)", where the verb and the agent in the answer are other than those in the imperative. You say: "Go, and Zayd will go (اذْهَبْ يَذْهَبْ زَيْدٌ)", where the two verbs agree and the two agents differ. You say: "Go, and you will benefit (اذْهَبْ تَنْتَفِعْ)", where the two agents agree and the two verbs differ. As for the two verbs and the two agents both agreeing, that is not permissible, as in your saying: "Go, and you will go (اذْهَبْ تَذْهَبْ)"; the reason for this is that a thing is not a condition for itself.

ukberi-tibyan:118-118.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ لَوْلَا يُكَلِّمُنَا اللَّهُ أَوْ تَأْتِينَا آيَةٌ كَذَلِكَ قَالَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ . . . . . . (١١٨)).
His saying, the Exalted: (لَوْلَا يُكَلِّمُنَا اللَّهُ): this لَوْلَا, when an imperfect comes after it, is for urging (taḥḍīḍ), and when a past comes after it, it is for rebuke (tawbīkh). In both its kinds it is restricted to the verb, because urging and rebuke apply only to a verb.
(كَذَلِكَ قَالَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ): whatever this place admits is carried over here from the i'rab of the first place.

ukberi-tibyan:119-119.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ بِالْحَقِّ بَشِيرًا وَنَذِيرًا وَلَا تُسْأَلُ عَنْ أَصْحَابِ الْجَحِيمِ (١١٩)).
His saying, the Exalted: (إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ بِالْحَقِّ): the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object, its implied form being: "We sent you with the truth accompanying you". It may also be a ḥāl from the agent, i.e. "with the truth accompanying Us". It may also be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "for the sake of establishing the truth". (بَشِيرًا وَنَذِيرًا): two ḥāls. (وَلَا تُسْأَلُ): whoever reads it with the nominative and a ḍamma on the tāʾ, its position is also a ḥāl, i.e. "and not being questioned"; it may also be resumptive. It is read with a fatḥa on the tāʾ and a ḍamma on the lām [i.e. تَسْأَلُ], and its ruling is the ruling of the reading before it.
It is also read with a fatḥa on the tāʾ and the jussive [i.e. وَلَا تَسْأَلْ], as a prohibition.

ukberi-tibyan:120-120.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَنْ تَرْضَى عَنْكَ الْيَهُودُ وَلَا النَّصَارَى حَتَّى تَتَّبِعَ مِلَّتَهُمْ قُلْ إِنَّ هُدَى اللَّهِ هُوَ الْهُدَى وَلَئِنِ اتَّبَعْتَ أَهْوَاءَهُمْ بَعْدَ الَّذِي جَاءَكَ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ مَا لَكَ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ وَلَا نَصِيرٍ (١٢٠)).
His saying, the Exalted: (هُوَ الْهُدَى): هُوَ may be a tawkīd (emphasis) of the noun of إِنَّ, a separating pronoun (faṣl), or a mubtadaʾ (subject); its parallel has preceded. مِنَ الْعِلْمِ [Translator's note: the source gives no separate heading here; this phrase begins a new comment] is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in جَاءَكَ.

ukberi-tibyan:121-121.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ يَتْلُونَهُ حَقَّ تِلَاوَتِهِ أُولَئِكَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ . . . . . (١٢١)).
His saying, the Exalted: (الَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ): (الَّذِينَ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and آتَيْنَاهُمْ is its ṣila (relative clause). (يَتْلُونَهُ) is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara) from هُمْ or from الْكِتَابَ, because at the time it was given they were not reciting it. And (حَقَّ) is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because it is originally an adjective of the recitation, the implied form being "a true recitation (تِلَاوَةً حَقًّا)"; when the adjective of a maṣdar is put first and put in construct with it, it takes the accusative of the maṣdar. It may also be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar. And (أُولَئِكَ) is a mubtadaʾ, (يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ) its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of الَّذِينَ. يَتْلُونَهُ cannot be the khabar of الَّذِينَ, because not everyone who was given the Book recited it as it truly should be recited, since the meaning of حَقَّ تِلَاوَتِهِ is acting upon it. It is also said that يَتْلُونَهُ is the khabar, and الَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمْ is general in wording but specific in what is meant, namely everyone of the People of the Book who believed in the Prophet; or by الْكِتَابَ the Quran is meant.

ukberi-tibyan:124-124.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذِ ابْتَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ رَبُّهُ بِكَلِمَاتٍ فَأَتَمَّهُنَّ قَالَ إِنِّي جَاعِلُكَ لِلنَّاسِ إِمَامًا قَالَ وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي قَالَ لَا يَنَالُ عَهْدِي الظَّالِمِينَ (١٢٤)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَإِذِ ابْتَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ): إِذْ is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "remember". The alif in ابْتَلَى is converted from a wāw; its origin is from بَلَا يَبْلُو [Translator's note: printed «بَلَى»] when one tests.
There are several dialectal forms of إِبْرَاهِيمَ. One is إِبْرَاهِيمُ with the alif and the yāʾ, which is the well-known one.
And «إِبْرَاهِمُ» is likewise, except that the yāʾ is dropped;
and إِبْرَاهَامُ with two alifs;
and إِبْرَاهُمُ with one alif and a ḍamma on the hāʾ; and it has been read in every one of these.
It is a definite foreign noun. Its plural is أَبَارِهُ according to some, and according to others بَرَاهِمُ; and أَبَارِهَةُ and بَرَاهِمَةُ have also been said for it.
His saying, the Exalted: (جَاعِلُكَ): it is transitive to two objects, because it is from جَعَلَ in the sense of صَيَّرَ ("to make into"). And (لِلنَّاسِ) may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to جَاعِلٌ, i.e. "for the sake of the people".
It may also be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the implied form being: "a leader for the people"; when He put it first, He made it accusative, as we have mentioned. (قَالَ وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي): the two objects are omitted, the implied form being: "make a party of my offspring leaders". (لَا يَنَالُ عَهْدِي الظَّالِمِينَ): this is the well-known reading, making الْعَهْدُ the agent. It is also read الظَّالِمُونَ, the reverse; and the two meanings are close, because what you have attained has attained you.

ukberi-tibyan:125-125.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ جَعَلْنَا الْبَيْتَ مَثَابَةً لِلنَّاسِ وَأَمْنًا وَاتَّخِذُوا مِنْ مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ مُصَلًّى وَعَهِدْنَا إِلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ أَنْ طَهِّرَا بَيْتِيَ لِلطَّائِفِينَ وَالْعَاكِفِينَ وَالرُّكَّعِ السُّجُودِ (١٢٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَإِذْ جَعَلْنَا): like «وَإِذِ ابْتَلَى».
And جَعَلَ here may be in the sense of صَيَّرَ ("to make into"); it may also be in the sense of خَلَقَ ("to create") or وَضَعَ ("to set"), in which case (مَثَابَةً) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). The original form of مَثَابَةٌ is مَثْوَبَةٌ [Translator's note: printed «مَثُوبَةٌ»], because it is from ثَابَ يَثُوبُ when one returns. And (لِلنَّاسِ) is an adjective of مَثَابَةً; it may also be attached (mutaʿalliq) to جَعَلْنَا, the implied form being: "for the sake of benefiting the people".
And (وَاتَّخِذُوا) is read in the form of a statement [i.e. وَاتَّخَذُوا], what it is conjoined to being omitted, its implied form being: "so they returned
and took".
It is read in the form of the imperative, and on this view it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf). And (مِنْ مَقَامِ): مِنْ may be partitive, i.e. "part of the station of Ibrāhīm as a place of prayer".
مِنْ may also be in the sense of فِي ("in"). It may also be redundant (zāʾida), according to the view of al-Akhfash. And (مُصَلًّى) is the object of اتَّخِذُوا; its alif is converted from a wāw, its pattern is مُفَعَّلٌ [Translator's note: printed «مُفْعَلٌ»], and it is a place, not a maṣdar (verbal noun). It may also be a maṣdar, with an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being "a place of مُصَلًّى", i.e. a place of prayer. And الْمَقَامُ is the place of standing; it is not a maṣdar here, because the standing of Ibrāhīm is not taken as a place of prayer.
(أَنْ طَهِّرَا): «أَنْ» here may be in the sense of أَيْ, the explicative (al-mufassira), because عَهِدْنَا means قُلْنَا ("We said"), and the explicative comes after "saying" and what is in its sense; on this view it has no grammatical position.
It may also be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), with the imperative as its ṣila (relative clause); this is among what may be a ṣila with أَنْ [Translator's note: printed «أَنَّ»] and not with the others. On this view the implied form is: "that they purify (بِأَنْ طَهِّرَا)", so its position is genitive or accusative, according to the disagreement between al-Khalīl and Sībawayh. And (السُّجُودِ) is the plural of سَاجِدٌ; it is also said that it is a maṣdar, with an omitted muḍāf in it, i.e. "those bowing, possessing prostration".

ukberi-tibyan:174-174.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْتُمُونَ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ وَيَشْتَرُونَ بِهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا أُولَئِكَ مَا يَأْكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ إِلَّا النَّارَ وَلَا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ اللَّهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَلَا يُزَكِّيهِمْ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (١٧٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنَ الْكِتَابِ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted referent pronoun, i.e. "what Allah sent down, being from the Book". And (إِلَّا النَّارَ) is the object of «يَأْكُلُونَ». (فِي بُطُونِهِمْ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from النَّارَ, its implied form being: "they eat nothing but fire, fixed — or being — in their bellies". It is preferable for the ḥāl to be an anticipated one (muqaddara), because at the time of eating it is not in their bellies; it only comes to be so. The best is for it to be an adverbial for يَأْكُلُونَ, with an omitted muḍāf implied in it, i.e. "into the passage of their bellies".
The first view entails placing the ḥāl before the particle of exception, which is weak — unless the object is made omitted, with فِي بُطُونِهِمْ a ḥāl from it or an adjective (ṣifa) of it, i.e. "[they eat] something in their bellies". This speech is, in meaning, figurative, while the i'rab follows the rule of the wording.

ukberi-tibyan:175-175.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلَالَةَ بِالْهُدَى وَالْعَذَابَ بِالْمَغْفِرَةِ فَمَا أَصْبَرَهُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ (١٧٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَمَا أَصْبَرَهُمْ): «مَا» is in the position of the nominative, and the speech is an exclamation of wonder (taʿajjub) by which Allah made the believers wonder. أَصْبَرَ is a verb containing the pronoun of the agent, which refers back to مَا.
It is also possible for مَا to be interrogative here, and its rule in i'rab is like its rule when it is exclamatory; it is an indefinite noun, not qualified by an adjective, complete in itself.
It is also said that it is negation, i.e. "Allah has not made them patient upon the Fire".

ukberi-tibyan:176-176.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ نَزَّلَ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ. . . . . . (١٧٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذَلِكَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ» is the khabar (predicate); the implied form is: "that punishment is deserved by what Allah sent down in the Quran concerning the disbeliever's deserving of punishment". So the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:177-177.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَيْسَ الْبِرَّ أَنْ تُوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ قِبَلَ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ وَلَكِنَّ الْبِرَّ مَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالْكِتَابِ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ وَآتَى الْمَالَ عَلَى حُبِّهِ ذَوِي الْقُرْبَى وَالْيَتَامَى وَالْمَسَاكِينَ وَابْنَ السَّبِيلِ وَالسَّائِلِينَ وَفِي الرِّقَابِ وَأَقَامَ الصَّلَاةَ وَآتَى الزَّكَاةَ وَالْمُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِهِمْ إِذَا عَاهَدُوا وَالصَّابِرِينَ فِي الْبَأْسَاءِ وَالضَّرَّاءِ وَحِينَ الْبَأْسِ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُتَّقُونَ (١٧٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَيْسَ الْبِرَّ): it is read with the rāʾ nominative [الْبِرُّ], in which case أَنْ تُوَلُّوا is the khabar (predicate) of لَيْسَ; this is strengthened by the fact that the basic order is for the agent to precede the object.
It is also read in the accusative, on the basis that it is the khabar of لَيْسَ and أَنْ تُوَلُّوا is its noun. This is strengthened, for those who read it, by the fact that (أَنْ تُوَلُّوا) is more definite than الْبِرّ, since it is like a pronoun in that it cannot be qualified by an adjective, whereas الْبِرّ can be qualified. For this reason the reading with the accusative was strengthened in His saying: (فَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِ).
(قِبَلَ الْمَشْرِقِ): an adverb of place. وَلَكِنَّ الْبِرَّ is read with the nūn doubled and الْبِرَّ in the accusative, and with the nūn lightened [وَلَكِنِ الْبِرُّ] and الْبِرُّ nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). There are three views on the implied form. The first: that الْبَرّ here is an active participle from بَرَّ يَبِرُّ ("to be pious"), its original being بَرِرٌ, like فَطِنٌ, and the kasra of the rāʾ was transferred to the bāʾ. It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a description, like عَدْلٌ, so that it became like a concrete entity.
The second view: that the implied form is: "but the possessor of piety is whoever believes".
The third view: that the implied form is: "but piety is the piety of whoever believes" — with the omission of the muḍāf on both [of these last] implied forms. This was needed only because الْبِرّ is a maṣdar while مَنْ آمَنَ is a concrete entity, so the khabar is other than the mubtadaʾ in meaning; hence something is implied by which the second becomes the same as the first.
(وَالْكِتَابِ): here it is singular in wording, so it may denote the genus; this is strengthened by its being originally a maṣdar. It may also be that the singular suffices for the plural while the plural is intended.
It may also be that the Quran is meant by it, because whoever believes in it has believed in all the Books, since it bears witness to their truth. (عَلَى حُبِّهِ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "he gave wealth while loving [it]". الْحُبُّ is the maṣdar of حَبَبْتُ, which is a dialectal variant of أَحْبَبْتُ; it may also be the maṣdar of أَحْبَبْتُ with the augment dropped; and it may be a noun standing for the maṣdar, which is الْإِحْبَابُ. The hāʾ is the pronoun of the wealth, or the pronoun of the name of Allah, or the pronoun of the giving (al-ītāʾ); on these three views the maṣdar is put in construct with its object. And (ذَوِي الْقُرْبَى) is accusative governed by آتَى, not by the maṣdar, because the maṣdar is transitive to one object and has already taken it in full. It is also possible for the hāʾ to be the pronoun of مَنْ, in which case the maṣdar is put in construct with its agent; on this view ذَوِي الْقُرْبَى may be the object of the maṣdar, or it may be the object of آتَى, with the object of the maṣdar omitted, its implied form being: "and he gave the wealth, despite his love of it, to the relatives".
(وَابْنَ السَّبِيلِ): singular in wording; it denotes the genus, or it is a singular in wording standing in place of the plural.
(وَفِي الرِّقَابِ): i.e. "in freeing the necks (slaves)", or "in manumitting the necks"; and «فِي» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to آتَى. (وَالْمُوفُونَ): there are three views on its being nominative. The first: that it is conjoined to مَنْ آمَنَ, the implied form being: "but piety is the believers and those who fulfil".
The second: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "and they are those who fulfil". On these two views «الصَّابِرِينَ» is accusative by an implied "I mean" (أَعْنِي); in meaning it is conjoined to مَنْ, but the accusative was permissible because the qualities were repeated. It is not permissible for it to be conjoined to ذَوِي الْقُرْبَى, lest the [element] conjoined to, which has the status of [part of] the ṣila (relative clause), be separated by something extraneous, namely "and they are those who fulfil".
The third view: that الْمُوفُونَ is conjoined to the pronoun in آمَنَ, the length of the speech taking the place of emphasizing the pronoun. On this view «الصَّابِرِينَ» may be accusative by an implied "I mean", or by conjunction to ذَوِي الْقُرْبَى, because on this view الْمُوفُونَ is included within the ṣila.
(وَحِينَ الْبَأْسِ): an adverb of time for الصَّابِرِينَ.

ukberi-tibyan:178-178.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِصَاصُ فِي الْقَتْلَى الْحُرُّ بِالْحُرِّ وَالْعَبْدُ بِالْعَبْدِ وَالْأُنْثَى بِالْأُنْثَى فَمَنْ عُفِيَ لَهُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ شَيْءٌ فَاتِّبَاعٌ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَأَدَاءٌ إِلَيْهِ بِإِحْسَانٍ ذَلِكَ تَخْفِيفٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَرَحْمَةٌ فَمَنِ اعْتَدَى بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَلَهُ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (١٧٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الْحُرُّ بِالْحُرِّ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the implied form is: "the free man is taken for the free man".
(فَمَنْ عُفِيَ لَهُ): مَنْ is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; it may be conditional, or it may mean "the one who" (الَّذِي). The khabar is (فَاتِّبَاعٌ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ), and the implied form is: "then upon him is a following".
And (مِنْ أَخِيهِ): i.e. "from the blood of his brother". And «مِنْ» [Translator's note: so vowelled in the source; مَنْ is meant] refers to the guardian of the killer (وَلِيِّ الْقَاتِلِ) [Translator's note: so in the source; the explanation that follows suggests the guardian of the slain person is meant], i.e. "whoever is given, for the blood of his brother, a compensation", namely retaliation or blood-money. And (شَيْءٌ) refers to that which is due.
It is also said that «مِنْ» refers to the killer, and the meaning is: when the killer is pardoned and blood-money is accepted from him.
And it is said: شَيْءٌ is in the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "whoever is granted by his brother some pardon", as He said: «لَا يَضُرُّكُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْئًا», i.e. "any harm". (وَأَدَاءٌ إِلَيْهِ): i.e. to the guardian of the slain person. (بِإِحْسَانٍ): in the position of the accusative governed by أَدَاءٌ; it may also be an adjective (ṣifa) of the maṣdar, and likewise بِالْمَعْرُوفِ; and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ, i.e. "then upon him is following him, being just and doing good", and what governs the ḥāl is the meaning of settledness (al-istiqrār). (فَمَنِ اعْتَدَى): conditional, and «فَلَهُ» is its apodosis (jawāb); it may also mean "the one who".

ukberi-tibyan:179-179.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَكُمْ فِي الْقِصَاصِ حَيَاةٌ يَا أُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ (١٧٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَا أُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ): in the nominative it is said with wāw [أُولُو], and أُولِي with yāʾ in the genitive and accusative, like ذَوُو. أُولُو is a plural whose singular is ذُو, not from its own root; it has no singular from its own root.

ukberi-tibyan:283-283.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ عَلَى سَفَرٍ وَلَمْ تَجِدُوا كَاتِبًا فَرِهَانٌ مَقْبُوضَةٌ فَإِنْ أَمِنَ بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضًا فَلْيُؤَدِّ الَّذِي اؤْتُمِنَ أَمَانَتَهُ وَلْيَتَّقِ اللَّهَ رَبَّهُ وَلَا تَكْتُمُوا الشَّهَادَةَ وَمَنْ يَكْتُمْهَا فَإِنَّهُ آثِمٌ قَلْبُهُ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ عَلِيمٌ (٢٨٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَرِهَانٌ): the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "then the security [is]", or "the securing [is]".
It is read [رُهُن / رُهْن] with ḍamma on the hāʾ and with sukūn on it; it is the plural of رَهْن, like سَقْف and سُقُف, and أَسَد and أُسُد; the sukūn is because of the heaviness of a ḍamma after a ḍamma.
It has been said that رُهُن is the plural of رِهان, and رِهان is the plural of رَهْن — and it has been read so — like كَلْب and كِلاب. الرَّهْن is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), and here it means "pledged thing".
(الَّذِي اؤْتُمِنَ): if you pause on الذي, you begin أُوتُمِن; the hamza is for connection (waṣl), and the wāw is a substitute for the hamza that is the first radical (fāʾ) of the verb. When you continue, you drop the connecting hamza and return the wāw to its origin, which is the hamza; and the yāʾ of «الذي» is dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. The hamza has also been changed into a quiescent yāʾ, the yāʾ of الذي being dropped for the reason we mentioned; and it has been read so.
(أَمَانَتَهُ) is the object of يؤدّ, not the maṣdar of اؤتمن; الأمانة here means "the thing entrusted".
(وَلَا تَكْتُمُوا): the majority read it with tāʾ, for second-person address, like the beginning of the verse.
It has been read with yāʾ, in the third person, because before it there is a third person — except that what precedes it is singular in wording, yet it is a genus; therefore the pronoun came in the plural according to the meaning.
(فَإِنَّهُ): the hāʾ is the pronoun of مَن, and it may be the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn).
(آثِمٌ): there are several views on it. The first: that it is the khabar of إنّ, and «قلبه» is nominative by it [as its fāʿil (agent)].
The second: likewise, except that قلبه is a badal (substitute) from آثم, not with the intention of discarding the first.
The third: that قلبه is a badal from the pronoun in آثم.
The fourth: that قلبه is a mubtadaʾ and آثم a khabar placed first, the clause being the khabar of إنّ.
Some allowed قلبَه in the accusative as a tamyīz (specification); that is far-fetched, because it is definite.

ukberi-tibyan:284-284.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَإِنْ تُبْدُوا مَا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ يُحَاسِبْكُمْ بِهِ اللَّهُ فَيَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (٢٨٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَيَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ): both are read in the nominative as a resumption (istiʾnāf), i.e. "He forgives"; in the jussive, conjoined to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and in the subjunctive, conjoined according to the meaning with an implied أن, its implied form being: فأن يغفر — this is called al-ṣarf ("diversion") — the implied sense being: "there will be from Him a reckoning, then forgiveness".
It has been read, among the irregular (shādhdh) readings, without the fāʾ and in the jussive, on the basis that it is a badal (substitute) from يحاسبكم.

ukberi-tibyan:285-285.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (آمَنَ الرَّسُولُ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ كُلٌّ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ رُسُلِهِ وَقَالُوا سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا غُفْرَانَكَ رَبَّنَا وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ (٢٨٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ): conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الرسول, so the speech is complete at it. It has been said:
المؤمنون is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «كل» a second mubtadaʾ, the implied form being "each of them"; «آمن» is the khabar (predicate) of the second mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of the first. The pronoun in آمن is singular in reference to the wording of كل.
