(وَكُتُبِهِ): it is read without alif, as a plural, because what is with it is plural; and it is read «وكتابه» as a singular, being a genus — and it may be that the Quran alone is meant by it.
(وَرُسُلِهِ): it is read with ḍamma and with sukūn [on the sīn]; its justification has been mentioned.
(لَا نُفَرِّقُ): its implied form is "saying", and it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). بين is put in construct with أحد because أحد carries the meaning of a plural. (وَقَالُوا): conjoined to آمن.
(غُفْرَانَكَ): i.e. "forgive Your forgiveness", so it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun).
It has been said that the implied form is: "we ask You Your forgiveness".

ukberi-tibyan:286-286.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا اكْتَسَبَتْ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا إِنْ نَسِينَا أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَا إِصْرًا كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِنَا رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ وَاعْفُ عَنَّا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَا أَنْتَ مَوْلَانَا فَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ (٢٨٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَسَبَتْ), and in the second (اكْتَسَبَتْ): some said there is no difference between them, and they adduced as proof His saying «وَلَا تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ إِلَّا عَلَيْهَا», and He said «ذُوقُوا مَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْسِبُونَ» — so He used kasb for evil deeds just as He used it for good deeds.
Others said: اكتسب, on the iftaʿala pattern, indicates intensity of effort, and doing an evil deed is grave because of what it leads to.
(لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا): it is read with the hamza and with lightening [of the hamza]; the past is آخذتُه, and it is from being taken to task for a sin. واخذتُه, with wāw, has also been reported.

ukberi-tibyan:252-252.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (تِلْكَ آيَاتُ اللَّهِ نَتْلُوهَا عَلَيْكَ بِالْحَقِّ وَإِنَّكَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ (٢٥٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تِلْكَ آيَاتُ اللَّهِ): تِلْكَ is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and آيَاتُ اللَّهِ is the khabar (predicate).
And (نَتْلُوهَا): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of al-āyāt, the governing element in it being the meaning of the demonstrative (pointing); and it may be resumptive. And (بِالْحَقِّ): it may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), or a ḥāl of the accusative pronoun referring to the verses, i.e. "bound up with the truth". It may also be a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent), i.e. "with the truth being with Us". And it may be a ḥāl of the kāf, i.e. "with the truth being with you".

ukberi-tibyan:253-253.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (تِلْكَ الرُّسُلُ فَضَّلْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ مِنْهُمْ مَنْ كَلَّمَ اللَّهُ وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَهُمْ دَرَجَاتٍ وَآتَيْنَا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ الْبَيِّنَاتِ وَأَيَّدْنَاهُ بِرُوحِ الْقُدُسِ وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مَا اقْتَتَلَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ وَلَكِنِ اخْتَلَفُوا فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ آمَنَ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ كَفَرَ وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مَا اقْتَتَلُوا وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَفْعَلُ مَا يُرِيدُ (٢٥٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تِلْكَ الرُّسُلُ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).
And (فَضَّلْنَا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of al-rusul. It is also possible that al-rusul is a naʿt (adjective) or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), and فَضَّلْنَا is the khabar. (مِنْهُمْ مَنْ كَلَّمَ اللَّهُ): it may be resumptive, having no grammatical position, and it may be a badal (substitute) of the position of فَضَّلْنَا. It is also read (كَلَّمَ اللَّهَ) with the accusative, and it is read «كَالَمَ اللَّهُ».
And (دَرَجَاتٍ) is a ḥāl of بَعْضَهُمْ, i.e. "possessing ranks".
It has also been said: دَرَجَات is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl. And it has been said: it is in the accusative as a maṣdar, because daraja is in the sense of rifʿa (raising); so it is as if He said: "and We raised some of them raisings".
It has also been said that the implied form is "upon ranks", or "in ranks", or "to ranks"; when the preposition was dropped, the verb reached it by itself. (مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْهُمُ): it may be a badal of بَعْدِهِمْ with repetition of the preposition.
It is also possible that the second «مِنْ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) اقْتَتَلَ, with the first pronoun referring back to the messengers, and the pronoun in جَاءَتْهُمْ referring back to the nations. (وَلَكِنِ): a rectification (istidrāk) of what the speech indicated, because their fighting one another came from their disagreement.
Then He explained the disagreement by His saying (فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ آمَنَ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ كَفَرَ), and the implied form is: "so they fought one another".
(وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَفْعَلُ مَا يُرِيدُ): also a rectification according to the meaning, because the meaning is: "had Allah willed, He would have prevented them; but Allah does what He wills", and He willed not to prevent them, or He willed their disagreement and their fighting.

ukberi-tibyan:254-254.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْفِقُوا مِمَّا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ لَا بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلَا خُلَّةٌ وَلَا شَفَاعَةٌ وَالْكَافِرُونَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ (٢٤٥)). «[Translator's note: the verse number is printed as ٢٤٥; this is verse ٢٥٤.]»
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَنْفِقُوا): its object is omitted, i.e. "something". (مِمَّا): «مَا» is in the sense of الَّذِي (that which), and the referring pronoun is omitted, i.e. "We provided you with it". (لَا بَيْعٌ فِيهِ): in the position of the nominative as an adjective of يَوْم. (وَلَا خُلَّةٌ): i.e. "in it". (وَلَا شَفَاعَةٌ): i.e. "in it". It is read in the nominative with nunation, and its reasoning has passed in His saying (فَلَا رَفَثَ).

ukberi-tibyan:255-255.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ (٢٥٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); we have mentioned the position of هُوَ in His saying (وَإِلَهُكُمْ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ).
(الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ): it may be a second khabar; or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "He"; or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is لَا تَأْخُذُهُ; or a badal (substitute) of هُوَ; or a badal of لَا إِلَهَ.
Al-qayyūm is fayʿūl from qāma yaqūmu: when the wāw and the yāʾ came together, and the first of them preceded with sukūn, the wāw was changed into yāʾ, and the two were assimilated. It is not permissible for it to be faʿʿūl from this, because were that so it would be qawwūm with wāw, since the doubled middle radical is always of the same kind as the original middle radical, as in subbūḥ and quddūs, and as in ḍarrāb and qattāl: the augment is of the same kind as the middle radical. So since the yāʾ came, this showed that it is fayʿūl.
It is also read al-qayyim, on the pattern fayʿil, like sayyid and mayyit; and it is read al-qayyām, on the pattern fayʿāl, like bayṭār.
It has been read anomalously (shādhdh) al-qāʾim, like His saying: قَائِمًا بِالْقِسْطِ. And it has also been read anomalously «الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ» in the accusative, by implying aʿnī (I mean).
The middle and final radicals of al-ḥayy are both yāʾ, and there is a place where the discussion of it is given in full.
(لَا تَأْخُذُهُ): it may be resumptive, and it may have a grammatical position; there are several views on that. The first: that it is another khabar of «اللَّهُ», or a khabar of al-ḥayy.
It may also be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in al-qayyūm, i.e. "He sustains the affairs of creation, not being heedless". The original of al-sina is wasna, and the verb from it is wasina yasinu, like waʿada yaʿidu; when the wāw was dropped in the verb, it was dropped in the maṣdar. (وَلَا نَوْمٌ): لَا is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, and its benefit is that if it were dropped, the speech could mean that drowsiness and sleep do not overtake Him in a single state; but when He says وَلَا نَوْمٌ, He negates both in every state.
(لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ): it may be another khabar of what preceded, or it may be resumptive.
(مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي): it has been discussed in His saying, Exalted is He: (مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ).
And (عِنْدَهُ) is an adverb (ẓarf) of يَشْفَعُ. It has been said: it may be a ḥāl of the pronoun in يَشْفَعُ; this is weak in meaning, because the meaning is "intercedes with Him".
It has also been said: rather, the ḥāl is stronger, because if one who is with Him and near to Him is not granted intercession, then the intercession of anyone else is more remote. (إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ): in the position of a ḥāl; the implied sense is: "no one intercedes with Him except as one given permission", or "except with permission accompanying him", or "except in the state of permission". It may also be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "by His permission they intercede", as you say "he struck with his sword", i.e. it is the instrument of the striking. And (يَعْلَمُ) may be another khabar, or it may be resumptive.
(مِنْ عِلْمِهِ): i.e. what is known by Him, because He said: إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ; and His knowledge that is an attribute of His is not encompassed, nor is anything of it; and for this reason He said: (وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِهِ عِلْمًا).
(إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ): a badal of شَيْء, as you say "I did not pass by anyone except Zayd".
(وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ): the majority read it with fatḥa on the wāw and kasra on the sīn, on the basis that it is a verb (faʿila), and al-kursī is its fāʿil (agent). It is also read with sukūn on the sīn, as a lightening of the kasra, like ʿalma for ʿalima. «[Translator's note: the text prints the lightened form as «عِلِمٍ».]»
It is also read with fatḥa on the wāw, sukūn on the sīn and the nominative on the ʿayn (wasʿu), with كُرْسِيِّهِ in the genitive,
and (السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ) in the nominative, on the basis that it is a mubtadaʾ and khabar.
Al-kursī is fuʿlī from al-karas, which is gathering; the most eloquent form has ḍamma on the kāf, and kasra is permissible for vowel harmony (itbāʿ). (وَلَا يَئُودُهُ): the majority pronounce the hamza fully, according to the original.
It is also read with the hamza dropped, as the hamza of unās was dropped; and it is read with a wāw bearing ḍamma in place of the hamza, by substitution.
And (الْعَلِيُّ) is faʿīl, and its original is ʿaliyw, because it is from ʿalā yaʿlū.

ukberi-tibyan:256-256.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لَا إِكْرَاهَ فِي الدِّينِ قَدْ تَبَيَّنَ الرُّشْدُ مِنَ الْغَيِّ فَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِالطَّاغُوتِ وَيُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدِ اسْتَمْسَكَ بِالْعُرْوَةِ الْوُثْقَى لَا انْفِصَامَ لَهَا وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ (٢٥٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَدْ تَبَيَّنَ) الرُّشْدُ: the majority assimilate the dāl into the tāʾ, because it is from its point of articulation; and turning the dāl into tāʾ is preferable, because the dāl is plosive (shadīda) and the tāʾ is voiceless (mahmūsa), and the voiceless is lighter. It is also read with the dāl pronounced distinctly (iẓhār), and that is weak, for the reason we mentioned.
Al-rushd, with ḍamma on the rāʾ and sukūn on the shīn, is the well-known reading; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of rashada, with fatḥa on the shīn, yarshudu, with ḍamma on it. It is also read with fatḥa on the rāʾ and the shīn (al-rashad), and its verb is rashida yarshadu, like ʿalima yaʿlamu.
(مِنَ الْغَيِّ): in the position of the accusative, on the basis that it is an object. The original of al-ghayy is ghawy, because it is from ghawā yaghwī; the wāw was changed into yāʾ because of its sukūn and its preceding, and then it was assimilated.
And (الطَّاغُوتِ) is treated as masculine and feminine, and is used in one form for plural and singular, masculine and feminine; from this is His saying (وَالَّذِينَ اجْتَنَبُوا الطَّاغُوتَ أَنْ يَعْبُدُوهَا). Its original is ṭaghyūt, because it is from ṭaghayta taṭghā. It may also be from wāw, because one also says yaṭghū regarding it, but the yāʾ is more common, and on it came al-ṭughyān. Then the final radical was brought forward and placed before the ghayn, so it became ṭayghūt or ṭawghūt; when the letter had a vowel and what preceded it had fatḥa, it was changed into alif, so its pattern now is falʿūt. It is originally a maṣdar, like al-malakūt and al-rahabūt. (الْوُثْقَى): the feminine of al-awthaq, like al-wusṭā and al-awsaṭ; its plural is al-wuthaq, like al-ṣughar and al-kubar. As for al-wuthuq with two ḍammas, it is the plural of wathīq.
(لَا انْفِصَامَ لَهَا): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of al-ʿurwa.
It may also be a ḥāl of the pronoun in al-wuthqā.

ukberi-tibyan:257-257.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (اللَّهُ وَلِيُّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يُخْرِجُهُمْ مِنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَوْلِيَاؤُهُمُ الطَّاغُوتُ يُخْرِجُونَهُمْ مِنَ النُّورِ إِلَى الظُّلُمَاتِ أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ (٢٥٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): a mubtadaʾ (subject); أَوْلِيَاؤُهُمْ is a second mubtadaʾ; «الطَّاغُوتُ» is the khabar (predicate) of the second; and the second with its khabar is the khabar of the first.
It has been read al-ṭawāghīt in the plural; it was pluralised, although it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), only because it became a noun for what is worshipped besides Allah. (يُخْرِجُونَهُمْ): resumptive, having no grammatical position.
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), the governing element in it being the meaning of al-ṭāghūt; this is parallel to what Abū ʿAlī said regarding His saying (إِنَّهَا لَظَى نَزَّاعَةً) [al-Maʿārij: 15–16], and we shall mention it in its place.
As for (يُخْرِجُهُمْ), it may be a second khabar, or a ḥāl of the pronoun in «وَلِيُّ».

ukberi-tibyan:219-219.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْخَمْرِ وَالْمَيْسِرِ قُلْ فِيهِمَا إِثْمٌ كَبِيرٌ وَمَنَافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ وَإِثْمُهُمَا أَكْبَرُ مِنْ نَفْعِهِمَا وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَا يُنْفِقُونَ قُلِ الْعَفْوَ كَذَلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمُ الْآيَاتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ (١١٩)). [Translator's note: the verse number is printed as ١١٩; it is verse 219.]
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِيهِمَا إِثْمٌ كَبِيرٌ): the better reading is with the bāʾ (كَبِيرٌ, "great"), because one says "a great sin" and "a small sin", and one says of the enormous indecencies "the major sins" (الكبائر) and of what is below that "the minor sins" (الصغائر). It has also been read with the thāʾ (كَثِيرٌ, "much"), and that is good in meaning, because muchness is greatness and the much is great, just as the small is slight and paltry. (وَإِثْمُهُمَا) and (نَفْعِهِمَا): two maṣdars (verbal nouns) annexed to (الخمر) and (الميسر). It may be the annexation of the maṣdar to its agent, because it is wine that causes sin.
The annexation to them may also be because they are the cause of the sin or its locus.
(قُلِ الْعَفْوَ): read in the nominative (الْعَفْوُ) as a khabar (predicate) with the mubtadaʾ (subject) omitted, its implied form being "say: what is spent is…"; this is when you make (ماذا) a mubtadaʾ and khabar. It is read in the accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "they spend the surplus"; this is when you make (ما) and (ذا) one noun, because (العفو) is an answer, and the i'rab of the answer is like the i'rab of the question.
(كَذَلِكَ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative, an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "with an explanation like this explanation He explains to you".

ukberi-tibyan:220-220.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْيَتَامَى قُلْ إِصْلَاحٌ لَهُمْ خَيْرٌ وَإِنْ تُخَالِطُوهُمْ فَإِخْوَانُكُمْ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ الْمُفْسِدَ مِنَ الْمُصْلِحِ وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَأَعْنَتَكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ (٢٢٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ): (في) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (يتفكرون); it may also be attached to (يبين).
(إِصْلَاحٌ لَهُمْ خَيْرٌ): (إصلاح) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), (لهم) is a naʿt (adjective) of it, and (خير) is its khabar (predicate). The implied form may be "better for them", and it may be "better for you", i.e. "setting them right is beneficial to you".
(لهم) may also be an adjective of (خير) placed before it, and so be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).
Beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted, even if it were not described, because the noun here has the sense of a verb, its implied form being "set them right". It may also be that indefinite and definite are the same here, because it is a genus.
(فَإِخْوَانُكُمْ): i.e. "then they are your brothers". The accusative is permissible in speech, its implied form being "then you have mixed with your brothers".
And (الْمُفْسِدَ) and (الْمُصْلِحِ) here are two genera; the alif and lām are not for the definiteness of something known.
(وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ): the object is omitted, its implied form being "had Allah willed to put you in hardship, He would have put you in hardship".

ukberi-tibyan:221-221.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا تَنْكِحُوا الْمُشْرِكَاتِ حَتَّى يُؤْمِنَّ وَلَأَمَةٌ مُؤْمِنَةٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ مُشْرِكَةٍ وَلَوْ أَعْجَبَتْكُمْ وَلَا تُنْكِحُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ حَتَّى يُؤْمِنُوا وَلَعَبْدٌ مُؤْمِنٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ مُشْرِكٍ وَلَوْ أَعْجَبَكُمْ أُولَئِكَ يَدْعُونَ إِلَى النَّارِ وَاللَّهُ يَدْعُو إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ وَالْمَغْفِرَةِ بِإِذْنِهِ وَيُبَيِّنُ آيَاتِهِ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ (٢٢١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلَا تنْكِحُوا المشركات}: the past tense of this verb has three letters; one says نَكَحْتُ الْمَرْأَةَ when you marry her.
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَا تُنْكِحُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ): with ḍamma on the tāʾ, because it is from أَنْكَحْتُ الرَّجُلَ, when you give him in marriage. (وَلَوْ أَعْجَبَكُمْ): (لو) here means (إن) ("even if"), and likewise in every place where a past verb comes after (لو) and its answer precedes it. (وَالْمَغْفِرَةِ بِإِذْنِهِ): read in the genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (الجنة), and in the nominative (وَالْمَغْفِرَةُ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject).

ukberi-tibyan:222-222.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْمَحِيضِ قُلْ هُوَ أَذًى فَاعْتَزِلُوا النِّسَاءَ فِي الْمَحِيضِ وَلَا تَقْرَبُوهُنَّ حَتَّى يَطْهُرْنَ فَإِذَا تَطَهَّرْنَ فَأْتُوهُنَّ مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ التَّوَّابِينَ وَيُحِبُّ الْمُتَطَهِّرِينَ (٢٢٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَنِ الْمَحِيضِ): (المحيض) may be the place of menstruation, and it may be menstruation itself; the implied form is "they ask you about intercourse in the time of menstruation, or in the place of menstruation, while menstruation is present". (فَاعْتَزِلُوا النِّسَاءَ): i.e. intercourse with women; and (هو) [Translator's note: i.e. the pronoun in (قُلْ هُوَ أَذًى)] refers to the forbidden intercourse.
It may also refer to (المحيض), the implied form being "it is a cause of harm".
(حَتَّى يَطْهُرْنَ): read without doubling, its past tense being طَهُرْنَ, i.e. "their bleeding has stopped"; and with doubling (يَطَّهَّرْنَ), the original being يَتَطَهَّرْنَ, i.e. "they wash", the tāʾ having been given sukūn, changed into a ṭāʾ and assimilated.
(مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ): (من) here is for the beginning of the extent, according to its basic meaning, i.e. "from the direction that leads to the place of menstruation". It may also mean "in" (في), so as to match His saying (في المحيض). There is an omission in the speech, its implied form being "Allah commanded you to come (to them) from it".

ukberi-tibyan:223-223.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (نِسَاؤُكُمْ حَرْثٌ لَكُمْ فَأْتُوا حَرْثَكُمْ أَنَّى شِئْتُمْ وَقَدِّمُوا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّكُمْ مُلَاقُوهُ وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (٢٢٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حَرْثٌ لَكُمْ): the khabar (predicate) is singular while the mubtadaʾ (subject) is plural only because (الحرث) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a description, and it has the sense of the passive participle, i.e. "tilled fields".
(أَنَّى شِئْتُمْ): i.e. "however you wish"; it has also been said: "whenever you wish"; and it has also been said: "from wherever you wish", provided it is in the permitted place. The object is omitted, i.e. "you wish to come (to them)".
The object of (قَدِّمُوا) is omitted, its implied form being "the intention of (having) a child" or "the intention of chastity".
(وَبَشِّرِ): an address to the Prophet ﷺ, since he has been mentioned in His saying (يسألونك).

ukberi-tibyan:224-224.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا تَجْعَلُوا اللَّهَ عُرْضَةً لِأَيْمَانِكُمْ أَنْ تَبَرُّوا وَتَتَّقُوا وَتُصْلِحُوا بَيْنَ النَّاسِ وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ (٢٢٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ تَبَرُّوا): in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for fear that you be righteous"; according to the Kufans, "lest you be righteous". Abū Isḥāq [Translator's note: al-Zajjāj] said: it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar (predicate) omitted, i.e. "that you be righteous and fear (Allah) is better for you". It has also been said: the implied form is "in (في) that you be righteous", and when the preposition was omitted it became accusative; and it has also been said: it is in the position of the genitive by the omitted preposition.

ukberi-tibyan:225-225.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لَا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ اللَّهُ بِاللَّغْوِ فِي أَيْمَانِكُمْ وَلَكِنْ يُؤَاخِذُكُمْ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ (٢٢٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي أَيْمَانِكُمْ): «فِي» may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to the maṣdar (verbal noun), as you say "he spoke idly in his oath". It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of it, its implied form being "for the idle talk, being in your oaths". What brings this meaning close to you is that if you brought (الذي) the meaning would be sound, and it would be an adjective, as in your saying "for the idle talk which is in your oaths".
(بِمَا كَسَبَتْ): «مَا» may be maṣdariyya (infinitival), and so need no pronoun; and it may mean "that which", or be a described indefinite noun, in which case the referring pronoun is omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:226-226.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لِلَّذِينَ يُؤْلُونَ مِنْ نِسَائِهِمْ تَرَبُّصُ أَرْبَعَةِ أَشْهُرٍ فَإِنْ فَاءُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (٢٢٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِلَّذِينَ يُؤْلُونَ): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, namely "being established", and it is the khabar (predicate), the mubtadaʾ (subject) being «تَرَبُّصُ». According to al-Akhfash it is a verb and agent [Translator's note: i.e. (تربص) is the fāʿil of the prepositional phrase, which acts like a verb].
As for (مِنْ), it has been said: it is attached to (يؤلون); one says آلَى مِنَ امْرَأَتِهِ and آلَى عَلَى امْرَأَتِهِ ("he swore off his wife"). It has also been said: the original is (على), and (من) may not be put in place of (على); in that case (من) is attached to the sense of being established. The annexation of (التربص) to (الأشهر) is the annexation of a maṣdar (verbal noun) to its adverbial in meaning, while it is a direct object by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa). The alif in (فَاءُوا) is changed from a yāʾ, as you say فَاءَ يَفِي فَيْئَةً. [Translator's note: so printed («يَفِي»); the usual imperfect is يَفِيءُ.]

ukberi-tibyan:227-227.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِنْ عَزَمُوا الطَّلَاقَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ (٢٢٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِنْ عَزَمُوا الطَّلَاقَ): i.e. "on (على) divorce"; when the preposition was omitted it became accusative. It may also be that (عزم) was construed like (نوى) ("intended"), and so made transitive without a preposition. (الطلاق) is the noun of the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar), the maṣdar being التطليق.

ukberi-tibyan:180-180.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ إِنْ تَرَكَ خَيْرًا الْوَصِيَّةُ لِلْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ حَقًّا عَلَى الْمُتَّقِينَ (١٨٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَ): what governs إِذَا is كُتِبَ. What is meant by the coming of death is the coming of its causes and preliminaries, and that is the time at which the bequest was made obligatory. What is meant by "writing" (al-katb) is not literal inscription on the Tablet; rather it is like His saying «كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِصَاصُ فِي الْقَتْلَى» and the like. It is also possible for what governs إِذَا to be the meaning of bequeathing (الْإِصَاءِ [Translator's note: so in the source, evidently for الْإِيصَاءِ]), which is indicated by His saying الْوَصِيَّةُ.
It is not permissible for what governs it to be the word الْوَصِيَّةُ mentioned in the verse, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and a maṣdar is not preceded by what it governs. This is what is called al-tabyīn (explication).
As for His saying (إِنْ تَرَكَ خَيْرًا), its apodosis (jawāb) according to al-Akhfash is «الْوَصِيَّةُ», with the fāʾ omitted, i.e. "then the bequest is for the parents"; and he cited as evidence the saying of the poet:
مَنْ يَفْعَلِ الْحَسَنَاتِ اللَّهُ يَشْكُرُهَا وَالشَّرُّ بِالشَّرِّ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ مِثْلَانِ.
("Whoever does good deeds, Allah appreciates them; and evil for evil is, with Allah, an equal pair.")
On this view الْوَصِيَّةُ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «لِلْوَالِدَيْنِ» is its khabar (predicate).
Others said: the apodosis of the condition is, in meaning, what has preceded, namely the meaning of prescribing the bequest, as you say: أَنْتَ ظَالِمٌ إِنْ فَعَلْتَ ("you are a wrongdoer if you did [it]"). It is also possible for the apodosis of the condition to be the meaning of bequeathing, not the meaning of prescribing. This is sound on the view of those who make الْوَصِيَّةُ nominative by كُتِبَ, and that is the correct view. It is also said that what is made nominative by كُتِبَ is the preposition and its genitive noun, namely عَلَيْكُمْ; and this is nothing.
(بِالْمَعْرُوفِ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "bound up with what is fair, with no injustice in it".
(حَقًّا): accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. "that is made a duty, truly".
It may also be an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a true prescribing", or "a true bequeathing".
Outside the Quran the nominative is permissible, in the sense of "that is a duty" (ذَلِكَ حَقٌّ).
And (عَلَى الْمُتَّقِينَ) is an adjective of حَقًّا.
It is also said that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the maṣdar itself, but this is weak, because the emphasizing maṣdar does not govern; the maṣdar governs only when it is accusative by an omitted verb and stands in for it, as when you say ضَرْبًا زَيْدًا, i.e. "strike [Zayd]!".

ukberi-tibyan:181-181.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَمَنْ بَدَّلَهُ بَعْدَمَا سَمِعَهُ فَإِنَّمَا إِثْمُهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ يُبَدِّلُونَهُ. . . . . . . . (١٨١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَمَنْ بَدَّلَهُ): مَنْ is conditional, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). The hāʾ is the pronoun of the bequeathing (al-īṣāʾ), because it is in the sense of الْوَصِيَّة. It is also said that it is the pronoun of the prescribing (al-katb); and it is said that it is the pronoun of the command to bequeath, or of the ruling that was commanded; and it is said that it is the pronoun of الْمَعْرُوف; and it is said: the pronoun of الْحَقّ.
(بَعْدَمَا سَمِعَهُ): مَا is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun).
It is also said that it means "that which" (الَّذِي), i.e. "after what he heard of the prohibition against altering".
The hāʾ in (إِثْمُهُ) is the pronoun of the altering (al-tabdīl) indicated by بَدَّلَ.

ukberi-tibyan:182-182.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَمَنْ خَافَ مِنْ مُوصٍ جَنَفًا أَوْ إِثْمًا. . . (١٨٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ مُوصٍ): it is read with sukūn on the wāw and the ṣād undoubled, from أَوْصَى, and with fatḥa on the wāw and the ṣād doubled [مُوَصٍّ], from وَصَّى; both have one meaning.
The doubling here does not mean intensiveness, because that occurs only in a triliteral verb when it is doubled; but when the doubling is the counterpart of the hamza [of form IV], it does not indicate intensiveness; like it are نَزَّلَ and أَنْزَلَ [Translator's note: the source has نَزَلَ].
And (مِنْ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to خَافَ. It may also be attached to something omitted, on the basis that it is originally an adjective (ṣifa) of جَنَفًا, the implied form being: "whoever fears an injustice coming from a testator"; when it was placed first, it became accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Like it is أَخَذْتُ مِنْ زَيْدٍ مَالًا ("I took wealth from Zayd"): if you wish, you attach مِنْ to أَخَذْتُ, and if you wish, the implied form is "wealth belonging to Zayd".

ukberi-tibyan:183-183.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ. . . . . . (١٨٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيَامُ): [الصِّيَامُ is] the object standing in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)).
There are four views on the position of the kāf. The first: it is in the position of the accusative as an adjective (ṣifa) of the prescribing, i.e. "a prescribing like what was prescribed"; on this view مَا is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun). The second: that it is an adjective of the fasting, i.e. "a fasting like what was prescribed"; on this view مَا means "that which" (الَّذِي), i.e. "a fasting resembling the fasting prescribed for those before you". صَوْمٌ here is, in meaning, an emphasizing maṣdar (verbal noun), because الصِّيَامُ means "that you fast a fast". The third: that the kāf is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الصِّيَامُ, i.e. "resembling what was prescribed for those before you". The fourth: that it is in the position of the nominative as an adjective of الصِّيَامُ.
If it is said: the preposition and its genitive noun are indefinite, while الصِّيَامُ is definite, and an indefinite cannot be an adjective of a definite —
it is answered: since no specific fasting was intended by الصِّيَامُ, it is like an indefinite. We have mentioned something similar in [Sūrat] al-Fātiḥa. This is strengthened by الصِّيَامُ being a maṣdar, and a maṣdar denotes a genus, and the definiteness of a genus is close to its indefiniteness.

ukberi-tibyan:184-184.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَيَّامًا مَعْدُودَاتٍ فَمَنْ كَانَ مِنْكُمْ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَى سَفَرٍ فَعِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُ فِدْيَةٌ طَعَامُ مِسْكِينٍ فَمَنْ تَطَوَّعَ خَيْرًا فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَهُ وَأَنْ تَصُومُوا خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ (١٧٨)). [Translator's note: so numbered in the source; this is verse 184.]
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَيَّامًا مَعْدُودَاتٍ): it may not be accusative governed by the maṣdar (verbal noun) of the first «كُتِبَ», neither as an adverb of time nor as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa), because the kāf in كَمَا is a description of an omitted maṣdar, and a maṣdar, when qualified by an adjective, does not govern; and likewise the active participle. Nor may it be accusative governed by الصِّيَامُ mentioned in the verse, because it is a maṣdar, and it has been separated from أَيَّامًا by His saying «كَمَا كُتِبَ»; what the maṣdar governs is like the ṣila (relative clause), and the ṣila is not separated from what it belongs to (al-mawṣūl) by something extraneous. And if [the kāf] is made an adjective of الصِّيَامُ, it is also not permissible, because a maṣdar, when qualified by an adjective, does not govern.
The correct view is that what governs أَيَّامًا is omitted, its implied form being: "fast days"; on this view أَيَّامًا is an adverb of time, because an adverb can be governed by the meaning. It may also be that أَيَّامًا is accusative governed by كُتِبَ, because الصِّيَامُ is nominative by it, and كَمَا is either a maṣdar for كُتِبَ or an adjective (naʿt) of الصِّيَامُ, and neither of them prevents the verb from governing; on this view it may be an adverb of time, or a mafʿūl bihi by extension.
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَوْ عَلَى سَفَرٍ): in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the khabar (predicate) of كَانَ, its implied form being: "or was travelling". عَلَى entered here only because the traveller is resolved upon completing his journey, so the implied form ought to be: "or was resolved upon completing a journey". سَفَرٍ here is indefinite, but a specific journey is meant by it, namely the journey of the distance determined in the Sharīʿa. (فَعِدَّةٌ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "then upon him is a number"; and it contains an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the fasting of a number". Had it been read in the accusative, it would have been sound, the implied form being: "then let him fast a number".
There is an omission in the speech, its implied form being: "and he broke the fast, then upon him…". And (مِنْ أَيَّامٍ) is an adjective of عِدَّةٌ. And (أُخَرَ) is a diptote (lā yanṣarif) because of being descriptive and because of its deviation (ʿadl) from [the form with] the alif and lām, since the basic rule for the pattern fuʿlā used as an adjective is that it be used in the plural with the alif and lām, like الْكُبْرَى and الْكُبَرُ, and الصُّغْرَى and الصُّغَرُ. (يُطِيقُونَهُ): the majority read it with yāʾ.
It was also read «يُطَوَّقُونَهُ» with a doubled wāw bearing fatḥa; it is from الطَّوْقُ, which is the measure of capacity, and the meaning is "they are burdened with it". (فِدْيَةٌ): it is read with tanwīn, and «طَعَامُ» in the nominative as a badal (substitute) for it, or with an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is the feeding". And (مِسْكِينٍ) [is read] in the singular, the meaning being that what is required for breaking the fast on each day is the feeding of one poor person.
It is also read without tanwīn, with طَعَامِ in the genitive and مَسَاكِينَ in the plural. The construct of فِدْيَة with طَعَام is the construct of a thing with its genus, as when you say خَاتَمُ فِضَّةٍ ("a ring of silver"), because the feeding of a poor person may be a ransom or not a ransom. الْمَسَاكِين was put in the plural only because He used the plural in His saying «وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُ», so He matched plural with plural; and He did not put فِدْيَة in the plural for two reasons:
The first: that it is a maṣdar, and the hāʾ in it does not indicate a single instance; rather it is only for the feminine.
The second: that since He put it in construct with something that is in construct with a plural, the plural is understood from it. الطَّعَامُ here means "feeding" (الْإِطْعَامُ), like الْعَطَاءُ in the sense of الْإِعْطَاءُ. It is weak for الطَّعَام to be the food itself, because He put it in construct with الْمِسْكِين, and the food does not belong to the poor person before it has been made his property; if it were taken in that sense it would be figurative, because its implied form would be: "then upon him is to bring out food that becomes the poor people's". Yet if the verse were taken in that sense, it would not be impossible, because the omission of the muḍāf is permissible, and naming a thing by what it will become is permissible.
(فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَهُ): the pronoun refers to the voluntary act (al-taṭawwuʿ); its word is not mentioned, but it is indicated by the verb. (وَأَنْ تَصُومُوا): in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and «خَيْرٌ» is its khabar, and «لَكُمْ» is an adjective of خَيْرٌ; and «إِنْ كُنْتُمْ» is a condition whose apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, and what indicates the omitted element is أَنْ تَصُومُوا.

ukberi-tibyan:258-258.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِي حَاجَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي رَبِّهِ أَنْ آتَاهُ اللَّهُ الْمُلْكَ إِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ رَبِّيَ الَّذِي يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ قَالَ أَنَا أُحْيِي وَأُمِيتُ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْتِي بِالشَّمْسِ مِنَ الْمَشْرِقِ فَأْتِ بِهَا مِنَ الْمَغْرِبِ فَبُهِتَ الَّذِي كَفَرَ وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ (٢٥٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ آتَاهُ اللَّهُ) is in the position of the accusative according to Sībawayh and of the genitive according to al-Khalīl, because its implied form is "because (li-an) Allah gave him"; so it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and the governing word in it is «حَاجَّ». The hāʾ is the pronoun of Ibrāhīm.
It may also be the pronoun of الَّذِي. And (إِذْ) may be an adverb (ẓarf) of حَاجَّ, or of آتَاهُ.
Some have mentioned that it is a badal (substitute) of «أَنْ آتَاهُ», and that is nothing, because the adverb of time is other than the maṣdar (verbal noun); so if it were a badal it would be a badal of error (ghalaṭ), unless you make إِذْ in the sense of the maṣdariyya أَنْ; that has occurred, and you will come across its like in the Quran. (أَنَا أُحْيِي): the noun is the hamza and the nūn; the alif was added to it in pausal form only to make clear the vowel of the nūn, so when you join it to what follows you drop the alif, as it is no longer needed.
Nāfiʿ read it retaining the alif in continuous recitation, and that is by treating continuation like pause; this has occurred in poetry.
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْتِي): the fāʾ entered to signal the connection of this speech with what precedes it. The meaning is: since you claim to give life and death and you have not understood, then the proof is that Allah brings the sun; this is the meaning. And (مِنَ الْمَشْرِقِ) and (مِنَ الْمَغْرِبِ) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb mentioned, and are not two ḥāls (circumstantials); they are only for the starting point of the bringing. They may also be two ḥāls, the implied form being "subjected" or "made compliant".
(فَبُهِتَ): in the passive (mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu). It is also read with fatḥa on the bāʾ and ḍamma on the hāʾ (bahuta), and with fatḥa on the bāʾ and kasra on the hāʾ (bahita); these are two dialectal forms, and the verb in both is intransitive. It is also read with fatḥa on both (bahata), and so the fāʿil (agent) may be the pronoun of Ibrāhīm and «الَّذِي» the object.
It is also possible that الَّذِي is the fāʿil, with the verb intransitive.

ukberi-tibyan:259-259.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَوْ كَالَّذِي مَرَّ عَلَى قَرْيَةٍ وَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَى عُرُوشِهَا قَالَ أَنَّى يُحْيِي هَذِهِ اللَّهُ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا فَأَمَاتَهُ اللَّهُ مِائَةَ عَامٍ ثُمَّ بَعَثَهُ قَالَ كَمْ لَبِثْتَ قَالَ لَبِثْتُ يَوْمًا أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ قَالَ بَلْ لَبِثْتَ مِائَةَ عَامٍ فَانْظُرْ إِلَى طَعَامِكَ وَشَرَابِكَ لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ وَانْظُرْ إِلَى حِمَارِكَ وَلِنَجْعَلَكَ آيَةً لِلنَّاسِ وَانْظُرْ إِلَى الْعِظَامِ كَيْفَ نُنْشِزُهَا ثُمَّ نَكْسُوهَا لَحْمًا فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ قَالَ أَعْلَمُ أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (٢٥٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَوْ كَالَّذِي): regarding the kāf there are two views. The first: that it is redundant (zāʾida), and the implied form is: "Have you not seen the one who disputed, or the one who passed by a town?"; it is like His saying (لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ).
The second: it is not redundant, and its position is accusative; the implied form is: "or have you seen the like of the one who…", and this omitted element is indicated by His saying «أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِي حَاجَّ».
And (أَوْ) is for detailing, or for giving a choice in wondering at the state of whichever of the two groups one wishes; it has been discussed in His saying (أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ) and elsewhere.
The root of al-qarya is from qaraytu al-māʾa, when I gathered the water; so the qarya is the gathering place of people.
(وَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ): in the position of the genitive as an adjective of قَرْيَة.
(عَلَى عُرُوشِهَا): attached to (mutaʿalliq) خَاوِيَة, because its meaning is "fallen upon its roofs".
It has also been said: it is a badal (substitute) of al-qarya, its implied form being: "he passed by a town, by its roofs", i.e. he passed by the roofs of the town; and the preposition was repeated with the badal.
On this view, عَلَى عُرُوشِهَا may also be an adjective of al-qarya, not a badal, its implied form being: "by a town fallen upon its roofs". On this basis «وَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ» may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of al-ʿurūsh; or a ḥāl of al-qarya, since it has been described; or a ḥāl of the hāʾ of the muḍāf ilayhi, the governing element being the meaning of the annexation, and this is weak, though permissible.
(أَنَّى): in the position of the accusative, governed by يُحْيِي, and it is in the sense of "when", so on this basis it is an adverb (ẓarf). It may also be in the sense of "how", so that its position is a ḥāl of هَذِهِ; and it is placed first because of the interrogation it contains. (مِائَةَ عَامٍ): an adverb of أَمَاتَهُ according to the meaning, because the meaning is "He kept him dead for a hundred years".
It is not permissible for it to be an adverb according to the overt sense, because causing to die occurs in the shortest time. «[Translator's note: the text prints «الْأَمَانَةَ» (trust), evidently for «الْإِمَاتَةَ» (causing to die), and it is translated accordingly.]»
It may also be an adverb of an omitted verb, its implied form being: "so He caused him to die, and he remained a hundred years"; this is indicated by His saying «كَمْ لَبِثْتَ», then His saying «بَلْ لَبِثْتَ مِائَةَ عَامٍ».
(كَمْ): an adverb of لَبِثْتَ. (لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ): the hāʾ is added in pause, and on this basis there are two views on the origin of the verb. The first: it is yatasannanu, from His saying (حَمَإٍ مَسْنُونٍ); when three nūns came together, the last was changed into yāʾ, as it was changed in taẓannaytu; then the yāʾ was substituted by alif, and then dropped for the jussive.
The second: that the origin of the alif is wāw, from your saying asnā yusnā, when years have passed over it; and the origin of sana is sanwa, because they say sanawāt.
The hāʾ may also be radical, its derivation being from al-sana, whose origin is sanha, because they say sanhāʾ, and "ʿāmaltuhu musānahatan" (I dealt with him by the year); on this basis the hāʾ is retained in both continuation and pause, while on the first view it is retained in pause but not in continuation, and whoever retains it in continuation treats it like pause.
If it is said: what is the fāʿil (agent) of yatasannā? The reply is: it may be the pronoun of the food and the drink, since each of them needs the other and they are like one thing; for that reason the pronoun in the verb is singular.
It is also possible that He made the pronoun refer to "that" (dhālika), and dhālika is used to refer to one, two and many with a single form. It is also possible that the pronoun is for the drink, because it is nearer to it; and if the drink did not change, despite how quickly change comes to it, then that the food did not change is all the more so. It may also be that the singular is used in place of the dual, as the poet said:
فَكَأَنَّ فِي الْعَيْنَيْنِ حَبَّ قَرَنْفُلٍ ... أَوْ سُنْبُلٌ كُحِلَتْ بِهِ فَانْهَلَّتِ.
(It is as if in the two eyes were clove seeds, or spikenard with which it [the eye] was anointed, so it overflowed [with tears].)
(وَلِنَجْعَلَكَ): conjoined to an omitted verb, its implied form being: "We showed you that so that you might know the measure of Our power, and so that We might make you…". It has been said that the wāw is redundant; and it has been said that the implied form is: "and so that We might make you, We did that".
(كَيْفَ نُنْشِزُهَا): in the position of a ḥāl of al-ʿiẓām (the bones). The governing word in كَيْفَ is نُنْشِزُهَا; it is not permissible for انْظُرْ to govern it, because what precedes an interrogative does not govern it. Rather, كَيْفَ and نَنْشُرُهَا together are a ḥāl of al-ʿiẓām, and the governing word in it is انْظُرْ, its implied form being: "look at the bones being brought to life".
«وَنَنْشُرُهَا» is read with fatḥa on the nūn and ḍamma on the shīn, and its past is nashara; there are two views on it. The first: that it is the reflexive counterpart (muṭāwiʿ) of "anshara Allāhu al-mayyita fa-nushira" (Allah revived the dead, and he was revived), and nashara on this basis is in the sense of anshara, so the intransitive and the transitive have one form.
The second: that it is from al-nashr, which is the opposite of folding, i.e. He spreads them out by giving life.
It is also read with ḍamma on the nūn and kasra on the shīn, i.e. "We give them life", and it is like His saying (إِذَا شَاءَ أَنْشَرَهُ). It is also read with zāy, i.e. "We raise them", and it is from al-nashz, which is raised ground; on this basis there are two readings of it: ḍamma on the nūn and kasra on the shīn, from anshaztuhu,
and fatḥa on the nūn and ḍamma on the shīn, whose past is nashaztuhu; and they are two dialectal forms.
And (لَحْمًا) is a second object. (قَالَ أَعْلَمُ): it is read with fatḥa on the hamza and the lām, on the basis that he is informing about himself.
It is also read with the connecting hamza (waṣl), as an imperative, and the fāʿil of قَالَ is Allah. It has also been said: its fāʿil is ʿUzayr, and he commanded himself as one commands someone addressed, as you say to yourself, "Know, O ʿAbd Allāh"; this is called tajrīd (self-abstraction).
It has also been read with a disjunctive hamza (qaṭʿ) with fatḥa and kasra on the lām (aʿlim), and the meaning is "inform the people".

ukberi-tibyan:228-228.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَالْمُطَلَّقَاتُ يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بِأَنْفُسِهِنَّ ثَلَاثَةَ قُرُوءٍ وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَهُنَّ أَنْ يَكْتُمْنَ مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ فِي أَرْحَامِهِنَّ إِنْ كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَبُعُولَتُهُنَّ أَحَقُّ بِرَدِّهِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ إِنْ أَرَادُوا إِصْلَاحًا وَلَهُنَّ مِثْلُ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَلِلرِّجَالِ عَلَيْهِنَّ دَرَجَةٌ وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ (٢٢٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالْمُطَلَّقَاتُ يَتَرَبَّصْنَ): it has been said: its wording is a statement and its meaning a command, i.e. "let them wait".
It has also been said: it is in its proper sense, and the meaning is "the ruling on divorced women is that they wait three periods". (ثلاثة) here is accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), as is every number annexed to a time or a place. And (قُرُوءٍ) is a plural of abundance, while the context is one of paucity, so the proper form would have been ثَلَاثَةَ أَقْرَاءٍ. There is disagreement over how to interpret this: it has been said that He put the plural of abundance in place of the plural of paucity.
It has also been said: since He made (المطلقات) plural, He brought the wording of the plural of abundance, because each divorced woman waits three.
It has also been said: the interpretation is "three periods out of (many) periods". The singular of (القروء) is قُرْء, and it has been read with fatḥa and ḍamma (قَرْء / قُرْء).
(مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ): (ما) may mean "that which", and it may be a described indefinite noun; the referring pronoun is omitted, i.e. "Allah created it". (فِي أَرْحَامِهِنَّ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to (خلق). It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted pronoun, and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because at the time of its creation it is not anything until its creation is complete. (وَبُعُولَتُهُنَّ): the majority read it with ḍamma on the tāʾ; some irregular readers gave it sukūn (وَبُعُولَتْهُنَّ). Its rationale is that he dropped the case ending, because he likened it to a single connected word such as عَضُد and عَجُز.
(فِي ذَلِكَ): it has been said that (ذلك) refers to the waiting period (ʿidda); on this view it is attached to (أحق), i.e. "he is entitled to take her back as long as she is in the waiting period". The meaning is not that he has more right to return her into the waiting period; he returns her only into marriage, or to marriage.
It has also been said: (ذلك) refers to marriage, so «فِي» is attached to (الرد).
(بِالْمَعْرُوفِ): the bāʾ may be attached to the sense of being established in His saying «وَلَهُنَّ», i.e. "that is established by right". It may also be in the position of the nominative as an adjective of (مثل), because (مثل) has not become definite by annexation.
(وَلِلرِّجَالِ عَلَيْهِنَّ دَرَجَةٌ): (درجة) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (للرجال) the khabar (predicate). (عليهن) may be attached to the sense of being established in the lām. It may also be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of (الدرجة), the implied form being "a degree that is over them"; when the description of the indefinite noun was put before it, it became a ḥāl.
It is weak for (عليهن) to be the khabar and (لهن) [Translator's note: so in the text; evidently (للرجال) is meant] a ḥāl of (درجة), because the governing element would then be abstract (maʿnawī), and a ḥāl does not precede such a governor.

ukberi-tibyan:229-229.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الطَّلَاقُ مَرَّتَانِ فَإِمْسَاكٌ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ تَسْرِيحٌ بِإِحْسَانٍ وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَأْخُذُوا مِمَّا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ شَيْئًا إِلَّا أَنْ يَخَافَا أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ اللَّهِ فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ اللَّهِ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا فِيمَا افْتَدَتْ بِهِ تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ فَلَا تَعْتَدُوهَا وَمَنْ يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ اللَّهِ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ (٢٢٥)). [Translator's note: the verse number is printed as ٢٢٥; it is verse 229.]
His saying, Exalted is He: (الطَّلَاقُ مَرَّتَانِ): its implied form is "the number of divorces with which taking back is permitted is two". (فَإِمْسَاكٌ): i.e. "then upon you is retaining".
And (بِمَعْرُوفٍ): it may be an adjective of (إمساك), and it may be in the position of the accusative governed by (إمساك).
(أَنْ تَأْخُذُوا): its object is «شَيْئًا», and «مِمَّا» is a description of it placed before it, so it became a ḥāl (circumstantial). (من) is partitive, (ما) means "that which", and (آتيتم) takes two objects, one of which has been omitted, namely the pronoun referring to (ما), its implied form being «آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ إِيَّاهُ».
(إِلَّا أَنْ يَخَافَا): (أن) and the verb are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, the implied form being "except fearing", and there is the omission of a muḍāf in it; its implied form is "and it is not lawful for you to take in any circumstance, or in every circumstance, except in the circumstance of fear". It has been read (يُخَافَا) with ḍamma on the yāʾ, i.e. "that this be known of them, or feared".
(أَلَّا يُقِيمَا): in the position of the accusative governed by (يخافا), its implied form being "unless they both fear abandoning the limits of Allah".
(عَلَيْهِمَا): the khabar (predicate) of (لا). And (فِيمَا): attached (mutaʿalliq) to the sense of being established. (عليهما) may not be in the position of the accusative governed by (جناح), with (فيما افتدت) as the khabar, because when the noun of (لا) governs, it takes tanwīn.
(تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar. And (تَعْتَدُوهَا) means "transgress them" (تتعدّوها).

ukberi-tibyan:230-230.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَإِنْ طَلَّقَهَا فَلَا تَحِلُّ لَهُ مِنْ بَعْدُ حَتَّى تَنْكِحَ زَوْجًا غَيْرَهُ فَإِنْ طَلَّقَهَا فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا أَنْ يَتَرَاجَعَا إِنْ ظَنَّا أَنْ يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ اللَّهِ وَتِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ يُبَيِّنُهَا لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ (٢٣٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا أَنْ يَتَرَاجَعَا): i.e. "in that they return to each other".
(يُبَيِّنُهَا): read with yāʾ and with nūn (نُبَيِّنُهَا); the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (الحدود), and what governs it is the sense of pointing (in the demonstrative).

ukberi-tibyan:231-231.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ فَبَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ سَرِّحُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ وَلَا تُمْسِكُوهُنَّ ضِرَارًا لِتَعْتَدُوا وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ فَقَدْ ظَلَمَ نَفْسَهُ وَلَا تَتَّخِذُوا آيَاتِ اللَّهِ هُزُوًا وَاذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَمَا أَنْزَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ وَالْحِكْمَةِ يَعِظُكُمْ بِهِ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ (٢٣١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ضِرَارًا): a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose).
It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "causing harm", as in your saying "Zayd came running (رَكْضًا)".
And (لِتَعْتَدُوا): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (الضرار). The lām may also be the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba).
(نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ): «عَلَيْكُمْ» may be in the position of the accusative governed by (نعمة), because it is a maṣdar, i.e. "that He bestowed favour upon you". It may also be a ḥāl of it, and so be attached to something omitted.
(وَمَا أَنْزَلَ): «مَا» may be in the position of the accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (النعمة); on this view «يُعَظِّمُ» [Translator's note: so printed; evidently (يَعِظُكُمْ) is meant] is a ḥāl, if you wish of (ما), the pronoun referring to it being the hāʾ in (به), or if you wish of the name of Allah.
(ما) may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with (يعظكم) as its khabar (predicate). And (مِنَ الْكِتَابِ): a ḥāl of the omitted hāʾ, the implied form being "and what He sent down (أنزله) to you".

ukberi-tibyan:232-232.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ فَبَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَلَا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ أَنْ يَنْكِحْنَ أَزْوَاجَهُنَّ إِذَا تَرَاضَوْا بَيْنَهُمْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ ذَلِكَ يُوعَظُ بِهِ مَنْ كَانَ مِنْكُمْ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ ذَلِكُمْ أَزْكَى لَكُمْ وَأَطْهَرُ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ وَأَنْتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ (٢٣٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ يَنْكِحْنَ): its implied form is "from (من) marrying" or "away from (عن) marrying"; when the preposition was omitted it came to be in the position of the accusative according to Sībawayh, while according to al-Khalīl it is in the position of the genitive.
(إِذَا تَرَاضَوْا): an adverbial (ẓarf) for (أن ينكحن); if you wish, you may make it an adverbial for (تعضلوهن).
(بِالْمَعْرُوفِ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent; it may be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a mutual agreement that is according to what is right"; and it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb itself.
(ذَلِكَ): the outward wording would require it to be (ذلكم), because the address throughout the verse is to a plural. As for the singular, it may be addressed to the Prophet ﷺ alone, or to every person, or the singular may have been made to suffice for the plural. (أَزْكَى لَكُمْ): the alif in (أزكى) is substituted for a wāw, because it is from زَكَا يَزْكُو.
And (لَكُمْ): an adjective of it. (وَأَطْهَرُ): i.e. "for you".

ukberi-tibyan:260-260.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيْفَ تُحْيِي الْمَوْتَى قَالَ أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِنْ قَالَ بَلَى وَلَكِنْ لِيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي قَالَ فَخُذْ أَرْبَعَةً مِنَ الطَّيْرِ فَصُرْهُنَّ إِلَيْكَ ثُمَّ اجْعَلْ عَلَى كُلِّ جَبَلٍ مِنْهُنَّ جُزْءًا ثُمَّ ادْعُهُنَّ يَأْتِينَكَ سَعْيًا وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ (٢٦٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِذْ قَالَ): the governing word in «إِذْ» is omitted, its implied form being "remember"; so it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), not an adverb (ẓarf).
And (أَرِنِي) is read with sukūn on the rāʾ; it has been discussed in His saying (وَأَرِنَا مَنَاسِكَنَا).
(كَيْفَ تُحْيِ): the clause is in the position of the accusative, governed by أَرِنِي, i.e. "show me the manner of giving life to the dead"; and كَيْفَ is in the position of the accusative, governed by تُحْيِي.
لِيَطْمَئِنَّ: the lām is attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted, its implied form being: "I asked You so that [my heart] may be at rest".
The hamza in يَطْمَئِنَّ is radical, and its pattern is yafʿalillu; for that reason (فَإِذَا اطْمَأْنَنْتُمْ) came like iqshaʿrartum. (مِنَ الطَّيْرِ): an adjective of أَرْبَعَة, and, if you wish, you may attach it to خُذْ.
The origin of al-ṭayr is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of ṭāra yaṭīru ṭayran, like bāʿa yabīʿu bayʿan; then the genus was named by the maṣdar. It may also be that its origin is ṭayyir, like sayyid, then it was lightened as sayyid is lightened (to sayd).
It may also be a plural, like tājir and tajr; al-ṭayr applies to the genus, and the singular is ṭāʾir.
(فَصُرْهُنَّ): it is read with ḍamma on the ṣād and a single rāʾ (ṣurhunna), and with kasra on the ṣād and a single rāʾ (ṣirhunna). The two have two meanings. One of them: "incline them"; one says ṣārahu yaṣūruhu and yaṣīruhu when he inclines it. On this basis إِلَى is attached to the verb, and there is an omission in the speech, its implied form being: "incline them toward you, then cut them up".
The second meaning: that ṣārahu yaṣūruhu and yaṣīruhu is in the sense of "he cuts it up"; on this basis there is an omission in the speech to which «إِلَى» is attached, i.e. "so cut them up after you have inclined them toward you".
The best in my view is that إِلَيْكُمْ be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the implied object, its implied form being: "so cut them up, brought near to you", or "inclined", and the like. «[Translator's note: the text prints «إِلَيْكُمْ»; the verse has «إِلَيْكَ». It also prints «أَنْ يُصَوِّرَهُ وَيُصَيِّرَهُ» in the previous paragraph, translated here in the sense of the same verb ṣāra.]»
It is also read with ḍamma on the ṣād and shadda on the rāʾ (ṣurrahunna); some of them give it ḍamma, some fatḥa and some kasra, like muddahunna: the ḍamma is for vowel harmony (itbāʿ), the fatḥa for lightness, and the kasra is according to the original rule for the meeting of two quiescent letters. The meaning in all of them is from ṣarrahu yaṣurruhu, when he gathers it.
(مِنْهُنَّ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of «جُزْءًا»; its origin is an adjective of the indefinite noun which was placed before it and so became a ḥāl. It may also be an object of اجْعَلْ.
In al-juzʾ there are two dialectal forms: ḍamma on the zāy and sukūn on it, and it has been read with both. There is a third dialectal form, with kasra on the jīm, and I know of no one who read with it.
It has also been read with shadda on the zāy without hamza (juzzan). The explanation of it is that he intended pause on it, so he dropped the hamza after casting its vowel onto the zāy, then doubled the zāy, as you say in pause "hādhā faraḥḥ"; then he treated continuation like pause.
And (يَأْتِينَكَ) is the answer to the imperative. And (سَعْيًا) is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. "hastening".
It may also be an emphatic maṣdar, because hastening and coming are close in meaning; so it is as if He said: "they will come to you with a coming".

ukberi-tibyan:261-261.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ أَنْبَتَتْ سَبْعَ سَنَابِلَ فِي كُلِّ سُنْبُلَةٍ مِائَةُ حَبَّةٍ وَاللَّهُ يُضَاعِفُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ (٢٦١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ): in the speech there is omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being: "the likeness of the spending of those who spend", or "the likeness of the expenditure of those who spend". And مَثَلُ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ) is its khabar (predicate). The omitted element is implied only because those who spend are not likened to the grain; rather their spending or their expenditure is.
(أَنْبَتَتْ سَبْعَ سَنَابِلَ): the clause is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of حَبَّة.
(فِي كُلِّ سُنْبُلَةٍ مِائَةُ حَبَّةٍ): a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the genitive as an adjective of سَنَابِل.
It is also possible for مِائَةُ حَبَّةٍ to be in the nominative by the preposition (as its agent), because it has gained support (iʿtimād) by occurring as an adjective.
The clause may also be an adjective of سَبْع, as when you say "I saw seven free men (aḥrārin)" and "aḥrāran".
It is read anomalously (shādhdh) with مِائَةً in the accusative, as a badal (substitute) of سَبْع, or by an omitted verb, its implied form being "it brought forth". The nūn in sunbula is augmented, its root being from asbala; it has also been said that it is radical. The origin of miʾa is miʾya; one says "amʾat al-darāhimu" when the dirhams reach a hundred; then the final radical was dropped for lightness, as the final radical of yad was dropped.

ukberi-tibyan:262-262.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ لَا يُتْبِعُونَ مَا أَنْفَقُوا مَنًّا وَلَا أَذًى لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (٢٦٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is «لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ».
The final radical of al-adhā is yāʾ; one says adhiya yaʾdhā adhan, like naṣiba yanṣabu naṣaban. «[Translator's note: the text prints the imperfect as «يَأْذِي».]»

ukberi-tibyan:263-263.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَوْلٌ مَعْرُوفٌ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ صَدَقَةٍ يَتْبَعُهَا أَذًى وَاللَّهُ غَنِيٌّ حَلِيمٌ (٢٦٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَوْلٌ مَعْرُوفٌ): a mubtadaʾ (subject); (وَمَغْفِرَةٌ) is conjoined to it, and the implied form is "and a cause of forgiveness", because forgiveness is from Allah, so there is no comparison of superiority between it and the act of His servant.
It is also possible that the forgiveness is the almsgiver's overlooking and bearing with the poor person, so there would be no omission of a muḍāf in it. The khabar (predicate) is «خَيْرٌ مِنْ صَدَقَةٍ», and (يَتْبَعُهَا) is an adjective of صَدَقَة.
It has also been said: قَوْلٌ مَعْرُوفٌ is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "is more excellent than anything else"; and مَغْفِرَةٌ is a mubtadaʾ, and خَيْرٌ is its khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:264-264.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تُبْطِلُوا صَدَقَاتِكُمْ بِالْمَنِّ وَالْأَذَى كَالَّذِي يُنْفِقُ مَالَهُ رِئَاءَ النَّاسِ وَلَا يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَمَثَلُهُ كَمَثَلِ صَفْوَانٍ عَلَيْهِ تُرَابٌ فَأَصَابَهُ وَابِلٌ فَتَرَكَهُ صَلْدًا لَا يَقْدِرُونَ عَلَى شَيْءٍ مِمَّا كَسَبُوا وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْكَافِرِينَ (٢٦٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَالَّذِي يُنْفِقُ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), and in the speech there is omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being: "an annulling like the annulling of the one who spends".
It may also be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of the agents, i.e. "do not annul your charities, resembling the one who spends his wealth", i.e. resembling the one who annuls his spending by showing off.
And (رِئَاءَ النَّاسِ) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); it may also be a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. "he spends, showing off". The first hamza in riʾāʾ is the middle radical of the word, because it is from rāʾā; the last is a substitute for the yāʾ, because it occurs at the end after an augmented alif, as in al-qaḍāʾ and al-dimāʾ.
It is permissible to lighten the first hamza by changing it into yāʾ (riyāʾ), to escape the heaviness of the hamza after a kasra, and it has been read so. The maṣdar here is annexed to its object.
The fāʾ entered in His saying «فَمَثَلُهُ» to link the clause to what precedes it.
Al-ṣafwān is the plural of ṣafwāna; the better view is to say it is a collective genus noun (jins jamʿ), and for that reason the pronoun returns to it in the singular form in His saying «عَلَيْهِ تُرَابٌ».
It has also been said: it is singular. And it has been said: its singular is ṣafan, and the plural of faʿal on fiʿlān is rare; ṣifwān with kasra on the ṣād has been reported, and that is the more usual of the plurals. It is also read with fatḥa on the fāʾ (ṣafawān), and that is anomalous (shādhdh), because faʿalān is anomalous in nouns; it occurs only in maṣdars, like al-ghalayān, and in adjectives, like "yawmun ṣaḥawān" (a clear day). And (عَلَيْهِ تُرَابٌ) is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of صَفْوَان; you may make تُرَاب nominative by the preposition, because it has gained support from what precedes it, or make it nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject).
The fāʾ in (فَأَصَابَهُ) conjoins to the prepositional phrase, because its implied form is: "dust settled upon it, then [a downpour] struck it".
This is one of the things that strengthen the resemblance of the adverbial phrase to the verb.
The alif in «أَصَابَ» is converted from a wāw, because it is from ṣāba yaṣūbu.
(فَتَرَكَهُ صَلْدًا): it is like His saying (وَتَرَكَهُمْ فِي ظُلُمَاتٍ), which has been discussed at the beginning of the sura. (لَا يَقْدِرُونَ): resumptive, having no grammatical position. The plural is used here after the singular in His saying كَالَّذِي and what follows it only because الَّذِي here is generic, so the pronoun may return to it in the singular and the plural. It is not permissible for it to be [a ḥāl] of الَّذِي, because He has separated between them by His saying «فَمِثْلُهُ» and what follows it. «[Translator's note: the bracketed word is supplied for sense; the text also prints «فَمِثْلُهُ» for «فَمَثَلُهُ».]»

ukberi-tibyan:233-233.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَالْوَالِدَاتُ يُرْضِعْنَ أَوْلَادَهُنَّ حَوْلَيْنِ كَامِلَيْنِ لِمَنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يُتِمَّ الرَّضَاعَةَ وَعَلَى الْمَوْلُودِ لَهُ رِزْقُهُنَّ وَكِسْوَتُهُنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ لَا تُكَلَّفُ نَفْسٌ إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا لَا تُضَارَّ وَالِدَةٌ بِوَلَدِهَا وَلَا مَوْلُودٌ لَهُ بِوَلَدِهِ وَعَلَى الْوَارِثِ مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ فَإِنْ أَرَادَا فِصَالًا عَنْ تَرَاضٍ مِنْهُمَا وَتَشَاوُرٍ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا وَإِنْ أَرَدْتُمْ أَنْ تَسْتَرْضِعُوا أَوْلَادَكُمْ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذَا سَلَّمْتُمْ مَا آتَيْتُمْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ (٢٣٣)).
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: (وَالْوَالِدَاتُ): (الوالدات) and (الوالدة) are two adjectives that have come to be used predominantly as nouns; therefore the thing described is not mentioned with them, since they are treated as nouns. And (يُرْضِعْنَ) is like (يتربصن), which has already been mentioned. (حَوْلَيْنِ): an adverbial (ẓarf), and (كَامِلَيْنِ) an adjective of it. The benefit of this adjective is that the two years are to be reckoned without any shortfall; were the adjective not mentioned, it could be taken to mean less than two years by a month or two.
(لِمَنْ أَرَادَ): its implied form is "that is for whoever wishes". (أَنْ يُتِمَّ): the majority read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ, with the agent named and with «الرَّضَاعَةَ» in the accusative.
It is also read with a tāʾ with fatḥa and (الرضاعة) in the nominative (أَنْ تَتِمَّ الرَّضَاعَةُ). The good form is fatḥa on the rāʾ in (الرضاعة); kasra (الرِّضَاعَة) is permissible, and it has been read so.
(وَعَلَى الْمَوْلُودِ): the alif and lām mean "the one who" (الذي), and the pronoun referring to it is the hāʾ in «لَهُ»; and (له) is what stands in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil). (بِالْمَعْرُوفِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (الرزق) and (الكسوة), governed by the sense of being established in (على).
(إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا): a second object; it is not accusative by exception, because «كَلَّفَ» takes two objects. Had (الوسع) been put in the nominative here, it would not be permissible, because it is not a badal (substitute).
(لَا تُضَارَّ): read with ḍamma on the rāʾ and with doubling (لَا تُضَارُّ). There are two views on it: the first, that it is with the agent named, its implied form being لَا تُضَارِرْ with kasra on the first rāʾ; on this view the object is omitted, its implied form being "let no mother harm a father on account of her child".
The second: that the first rāʾ has fatḥa, as a verb whose agent is not named (passive); it was assimilated because the two letters are identical, and it is nominative because its wording is that of a statement while its meaning is prohibition.
It is also read with fatḥa on the rāʾ and doubling, as a prohibition; it was given a vowel because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and fatḥa was preferable for harmony with the alif and the fatḥa before it. On this reading its original may be تُضَارِرْ or تُضَارَرْ, with the agent named or not named, as we mentioned for the nominative reading.
It has been read irregularly with sukūn on the rāʾ (لَا تُضَارْ). Its rationale is that he dropped the second rāʾ to avoid doubling in the repeated letter, namely the rāʾ; and the combination of two quiescent letters was permitted either because he treated continuation like pause, or because the length of the alif functions like a vowel.
(عَنْ تَرَاضٍ): in the position of the accusative, an adjective of (فصال). It may also be attached (mutaʿalliq) to (أرادا).
(وَتَشَاوُرٍ): i.e. "on their part". (تَسْتَرْضِعُوا): its object is omitted, its implied form being "an outside woman" or "someone other than the mother".
(أَوْلَادَكُمْ): an object from which the preposition has been dropped, its implied form being "for your children" (لأولادكم), so the verb was made transitive to it, like his saying "I commanded you the good" (أمرتك الخير). (فَلَا جُنَاحَ): the fāʾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition. And (إِذَا سَلَّمْتُمْ) is also a condition, its answer being what is indicated by the first condition and its answer; and that meaning is what governs (إذا).
(مَا آتَيْتُمْ): read with madd (آتَيْتُمْ), the two objects being omitted, its implied form being "what you gave them". It is also read without madd (أَتَيْتُمْ), its implied form being "what you brought", and it was omitted [Translator's note: i.e. the pronoun «بِهِ»].
Abū ʿAlī said: its implied form is "what you have come to pay in cash or in advance", as you say أَتَيْتُ الْأَمْرَ, i.e. "I did it".

ukberi-tibyan:234-234.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَالَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنْكُمْ وَيَذَرُونَ أَزْوَاجًا يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بِأَنْفُسِهِنَّ أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ وَعَشْرًا فَإِذَا بَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا فَعَلْنَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ (٢٣٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنْكُمْ): there are several views on this verse. The first: that (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "and among what is recited to you is the ruling on those of you who die"; similar to it are (وَالسَّارِقُ وَالسَّارِقَةُ) and (الزَّانِيَةُ وَالزَّانِي); and His saying (يَتَرَبَّصْنَ) is an explanation of the recited ruling. This is the view of Sībawayh.
The second: that the mubtadaʾ is omitted and (الذين) has taken its place, its implied form being "and the wives of those of you who die", the khabar being (يَتَرَبَّصْنَ); the omitted word is indicated by His saying (وَيَذَرُونَ أَزْوَاجًا).
The third: that (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ and (يَتَرَبَّصْنَ) the khabar, the referring pronoun being omitted, its implied form being "they wait after them" or "after their death". The fourth: that (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ and the implied form of the khabar is "their wives wait": (أزواجهم) is a mubtadaʾ and (يتربصن) the khabar, and the mubtadaʾ was omitted because the speech indicates it.
The fifth: that He left off predicating anything of (الَّذِينَ) and made the predication about the wives whose mention is connected with (الذين), because the discourse is about them, regarding observing the waiting period in months; so the predication came about what is intended. This is the view of al-Farrāʾ. The majority read (يُتَوَفَّوْنَ) with ḍamma on the yāʾ, as a verb whose agent is not named (passive).
It is also read with fatḥa on the yāʾ (يَتَوَفَّوْنَ), with the agent named; the meaning is "they complete their life-spans".
And (مِنْكُمْ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the latent agent.
(وَعَشْرًا): i.e. ten nights, because dating is by the night when it is the beginning of the month, and the day follows it. (بِالْمَعْرُوفِ): a ḥāl of the feminine pronoun in the verb, or an object, or an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); its like has been discussed before.

ukberi-tibyan:235-235.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا عَرَّضْتُمْ بِهِ مِنْ خِطْبَةِ النِّسَاءِ أَوْ أَكْنَنْتُمْ فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ سَتَذْكُرُونَهُنَّ وَلَكِنْ لَا تُوَاعِدُوهُنَّ سِرًّا إِلَّا أَنْ تَقُولُوا قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفًا وَلَا تَعْزِمُوا عُقْدَةَ النِّكَاحِ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ الْكِتَابُ أَجَلَهُ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ فَاحْذَرُوهُ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ (٢٣٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ خِطْبَةِ النِّسَاءِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the genitive hāʾ (in بِهِ), so that what governs it is (عرضتم).
It may also be a ḥāl of «مَا», so that what governs it is the sense of being established.
(الخِطبة) with kasra is addressing a woman about marriage; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its object, the implied form being "of your proposing to women".
And (أَوْ) is for permission; the object is omitted, its implied form being "or you concealed it". One says أَكْنَنْتُ الشَّيْءَ فِي نَفْسِي when you have kept it hidden, and كَنَنْتُهُ when you have covered it with a garment or the like.
(وَلَكِنْ): this qualification (istidrāk) is from His saying (فِيمَا عَرَّضْتُمْ بِهِ).
And (سِرًّا): an object, because it means marriage, i.e. "do not promise them marriage".
It has also been said: it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl, its implied form being "concealing it", with the object omitted, its implied form being "do not promise them marriage secretly". It may also be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a secret promising".
It has also been said: the implied form is "in secret", so it is an adverbial (ẓarf). (إِلَّا أَنْ تَقُولُوا): in the position of the accusative by exception from the object; it is a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ), and it has also been said: connected (muttaṣil). (وَلَا تَعْزِمُوا عُقْدَةَ): i.e. "on (على) the knot of marriage".
It has also been said: (تَعْزِمُوا) means "intend", and this is transitive by itself, so it governs as it does. It has also been said: (تعزموا) means "contract", so that (عقدة النكاح) is a maṣdar, (العقدة) meaning (العقد) "contracting", and so the maṣdar is annexed to its object.

ukberi-tibyan:265-265.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَثَلُ الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمُ ابْتِغَاءَ مَرْضَاةِ اللَّهِ وَتَثْبِيتًا مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ كَمَثَلِ جَنَّةٍ بِرَبْوَةٍ أَصَابَهَا وَابِلٌ فَآتَتْ أُكُلَهَا ضِعْفَيْنِ فَإِنْ لَمْ يُصِبْهَا وَابِلٌ فَطَلٌّ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ (٢٦٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ابْتِغَاءَ): a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and (وَتَثْبِيتًا) is conjoined to it. Both may also be ḥāls (circumstantials), i.e. "seeking" and "making firm".
(مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ): مِنْ may be in the sense of the lām, i.e. "a strengthening for themselves", as you say "I did that as a breaking of my desire". It may also be in its original sense, i.e. "a strengthening issuing from themselves". Al-tathbīt is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of a transitive verb; so on the first view مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ is the object of the maṣdar, and on the second view the object is omitted, its implied form being: "and they make their deeds firm by sincerity of intention".
It is also possible that tathbītan is in the sense of tathabbut, so it is intransitive; maṣdars may differ and one may occur in the place of another. Its like is His saying, Exalted is He: (وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًا), i.e. tabattulan.
In His saying (وَمَثَلُ الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ) there is an omission, its implied form being: "and the likeness of the expenditure of those who spend", because the spender is not likened to the garden; rather, the expenditure that grows is likened to the garden that bears fruit.
(وَالرَّبْوَةُ): with ḍamma, fatḥa and kasra on the rāʾ are three dialectal forms; there is another dialectal form, rabāwa; and it has been read with all of that.
(أَصَابَهَا): an adjective of al-janna. It may also be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of al-janna, because it has been described.
It may also be a ḥāl of the pronoun in the preposition, with «قَدْ» implied with the verb.
And the clause may be an adjective of رَبْوَة, because the garden is part of the hill.
Al-wābil is from wabala, and one says awbala, so it is mūbil; it is an adjective that has become predominant (ṣifa ghāliba), with which mention of the described noun is not needed. And (آتَتْ) is transitive to two objects, one of which has been omitted, i.e. "it gave its owner".
It may also be transitive to one object, because the meaning of آتَتْ is "brought forth", and it is from al-ītāʾ, which is yield. Al-ukl with sukūn on the kāf and with ḍamma are two dialectal forms; it has been read as a plural, and its singular is ukla, which is what is eaten. He annexed the produce to it (the garden) because it is its place or its cause. And (ضِعْفَيْنِ) is a ḥāl, i.e. "doubled".
(فَطَلٌّ): the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "then what strikes it is a drizzle", or "then the striker of it", or "then its striker". It may also be a fāʿil (agent), its implied form being: "then a drizzle strikes it"; the verb is omitted because the protasis verb indicates it. The jussive in يُصِبْهَا is by لَمْ, not by إِنْ, because لَمْ is a governor specific to the future, whereas إِنْ may be followed by the past and the verb may be omitted with it, so its operation may be cancelled.

ukberi-tibyan:266-266.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَيَوَدُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَنْ تَكُونَ لَهُ جَنَّةٌ مِنْ نَخِيلٍ وَأَعْنَابٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ لَهُ فِيهَا مِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ وَأَصَابَهُ الْكِبَرُ وَلَهُ ذُرِّيَّةٌ ضُعَفَاءُ فَأَصَابَهَا إِعْصَارٌ فِيهِ نَارٌ فَاحْتَرَقَتْ كَذَلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمُ الْآيَاتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ (٢٦٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ نَخِيلٍ): an adjective of جَنَّة. Nakhīl is a plural, and that is a rare form; it has also been said that it is a genus noun.
And (تَجْرِي) is another adjective. (لَهُ فِيهَا مِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ): in the speech there is an omission, its implied form being: "he has in it provision of every kind", or "fruits of all kinds of fruits".
It is not permissible for (مِنْ) to be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with what precedes it as the khabar (predicate), because the mubtadaʾ cannot be a preposition with its genitive noun unless the preposition is redundant; nor a fāʿil (agent), because a preposition cannot be a fāʿil; but it may be an adjective of something omitted.
Nor is it permissible for (مِنْ) to be redundant (zāʾida), either according to Sībawayh or according to al-Akhfash, because the meaning would become "he has in it all the fruits", and the matter is not so; unless what is meant here is abundance rather than comprehensiveness, in which case it is permissible according to al-Akhfash, because he allows the addition of (مِنْ) in an affirmative statement. The annexation of (كُلّ) to what follows it is in the sense of the lām, because the muḍāf ilayhi is other than the muḍāf.
(وَأَصَابَهُ): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of أَحَد, with «قَدْ» intended, its implied form being: "and old age had struck him".
It has also been said: the past was put in the place of the imperfect. And it has been said: in the conjoining it was construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is "would one of you like that he had a garden, and [old age] struck him"; this is weak, since there is no need to alter the wording when its meaning is sound. (وَلَهُ ذُرِّيَّةٌ): a clause in the position of a ḥāl of the hāʾ in أَصَابَهُ.
There is disagreement about the origin of al-dhurriyya, on four views.
