The first: that its origin is dhurrūra, from dharra yadhurru, when he scatters; the second rāʾ was replaced by yāʾ because of the concurrence of rāʾs, then the wāw was replaced by yāʾ, then they were assimilated, then the rāʾ was given kasra for vowel harmony; some also give kasra to the dhāl for vowel harmony, and it has been read so. «[Translator's note: the text prints «ذُرْوَةٌ» (dhurwa); the process described (replacing the second rāʾ) presupposes dhurrūra.]» The second: that it is also from dharra, except that the two yāʾs were added, so its pattern is fuʿliyya.
The third: that it is from dharaʾa, with hamza; so its origin on this view is dharūʾa, on the pattern faʿūla; then the hamza was replaced by yāʾ, and the wāw was replaced by yāʾ, to escape the heaviness of the hamza, the wāw and the ḍamma.
The fourth: that it is from dharā yadhrū, because of His saying (تَذْرُوهُ الرِّيَاحُ); so its origin is dharūwa; then the wāw was replaced by yāʾ, and then what preceded was done. It may also be fuʿliyya on both of the last two views.
(فَأَصَابَهَا): conjoined to the adjective of the garden.

ukberi-tibyan:267-267.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْفِقُوا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَا كَسَبْتُمْ وَمِمَّا أَخْرَجْنَا لَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ وَلَا تَيَمَّمُوا الْخَبِيثَ مِنْهُ تُنْفِقُونَ وَلَسْتُمْ بِآخِذِيهِ إِلَّا أَنْ تُغْمِضُوا فِيهِ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ (٢٦٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْفِقُوا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ): the object is omitted, i.e. "something of the good things". It has been discussed fully in what preceded.
(وَلَا تَيَمَّمُوا): the majority read the tāʾ without shadda; its past is tayammama, and the original is tatayammamū, then the second tāʾ was dropped, as was mentioned regarding His saying «تَظَاهَرُونَ».
It is also read with shadda on the tāʾ, preceded by an alif (wa-lā ttayammamū); this is a combination of two quiescent letters, and what makes it acceptable is the prolongation (madd) in the alif. It has also been read with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the first mīm (tuyammimū), on the basis that nothing was dropped, and its pattern is tufaʿʿilū. «[Translator's note: the text gives the pattern as «تَفْعَلُوا».]»
(مِنْهُ): attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تُنْفِقُونَ», and the clause is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) in تَيَمَّمُوا; it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because spending from it occurs after intending it.
It may also be a ḥāl of al-khabīth, because the speech contains a pronoun referring back to it, i.e. "spending from it".
(وَالْخَبِيثُ) is an adjective that has become predominant (ṣifa ghāliba), so the described noun is not mentioned with it.
(وَلَسْتُمْ بِآخِذِيهِ): resumptive, having no grammatical position. (إِلَّا أَنْ تُغْمِضُوا): in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. "except in the state of closing the eyes".
The majority read it with ḍamma on the tāʾ, sukūn on the ghayn and kasra on the mīm; its past is aghmaḍa, and it is transitive, its object having been omitted, i.e. "that you close your eyes" or "your insight". It may also be intransitive, like "aghḍā ʿan kadhā" (he overlooked such-and-such). It is also read the same way but with shadda on the mīm and fatḥa on the ghayn (tughammiḍū), and the implied object is "your eyes".
It is also read tughmaḍū, with ḍamma on the tāʾ, without shadda, and with fatḥa on the mīm, in the passive; the meaning is "unless you are brought to overlook it and be lenient about it".
It may also be from ughmiḍa, when one is found in that state, as you say "uḥmida al-rajulu", i.e. he was found praiseworthy. It is also read with fatḥa on the tāʾ, sukūn on the ghayn and kasra on the mīm (taghmiḍū), from ghamiḍa yaghmiḍu, which is a dialectal form of ghamuḍa; and it is read the same way but with ḍamma on the mīm (taghmuḍū), from ghamuḍa, like ẓarufa, i.e. "your judgement about it is hidden from you".

ukberi-tibyan:268-268.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الشَّيْطَانُ يَعِدُكُمُ الْفَقْرَ وَيَأْمُرُكُمْ بِالْفَحْشَاءِ وَاللَّهُ يَعِدُكُمْ مَغْفِرَةً مِنْهُ وَفَضْلًا وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ (٢٦٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَعِدُكُمُ): its original is yawʿidukum; the wāw was dropped because it occurred between a yāʾ with fatḥa and a kasra. It is transitive to two objects, and it may come with the bāʾ: one says "waʿadtuhu bi-kadhā" (I promised him such-and-such).
(مَغْفِرَةً): it may be an adjective, or an object attached to يَعِدُ, i.e. "He promises you from His own self"; and وَفَضْلًا, its implied form being "from Him", the first [مِنْهُ] sufficing so that it need not be repeated. «[Translator's note: the description "an adjective … or attached to يَعِدُ … from His own self" evidently refers to «مِنْهُ» rather than to «مَغْفِرَةً»: it may be an adjective of مَغْفِرَة, or attached to يَعِدُ.]»

ukberi-tibyan:269-269.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يُؤْتِي الْحِكْمَةَ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَمَنْ يُؤْتَ الْحِكْمَةَ فَقَدْ أُوتِيَ خَيْرًا كَثِيرًا وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ إِلَّا أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ (٢٦٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَنْ يُؤْتَ): it is read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the tāʾ; «مَنْ» on this reading is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what follows it is the khabar (predicate). It is also read with kasra on the tāʾ (yuʾti); مَنْ on this reading is in the position of the accusative, governed by يُؤْتِ, and يُؤْتِ is jussive by it; so each governs what governs it. The fāʿil (agent) is the pronoun of the name of Allah.
The original of (يَذَّكَّرُ) is yatadhakkaru; the tāʾ was replaced by dhāl so as to be close to it, and then assimilated.

ukberi-tibyan:270-270.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِنْ نَفَقَةٍ أَوْ نَذَرْتُمْ مِنْ نَذْرٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُهُ وَمَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ أَنْصَارٍ (٢٧٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا أَنْفَقْتُمْ): مَا is conditional, and its position is accusative, governed by the verb that follows it; we have mentioned its like in His saying (وَمَا تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ يَعْلَمْهُ اللَّهُ).

ukberi-tibyan:271-271.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنْ تُبْدُوا الصَّدَقَاتِ فَنِعِمَّا هِيَ وَإِنْ تُخْفُوهَا وَتُؤْتُوهَا الْفُقَرَاءَ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ وَيُكَفِّرُ عَنْكُمْ مِنْ سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ (٢٧١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَنِعِمَّا): niʿma is an inflexible (jāmid) verb that has no imperfect. Its original is naʿima, like ʿalima, and it has occurred in that form in poetry; but they gave the ʿayn sukūn and transferred its vowel to the nūn, to be an indication of the original. Some leave the nūn with fatḥa according to the original (naʿma).
And some give kasra to both the nūn and the ʿayn for vowel harmony (niʿima); it has been read with each.
There is another reading here: sukūn on the ʿayn and the mīm, with assimilation (niʿmmā); this is far-fetched because it combines two quiescent letters. It has been said: the transmitter did not record the reading accurately, because the reciter slurred (ikhtalasa) the kasra of the ʿayn and he took it for sukūn. The fāʿil (agent) of niʿma is latent, and مَا is in the sense of "a thing"; it is the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ), i.e. "excellent is the thing, as a thing". «[Translator's note: as printed; on the usual analysis مَا is the tamyīz (specification) and هِيَ is the one specified for praise, as the next sentence goes on to say.]» (هِيَ): the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), as though someone said, "What is the thing praised?" and it is said, "It", i.e. the one praised is the charity. There is another view on it: that هِيَ is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and niʿma with its fāʿil is the khabar, i.e. "charity — excellent is the thing"; a pronoun referring back to the mubtadaʾ is dispensed with because the genus includes the mubtadaʾ.
(فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ): the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and its position is jussive. هُوَ is the pronoun of a maṣdar (verbal noun) that has not been mentioned, though its verb has been mentioned; the implied form is "then the concealing is better for you", or "then giving it to the poor in secret is better". (وَيُكَفِّرُ عَنْكُمْ): it is read with nūn, attributing the act to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
It is also read with yāʾ on this same construal, and also on another construal, namely that the fāʿil is the pronoun of the concealing.
It is also read wa-tukaffar, with tāʾ, on the basis that the verb is attributed to the pronoun of the charity.
It is read with the rāʾ in the jussive, conjoined to the position of فَهُوَ, and in the nominative by implying a mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and We…" or "and it…". And (مِنْ) here is redundant (zāʾida) according to al-Akhfash, so سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ would be the object; according to Sībawayh the object is omitted, i.e. "something of your misdeeds". Al-sayyiʾa is fayʿila, and its middle radical is wāw, because it is from sāʾa yasūʾu; its original is saywiʾa, then what we mentioned regarding صَيِّب was done to it.

ukberi-tibyan:273-273.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لِلْفُقَرَاءِ الَّذِينَ أُحْصِرُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ ضَرْبًا فِي الْأَرْضِ يَحْسَبُهُمُ الْجَاهِلُ أَغْنِيَاءَ مِنَ التَّعَفُّفِ تَعْرِفُهُمْ بِسِيمَاهُمْ لَا يَسْأَلُونَ النَّاسَ إِلْحَافًا وَمَا تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِهِ عَلِيمٌ (٢٣٧)). «[Translator's note: the verse number is printed as ٢٣٧; this is verse ٢٧٣.]»
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِلْفُقَرَاءِ): in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "the charities mentioned are for the poor". It has also been said that the implied form is: "give to the poor". (فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): «فِي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أُحْصِرُوا, on the basis that it is an adverb (ẓarf) of it.
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "they were restricted while striving".
(لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ): in the position of a ḥāl, the governing word in it being أُحْصِرُوا, i.e. "they were restricted, being unable".
It may also be resumptive. (يَحْسَبُهُمُ) is also a ḥāl, and it may be resumptive, having no grammatical position.
There are two dialectal forms in it: kasra on the sīn and fatḥa on it, and it has been read with both.
And (الْجَاهِلُ) is generic; for that reason it is not made plural, and a single person is not meant by it.
(مِنَ التَّعَفُّفِ): «مِنْ» may be attached to يَحْسَبُ, i.e. "he thinks them [rich] because of the abstaining". It is not permissible for it to be attached to the sense of أَغْنِيَاء, because the meaning would turn into the opposite of what is intended. That is, the meaning of the verse is that their condition is hidden from one who does not know them, so he thinks them rich; whereas if مِنْ were attached to أَغْنِيَاء, the meaning would become that the ignorant one thinks they are rich, but rich through abstaining, and one who is rich through abstaining is poor in wealth.
(تَعْرِفُهُمْ): it may be a ḥāl, or it may be resumptive; and (لَا يَسْأَلُونَ) is like it.
And (إِلْحَافًا) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) of an omitted verb indicated by يَسْأَلُونَ, so it is as if He said: "they do not importune". It may also be a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl, its implied form being: "and they do not ask, importuning".

ukberi-tibyan:274-274.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ سِرًّا وَعَلَانِيَةً فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (٢٧٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ): the relative noun and its ṣila (relative clause) are a mubtadaʾ (subject), and His saying فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ is a clause in the position of the khabar (predicate). The fāʾ entered here because of the resemblance of الَّذِي to the conditional in its vagueness and in its being linked to a verb.
(بِاللَّيْلِ): an adverb (ẓarf), the bāʾ in it being in the sense of "in".
And (سِرًّا وَعَلَانِيَةً): two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:275-275.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ الرِّبَا لَا يَقُومُونَ إِلَّا كَمَا يَقُومُ الَّذِي يَتَخَبَّطُهُ الشَّيْطَانُ مِنَ الْمَسِّ ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوا إِنَّمَا الْبَيْعُ مِثْلُ الرِّبَا وَأَحَلَّ اللَّهُ الْبَيْعَ وَحَرَّمَ الرِّبَا فَمَنْ جَاءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ فَانْتَهَى فَلَهُ مَا سَلَفَ وَأَمْرُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَمَنْ عَادَ فَأُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ (٢٧٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ الرِّبَا): a mubtadaʾ (subject); «لَا يَقُومُونَ» is its khabar (predicate). The kāf is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being: "except with a standing like the standing of the one whom [Satan] confounds". The final radical of al-ribā is wāw, because it is from rabā yarbū; its dual is ribawān, and it is written with alif.
The Kufans permitted writing it, and its dual, with yāʾ; they said this is because of the kasra at its beginning. That is an error in our view.
And (مِنَ الْمَسِّ) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يَتَخَبَّطُهُ, i.e. "on account of madness", so it is in the position of the accusative.
(ذَلِكَ): a mubtadaʾ, and «بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوا» is the khabar, i.e. "is deserved because of their saying".
(جَاءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٌ): the tāʾ (of the feminine) is not retained only because the femininity of al-mawʿiẓa is not real; al-mawʿiẓa and al-waʿẓ have one meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:276-276.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَمْحَقُ اللَّهُ الرِّبَا وَيُرْبِي الصَّدَقَاتِ وَاللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ أَثِيمٍ (٢٧٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَمْحَقُ اللَّهُ الرِّبَا): Abū Zayd al-Anṣārī reported that someone read it with kasra on the rāʾ, ḍamma on the bāʾ, and a quiescent wāw (al-ribuw). It is a far-fetched reading, since there is no noun in the language ending in a wāw preceded by a ḍamma, especially when a kasra precedes the ḍamma. It may be interpreted as pausal form according to the usage of those who say "hādhihi afʿū" (this is a viper), changing the alif into wāw in pause; so either the transmitter did not record the vowel of the bāʾ accurately, or he called its closeness to ḍamma a ḍamma.
